## BLOCKER

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/color-picke` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** A cold load / refresh / shared link on any route whose left pane is not the color-picker (10 of 14 routes) permanently stalls the overture beat DAG at B2: overture:b3 and overture:b4 never fire for the life of the session, and the picker's hero-blob ornament (v-if gated on b4) never mounts again on ANY route thereafter.

**Mechanism.** State derived from a source of truth that is not yet true: index.html:205-213 mounts without awaiting router.isReady(), so the first render uses the picker config; PaneSlot then swaps the child (router resolution + the deliberate one-rAF commit at PaneSlot.vue:95), which cancels Vue's `appear` transition so @after-appear never fires. B3 is the one beat in this boot chain with NO state-checked fallback (contrast useDockArrival.ts:63-72 and useOverture.ts:173), so one missed DOM event is terminal.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured with an isolated Chromium probe against localhost:9000. CONTROL cold-load /#/ → marks [b0,b1,b3,b2,b4], `.hero-blob-anchor` present. DEEPLINK /#/generate → marks [b0,b1,b2] only, blob absent; after hash-nav to /#/ still [b0,b1,b2], `.picker-shell` present but blob STILL absent. Identical for /#/browse. First-pane oracle (pre-navigation MutationObserver) on cold /#/generate records `picker-shell` as the FIRST mounted left pane before the GeneratePane. Code: App.vue:90 and App.vue:109 are the ONLY call sites of overture.noteLeftPlateSettled (grep), both via PaneSlot.vue:118 `@after-appear`; useViewManager.ts:43-46 falls back to "picker" while route.name is undefined; PaneSlot.vue:74 seeds liveComponent at setup; useOverture.ts:153-183 gates b4 on b3Complete.
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/probe-b3.mjs — launches chromium 1440x900, goto http://localhost:9000/#/generate (or /#/browse), wait 5s, read performance marks + `.hero-blob-anchor`; then set location.hash='#/', wait 7s, re-read. Compare against goto('/#/'). Deep links yield 3 marks and no blob; the control yields 5 marks and a blob.

**Proposed cure.** Take the MT-F012 entry cure and make it the idiomatic vue-router SPA boot: in the new main.ts do `app.use(router); await router.isReady(); app.mount('#app')`. With the route true at first render the first-mounted left pane is the final one, its appear completes, B3 and B4 fire. Second, independent arm: arm B3 on the left pane's MOUNT plus a getAnimations() settle check (the sibling beats' idiom) instead of a single Transition appear event.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** No entry module exists; App.vue is the composition root by default and silently carries the whole boot contract (router-plugin dependency, fouc-guard lockstep, body mount, CSS document root, two app-level installs in a component setup).

**Mechanism.** missing composition root — boot logic migrates into the root component because HTML cannot express one

**Evidence.**

```
`find demo -name "main.ts" -o -name "main.js"` → (no output). Entry = demo/color-picker/index.html:205-213 (inline `<script type="module">`). Assumption (a): App.vue:274 `useViewManager()` → demo/shell/useViewManager.ts:36-37 `useRouter()`/`useRoute()` then :41 `router.isReady()`. (b): index.html:159-201 fouc-guard; ground.ts:40-46 "LOCKSTEP CLAUSE 2" records the predicate having drifted (dropped 'auto' arm). (d): App.vue:199-210 four CSS imports; demo/styles/foundation.css:1,2,56,57,76,81,85 is itself the barrel. (e): App.vue:214 `useGlobalDark()`, :219 `provideApiClient()`, rationale at :212-213 = a mount-order contract in a comment. Build-side proof already measured in MT-F012.1: 698-byte application-free entry chunk, content hash `Dezn_h7o` byte-identical to a stock-Vite inline-entry repro.
```

**Reproduction.** docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/probes/vite-entry-repro/ for the build half. Structural half: remove `app.use(router)` from index.html:211 → TypeError at useViewManager.ts:41, a dependency App.vue never declares.

**Proposed cure.** Create demo/color-picker/main.ts holding createApp + `app.use(router)` + `app.provide(API_CLIENT_KEY, createApiClient())` + `initGlobalDark()` + `import "../styles/foundation.css"`, referenced as `<script type="module" src="./main.ts">`. Assumptions (a), (d), (e) become explicit compiler-checked lines; (c) becomes expressible; (b) reduces to the irreducible pre-module guard. App.vue drops both installs and all four CSS imports and becomes pure layout. Also fixes MT-F012 as a side effect — this is the form Vite documents.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure: module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The color-space catalog has four independent homes and no total consumer. PICKER_SPACE_NAMES→DISPLAY_COLOR_SPACE_NAMES = 18 members (this component's catalog); colorSpaceInfo = 13; MarkdownSpace = 11; INTERPOLATION_SPACES = 9. Seven of the 18 offered rows have no markdown doc; five have no info row. Every consumer covers the shortfall with a masking fallback (`: colorSpaceInfo.rgb`), an `as any`, or a silent `v-if`.

**Mechanism.** absent unique semantic ownership — one concept (the space catalog) split across four modules with zero type-level relation, so partial consumers mask the gap instead of failing to compile

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:72 (17 labels) → demo/color-session/color-model.ts:75 (+hex = 18) → ColorSpaceSelector.vue:150. demo/color-session/colorSpaceInfo.ts:18 (13 keys). demo/scenes/about/AboutPane.vue:82 (MarkdownSpace, 11). demo/color-session/color-space-meta.ts:26 (9). Fallbacks: demo/scenes/about/ColorNutritionLabel.vue:212-214 `space in colorSpaceInfo ? … : colorSpaceInfo.rgb`; demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ConsoleRail.vue:174 `(colorSpaceInfo as any)[space]`; demo/scenes/about/AboutPane.vue:51 `v-if="activeMarkdownModule"`. Live probe output: ABOUT AFTER display-p3 { "nutrition": "Definition | A color space based on the additive mixture of red, green, and blue light. | … | White Point: | Varies (typically D65) | Gamut: | Limited (device-specific) | Created: | 1931 | Components | Red | 0 ", "guide": "Detailed Guide", "triggers": ["Display P3","Display P3"] }. Screenshot: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ColorSpaceSelector/probe-display-p3-about.png
```

**Reproduction.** Dev server at http://localhost:9000/#/ (1600x1000). Click the color-space title in the picker card, select "Display P3". Both titles read "Display P3"; the About card beneath reads CIE RGB facts (Created: 1931, Components Red/Green/Blue) and the "Detailed Guide" heading has nothing under it. Script: scratchpad/chL-css-probe.mjs

**Proposed cure.** One `color-session/space-catalog.ts` exporting a single `readonly SpaceEntry[]` typed `satisfies Record<DisplayColorSpace, SpaceEntry>` where SpaceEntry carries id · label · channels · info · doc · interpolatable. Adding a SpaceId then fails to compile until its doc and info exist. All three fallbacks and both `as any`/`as keyof` casts delete; INTERPOLATION_SPACES becomes CATALOG.filter(e => e.interpolatable).

### `DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D) — demo/color-picker/App.vue, the app sh` · D-1 · DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D)

**Defect.** On mobile, nine named and enabled action-bar controls are completely inert, plus every colorPickerRef-dependent affordance. App.vue attaches PaneSlot's `:on-mount` only to the two DESKTOP slots, so the four pane-instance refs the action handlers dereference are permanently null at mobile — `null?.regenerate?.()` yields undefined with no call, no throw and no feedback.

**Mechanism.** breakpoint-forked slot plumbing — instance registration is a per-call-site prop (`:on-mount`), so liveness desynchronises with every v-if branch; `any`-typed refs (D-13) suppress the compiler diagnostic that would have caught it

**Evidence.**

```
App.vue:83-91 (mobile PaneSlot, NO :on-mount) vs App.vue:105 and App.vue:131 (:on-mount on the desktop slots). App.vue:323-328 onDesktopLeftMount is the sole writer of colorPickerRef/generatePaneRef/gradientPaneRef; App.vue:330-332 the sole writer of mixPaneRef. usePaneRouter.ts:196 `handler: () => paneRefs.generate.value?.regenerate?.()` (and :197,198,208,209,210,220,221,222 — 9 actions). Dock.vue:41 `hasAnyActionBar = !!actionBar || !!genericBar` gates rendering on metadata, not liveness, so the layer still draws. Downstream of the same null: App.vue:38 `:action-bar="colorPickerRef?.actionBarContext ?? null"`, App.vue:41-42 commit/cancel-edit, App.vue:352 usePaletteWiring(colorPickerRef, …). Measured: p3.mjs output `{"label":"mobile-390","clicked":"dispatched","specimenChanged":false,"errs":[]}` / `{"label":"desktop-1440","clicked":"dispatched","specimenChanged":true,"errs":[]}`; desktop before oklch(0.667417 0.182968 248.748459) -> after oklch(0.632577 0.21149 37.050613), mobile unchanged at oklch(0.685775 0.168594 55.603336). Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:100 "Commit uses one glass-ui action set"; :83 states "are never color-only. Role, accessible name, state/value and associated error/status are explicit."
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/p3.mjs  — webkit, http://localhost:9000/#/generate, waits 3000ms, dispatches a synthetic MouseEvent('click') on the nav.dock-band button whose aria-label/textContent matches /regenerate/i (the button is in a collapsed DockLayer so a real .click() times out), then diffs the first 10 `main [style*='background-color']` style attributes. Ran at viewport 390x844@3 isMobile and 1440x900. Mobile: no change. Desktop: palette regenerates.

**Proposed cure.** Do not pass instance capture per call site. `usePaneRouter` already owns the route table and the paneRefs record — let it own registration too: expose one `bindPane(slotName)` capture that every PaneSlot call site passes through, so a slot cannot mount without registering and the breakpoint cannot fork liveness. Type PaneSlot's onMount generically over the mounted component's instance type so the gap is a compile error, not a silent no-op. Under D-2's single-scene shell the branch disappears and the question stops existing.

```

Live table demo/shell/viewSchema.ts: right:"about" (:107), right:"palettes" (:116,126,135,154,163,190,199,208,217,226), right:"mix" (:144), right:"blob" (:181), right:null only at :172 (/atmosphere). **Defect.** The desktop two-part scene renders exactly 50.0000% / 50.0000%. The canon permits only `golden` (61.8033989/38.1966011) or `preview-dominant` (66.6666667/33.3333333), and binds Picker specifically to the exact golden inspector. Equal columns are shipped by written intent, so nothing in the frame identifies the protagonist.

**Mechanism.** the shell owns grid-template-columns, so one ratio is imposed on eleven differently-composed members; ratio is a property of the route composition, not of the shell

**Evidence.**

```
Measured at 1440x900 (probe-app-D.mjs, desktop-1440): `paneGridCols = "512px 512px"`, left {x:199,w:512}, right {x:729,w:512}, left share = 50.0000%. Delta from the nearest legal ratio = 11.80 percentage points. Source: demo/styles/shell.css:133-138 `.pane-container--dual { /* Equal columns always (the kept 1fr<->1fr invariant) */ grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(var(--pane-min), 1fr)); }`. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:27 (§3 law 1) and :43 (§3.1 Picker row, "exact golden inspector 38.1966011%"); also :28 (§3 law 2) "Empty secondary content ... never receives half the viewport" — every right:"palettes" route with an empty library receives exactly half. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:48 PR-04 requires Admin companion 50%->0.
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/probe-app-D.mjs  → row label "desktop-1440": getComputedStyle('.pane-container').gridTemplateColumns === '512px 512px'; getBoundingClientRect widths 512/512 inside a 1042px container.

**Proposed cure.** Move the ratio onto InstrumentChassis as named typed values (`golden` | `preview-dominant`) per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:40-52's table, and have the shell stop declaring grid-template-columns at all. The 50/50 grid then cannot outlive the composition that chose it.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · C-15 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** NEW. The destructive confirm button stays mounted, hit-testable and bound to the same closure for ~160-290 ms after it has already fired, so a single human double-click executes the action TWICE. On Prune that is two unscoped whole-collection destructions from one gesture, reported as one receipt.

**Mechanism.** C (new family) — a control outlives its own activation. `confirmOpen.value = false` is synchronous but DOM removal is a nextTick away and the Glass 7 Dialog plays a leave transition first; nothing disables the button or nulls the closure. Same shape as the uncancelled 3s timer (line 308) and the uncancelled in-flight disclosure fetch (C-19): work is started with no way to be finished, cancelled or made unrepeatable.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:283-286 — `onConfirm(){ confirmAction.value?.(); confirmOpen.value = false; }` (no disable, no re-entry guard, closure never cleared). MEASURED WINDOW (probe-C2c-window.json, elementFromPoint polled every ~20ms after the first click): chromium lastLiveAtMs 271 / firstDeadAtMs 294; webkit lastLiveAtMs 159 / firstDeadAtMs 181. REPRODUCTION (probe-C2b-controls.json K2b, both engines byte-identical): prunePosts = ["POST /admin/users/prune-empty","POST /admin/users/prune-empty"]; atSecondClick = {dialogPresent:true, elementUnderCursor:"button.button", elementText:"Prune"}; beat = "Pruned 2 users" (ONE receipt for TWO executions). Same shape on per-user delete (probe-C2-implementation.json N2): deleteRequests = ["DELETE /admin/users/alpha-keeper-0001","DELETE /admin/users/alpha-keeper-0001"]. CONTROL (probe-C2b-controls.json K2a, both engines): single click -> deletes = ["DELETE /admin/users/alpha-keeper-0001"] — exactly one.
```

**Reproduction.** Dev server live at :9000. `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-C2b-controls.mjs` (K2b = double-click prune, K2a = single-click control) and `probe-C2c-window.mjs` (W1 = the live-window trace). Manually: #/admin/users with >=1 empty user, click `Prune empty`, then double-click `Prune` in the dialog within ~150ms; watch the network panel for two POST /admin/users/prune-empty.

**Proposed cure.** Do NOT add `if (busy) return` to onConfirm — that leaves the button clickable and swallows the second event, a different lie. Make the control unable to outlive its activation: (a) onConfirm becomes async and the footer button binds `:disabled` to the pending state so it is VISIBLY inert the instant it fires and stays inert while in flight — which the current `action: () => void` signature cannot express; (b) `confirmAction.value = null` on fire so a late event has nothing to invoke, held in a `shallowRef` (a closure in a deep ref is a Vue 3.5 anti-idiom, edict 7). Since every showConfirm caller lives in this one file, extract the whole 33-line confirm engine (254-286) — it removes a concern from a 391-line SFC rather than adding to one (edict 1).

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** CARRIED (prior seat, re-corroborated by my C-19). The concurrent-expand race renders one user's palettes inside another user's open disclosure and then routes the admin delete against the WRONG owner.

**Mechanism.** A — a value is sourced from a different authority than the one that acts on it; expandedUserSlug and userPalettes are two independent cells joined only by wall-clock order.

**Evidence.**

```
AdminUsersPanel.vue:352-365 — `userPalettes.value = await pm.loadUserPalettes(slug)` with no generation guard; `finally` clears loading for whichever request settles first. Line 150 binds the card's admin delete to the ROW's slug, never the palette's owner: `@admin-delete="emit('adminDeleteUserPalette', $event, user.slug)"`. Prior probe-impl-c3.json (chromium and webkit identical): t_alphaLanded = {openRow:"beta-drifter-00022Pale", disclosure:"ALPHA-PALETTE-AAA 2 0"}, RACE_REPRODUCED true. Prior probe-impl-c3b.json: deleteRequests = ["http://localhost:9077/admin/palettes/alpha-p-1"] issued from beta's row; betaBadge 2->1, alphaBadge 4->4 (both numbers now wrong, in opposite directions). Re-corroborated at this HEAD by probe-C2-implementation.json N6 via a different gesture.
```

**Reproduction.** `VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:9077 npx vite --port 9077` then `node .../probe-impl-c3.mjs` and `.../probe-impl-c3b.mjs`. Cheaper route at this HEAD: `node .../probe-C2-implementation.mjs` (N6 leg) against live :9000, no second server needed.

**Proposed cure.** A colocated `useAdminUserPalettes(slugRef)` keyed resource: watch(slugRef, {flush:'post'}) + AbortController cancelled on key change, returning {palettes, loading, error} bound to the key it was fetched for. The race becomes unrepresentable rather than policed; it also supplies C-4's missing error cell and dissolves the defineExpose imperative surface.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** CARRIED (prior seat). The prune confirmation quotes a SEARCH-FILTERED count for a GLOBALLY SCOPED destruction: the number that describes and gates the action comes from a client-side view filter; the number destroyed is whatever the server finds.

**Mechanism.** A — the described scope and the executed scope have different authorities.

**Evidence.**

```
AdminUsersPanel.vue:241 emptyCount over the `users` prop; AdminPane.vue:28 `:users="pm.filteredAdminUsers.value"` (filtered, useAdminUsers.ts:29-34); demo/palettes/api/admin-users.ts:69 pruneEmptyUsers(token) — POST /admin/users/prune-empty takes no filter, no body, no slug list. Inverse arm C2_filteredNoEmpty: Prune DISABLED while three empty users exist. My C-16 frame (frames-C2/N4-webkit-search-false-negative.png) shows the disabled-arm live at this HEAD. Riders: the title never pluralises ("Prune 1 empty users?") while the description does.
```

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The primary action — add the current colour to the palette — is not a control. `tag="button"`, `:aria-label`, `@click` and the `<Plus>` slot child are all silently discarded by the producer; the add slot renders as a decorative `<span aria-hidden="true" style="pointer-events:none">` with no `+` glyph.

**Mechanism.** consumer passes props/listeners/slot children to a producer component that declares none of them and sets inheritAttrs:false + pointer-events:none — silent attribute-fallthrough loss, invisible to vue-tsc

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:95-105 (consumer). node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js — `inheritAttrs:!1`, props are only {color,variant,animate,cycleDuration,range,seed}, render is `o("span",{"aria-hidden":"true", class:l([c.value…]), style:u([f.value,{…pointerEvents:"none"…}])},[svg…])` with no slot. LIVE (cpe-probe3.mjs): `elements labelled 'Add current color': []`; DOM dump shows `<span aria-hidden="true" class="add-slot-ghost … watercolor-swatch" data-variant="ghost" style="…; pointer-events: none; …">`. LIVE (cpe-probe8.mjs): `4 savedColors length before/after clicking the add slot: 3 3`; `5 elementFromPoint at the add slot centre: {"tag":"DIV","cls":""}`.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000 → dock view-select → Palettes → click the dashed add slot. `localStorage["color-picker"].savedColors` is unchanged; `document.querySelectorAll('[aria-label^="Add current color"]').length === 0`.

**Proposed cure.** Stop pretending pigment is a control: wrap a real focusable design-system control around the decorative dot — `<Button variant="ghost" icon-only :aria-label=… @click=addCurrentColor><WatercolorDot … /><Plus/></Button>` — and delete the non-existent `tag` prop from all six `tag="button"` sites repo-wide (SwatchHoverMenu.vue:17,32, CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:98, MixSourceSelector.vue:168,215, GenerateControls.vue:203). If dot-shaped buttons are wanted as a thing, that variant belongs in glass-ui (edict 4), not in a `tag=` string the producer ignores.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Every current-palette swatch is a decorative aria-hidden, pointer-events:none span, so the touch action path — which the code itself declares to be THE accessible route — is dead: tapping a swatch on a phone opens nothing, and the component's entire accessibility tree contains no colour and no colour action.

**Mechanism.** reka-ui `as-child` merges the trigger's id/aria-expanded/aria-haspopup/onClick onto the child vnode; the child's inheritAttrs:false discards them all, so the Popover trigger is never wired and the swatch is never in the a11y tree or the hit region

**Evidence.**

```
SwatchHoverMenu.vue:13-21,29-36 pass tag/aria-label/@click into the same producer; :38-39 comment: "the reka-ui Popover (touch path) is the accessible route". ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · C-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The duplicate-name `Update` affordance irreversibly destroys a stored palette: `duplicateTarget` is a snapshot ref that is never invalidated when the name or the colour buffer changes, and `confirmUpdatePalette` lacks the emptiness guard its sibling `saveCurrentPalette` has.

**Mechanism.** derived state stored as a snapshot ref; the premise that produced it (a name + a non-empty buffer) can change arbitrarily while the affordance stays live and re-reads the CURRENT buffer at click time

**Evidence.**

```
CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:248 `if (savedColorStrings.length === 0) return;` (guarded) vs :267-276 `confirmUpdatePalette` (unguarded); no watcher clears `duplicateTarget`. Write path: usePaletteActions.ts:79-82 → usePaletteStore.ts:96-107 `palette.colors = patch.colors` into useStorage. LIVE (cpe-probe9.mjs): `1 store after save: [{"name":"Keeper","colors":3}]` … `3 swatches after emptying: 0` … `3 banner still present? "Start a new palette … \"Keeper\" already exists. Update Cancel"` … `4 store AFTER Update with an empty buffer: [{"name":"Keeper","colors":0}]`. Name-loss variant (cpe-probe5.mjs): after retyping "Totally different", the banner still says "Palette 2" already exists and `S store after Update: [{"name":"Palette 2","n":3}]`.
```

**Reproduction.** Save a palette named X; stage colours again; type X + Enter to raise the duplicate banner; remove the staged swatches via the swatch menu; click Update. The stored X now has colors: [] with no undo.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on `demo/palettes/b` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The swatch is not an interactive element: `tag="button"`, `:aria-label` and `@click.stop` are all discarded by glass-ui `WatercolorDot`, which declares `inheritAttrs: false` and renders a hard-coded `<span aria-hidden="true">` with inline `pointer-events: none`. ```
demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:14-20,29-36 (props sent) · node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts (declared props are exactly {color,variant,animate,cycleDuration,range,seed} — no `tag`) · node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js:80 `inheritAttrs: !1,` and :102-110 renders `o("span", {"aria-hidden":"true", … pointerEvents:"none"})` · live measurement: {"tagName":"SPAN","ariaHidden":"true","ariaLabel":null,"tagAttr":null,"attrs":["data-v-292b9032","aria-hidden","class","data-testid","data-variant","style"],"pointerEvents":"none","tabIndex":-1,"parentTag":"DIV","parentAttrs":["class=relative"]} · click probe: {"hitTest":"DIV.relative","panelsBefore":0,"panelsAfterClick":0} · Playwright actionability: `<div class="relative"> intercepts pointer events` (5000ms timeout)
```

**Reproduction.** 1) seed localStorage['color-palettes'] with a local palette before boot; 2) load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes; 3) click a card to expand; 4) `document.querySelector('.watercolor-swatch')` → SPAN, aria-hidden=true, aria-label null, pointer-events none; 5) dispatch a click at the swatch centre → `document.querySelectorAll('.floating-panel').length` stays 0

**Proposed cure.** Move the semantics to the consumer, not the primitive: SwatchHoverMenu renders its own `<button type="button" :aria-label>` and mounts `<WatercolorDot>` inside it as the pure decoration it already is (its `aria-hidden` + `pointer-events:none` then become correct by construction). ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on `demo/palettes/b` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** A malformed palette colour destroys the whole pane: `safeFirstColor` calls `certifyAccentInk`, which handles `parseCssColor`'s `!ok` result but not its THROW. `parseCssColor` throws a TypeError on the entire empty-argument colour-function class (`oklch()`, `rgb()`, `hsl()`, `lab()`, `lch()`, `oklab()`, `hwb()`, `color()`, `rgba()`, whitespace variants, case variants), and the API persists any string up to 200 chars with no colour validation.

**Mechanism.** a Result-returning parser that is actually partial — it throws instead of returning `{ok:false}` for a whole input class — so every caller's `!ok` degenerate is bypassed; this is the standing R1 crash class reaching a render-path computed over unvalidated remote data

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:226-230 (`firstColor` → `safeCss` → `certifyAccentInk`) bound at :144 · demo/color-session/ink.ts:38-43,130-143 (handles `!parsed.ok`, not the throw) · api/src/modules/palette/schema.ts:28 `css: z.string().min(1).max(200)` — no colour validation · vite-node probe over 18 inputs: `threw: 13 / 18`, e.g. `"oklch()" => THREW: TypeError Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')` · exact-call probe (node AND live browser via `import('/@fs/…/demo/color-session/ink.ts')`): `certifyAccentInk("oklch()", 0.45) => THREW: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')` while `"#888"` and `"not-a-color"` return normally · live: seeding colors[0].css="oklch()" and loading /#/palettes replaced the pane with "This panel hit an unexpected error. Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')"
```

**Reproduction.** `npx vite-node` on `import { certifyAccentInk } from 'demo/color-session/ink.ts'; certifyAccentInk('oklch()', 0.45)` → TypeError. Live: seed `localStorage['color-palettes']` with `{version:1,palettes:[{id:'x',name:'M',slug:'m',isLocal:true,colors:[{css:'oklch()',position:0}],createdAt:…,updatedAt:…}]}`, reload /#/palettes.

**Proposed cure.** Fix the parser at the root, not the call site: `parseCssColor` must return `{ok:false}` for the empty-args class (this is R1 from the π parser-proof gate and it is still live). `certifyAccentInk` already carries the correct degenerate — nothing in PaletteCard should change. Independently, `api/src/modules/palette/schema.ts` should refine `css` through the same parser so unparseable colours never persist.

**Defect.** Tag-filter checkboxes bound to `:checked` / `@update:checked`, which glass-ui 7.0.0's Checkbox does not expose (contract is `modelValue` / `update:modelValue`). `:checked` degrades to a dead DOM attribute, `@update:checked` listens for an event never emitted, and the component runs uncontrolled — so it visibly toggles and flips aria-checked to "true" while `update:selectedTags` never fires and nothing filters. **Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:51-55. Contract: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/checkbox/Checkbox.vue.d.ts (CheckboxProps has modelValue/defaultValue/disabled/value/id/class — no `checked`); compiled component node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.js:451 `emits: ["update:modelValue"]`. Measured (vitest+@vue/test-utils mount of the real SFC): rendered HTML `<button data-slot="checkbox" checked="false" role="checkbox" aria-checked="false" data-state="unchecked">`; `emitted after click: ["click"]`, `update:selectedTags = undefined`; `before click data-state: unchecked aria-checked: false` -> `after click data-state: checked aria-checked: true` with `update:selectedTags emitted: undefined`; with props selectedTags=['a','b'], `checkbox aria-checked: [ 'false', 'false' ]`. Family: `grep -rn "<Checkbox" demo/` returns exactly 2 sites — SearchFilterBar.vue:51 and TagEditPopover.vue:27 — and `grep -rn "update:checked|:checked=" demo/` shows both miswired (SearchFilterBar.vue:52-53, TagEditPopover.vue:28-29).
```

**Reproduction.** npx vitest run --config <scratch>/probe.config.ts with a mount of demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue (Popover/PopoverTrigger/PopoverContent stubbed open, availableTags=[{name:'warm'}]): click `[data-slot="checkbox"]` -> data-state flips unchecked->checked and aria-checked false->true, while w.emitted()['update:selectedTags'] is undefined. Latent in prod only because `curl -s https://api.color.babb.dev/colors/tags` returns `[]` (HTTP 200), hiding the section via v-if at line 47; e2e/smoke/admin/flows/tag-create.spec.ts creates tags on every run.

**Proposed cure.** Bind the real contract: `:model-value="selectedTags.includes(tag.name)" @update:model-value="() => toggleTag(tag.name)"` (toggleTag already derives the next array from the prop, so the CheckedState payload is discardable); same repair at TagEditPopover.vue:28-29 where the payload IS used — `(checked) => onToggle(tag.name, checked === true)`. Control `#ff0000` -> [0.6279553639214311,0.2248630684262744,0.125846277330585] (correct). The correct answers the guard threw away, measured through the SAME function: `oklab(hsl(120 100% 50%)) = [0.8664396175234368,-0.23388758093655815,0.1794984451609376]`, `oklab(#f00) = [0.6279553639214311,0.2248630684262744,0.125846277330585]`. The parser is fully capable: SearchFilterBar.vue:206 -> demo/color-session/color-utils.ts:11 -> demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:109-113 (parseCssColor), which throws a typed PickerColorError on real failure (picker-color.ts:112) — the exact error signal the component discards.
```

**Reproduction.** Mount SearchFilterBar (Popover stubbed open), `input[type=text].setValue('hsl(120 100% 50%)')` then `.trigger('keydown.enter')` -> emitted colorSearch payload is the OKLab of #4488cc, not of green. Repeat with '#f00', 'not-a-color', '   ' — identical payload each time; '#ff0000' is the only shape that works.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the regex and the fallback. Parse the trimmed text directly (rename hexToOklab -> cssToOklab, since it was never hex-only); on empty input or PickerColorError set a local `parseError` and DO NOT emit; render parseError into the polite aria-live region C-6 already requires. Net KISS deletion: one regex and one fallback out, one honest error branch in.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/palettes/brows` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The swatch is not an interactive element: glass-ui 7.0.0 `WatercolorDot` declares `inheritAttrs:false` and re-applies only `attrs.class`/`attrs.style`, so `tag="button"`, `:aria-label` and `@click.stop` — plus everything reka's `PopoverTrigger as-child` grafts on — are silently discarded onto a hardcoded `<span aria-hidden="true" style="pointer-events:none">`. The touch popover therefore never opens, `onSwatchClick`/`onPopoverUpdateTouch` are unreachable code, and the swatches are invisible to assistive tech.

**Mechanism.** Silent prop/listener drop across a component boundary — `inheritAttrs:false` with a partial attrs re-application, consumed as if it were a polymorphic `as`/`tag` component. No type or template gate is aimed at unknown props on a producer component.

**Evidence.**

```
Producer source `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js`: `inheritAttrs:!1`, props `{color,variant,animate,cycleDuration,range,seed}` (no `tag`), render `o("span",{"aria-hidden":"true", …, style:u([f.value,{…,pointerEvents:"none",…}])})`. Consumers: SwatchHoverMenu.vue:14-20 and :29-36. iPhone-13 emulation (`matchMedia("(hover: hover)")` → false), expanded card, tap swatch centre → `{"rekaPopover":0,"floatingPanel":false,"addBtn":false}`. Desktop toggle-close proof: with the panel open, clicking the swatch left it open (`desktop.panelAfterClickWhileOpen: true`) — `useHoverPopover.ts:51-54 onSwatchClick` never ran.
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe5.mjs — read `touch.popoverOpen`, `touch.triggerDom`, `desktop.panelAfterClickWhileOpen`. Requires an isolated vite with VITE_API_URL set (the :9000 server latches `misconfigured` and never fetches).

**Proposed cure.** Semantics belong to the consumer, not the decoration: `SwatchHoverMenu` renders its own `<button type="button" :aria-label>` and mounts `<WatercolorDot>` inside it as pure decoration — its `aria-hidden` and `pointer-events:none` then become correct by construction. One element, one file, no new producer prop. A polymorphic `tag` belongs in glass-ui (edict 4) only if genuinely wanted; KISS says do not buy back with a producer prop what a wrapping `<button>` gives free.

Live computed style at 1440×900: `{position:"static", zIndex:"auto", background:"rgba(0,0,0,0)", boxShadow:"none", borderRadius:"0px", parent:"BODY", rect:{top:900,left:-720,w:1440,h:40}, inline:"top: 494.656px; left: 258px; transform: translateX(-50%);"}`. Screenshot <scratchpad>/pcard-hover-panel.png shows the expanded card with the cursor on swatch #1 and no popover on screen. Pass-1 archaeology: the rule was `demo/@/styles/floating-panel.css` (`position:fixed; z-index:var(--z-overlay)`), deleted 2026-03-25 in c84504d3 claiming glass-ui provides it — it does not.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/palettes/brows` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** One malformed colour string on the public browse wall destroys the entire Browse pane for every visitor. `safeFirstColor` → `certifyAccentInk` → `parseCssColor` throws (rather than returning `{ok:false}`) on the empty-argument colour-function class, and the pane's error boundary swallows the whole wall including innocent neighbouring palettes.

**Mechanism.** A total function is advertised where a partial one ships: `certifyAccentInk` has the correct degenerate (`if (!accent) return css`) but the throw bypasses it. Combined with an error boundary that absorbs the throw, the failure is invisible to every console-scraping gate.

**Evidence.**

```
Four one-palette walls each seeded alongside an innocent "Neighbour", expand the first card: `oklch()` → articles 2 → 0, paneText "This panel hit an unexpected error. Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace') Try again", pageErrors [] consoleErrors []. `""` → 2 → 2 (no crash). `not-a-color` → 2 → 2. `#e11d48` control → 2 → 2. Call site PaletteCard.vue:230 `safeFirstColor = computed(() => safeCss(firstColor.value))`, consumed only by the expanded region (PaletteCard.vue:144 → PaletteCardSwatches.vue:10). Reachability: api/src/modules/palette/schema.ts:28 `css: z.string().min(1).max(200)` — no colour validation.
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe9.mjs — read the `oklch-empty` row (`articlesBefore` 2, `articlesAfter` 0, `paneText`).

**Proposed cure.** Three layers, all at the root. Library: `parseCssColor` returns `{ok:false}` for the empty-args class (π-gate R1, still live). API: the schema validates a colour, not a 200-char string. Demo: nothing about PaletteCard's structure changes. Additionally (C-3b) `PaletteCard.vue:226` uses `??`, so an empty-string css is not nullish and bypasses the documented `EMPTY_PALETTE_SWATCH` fallback entirely — use `||` with `.trim()`, and have PaletteColorStrip fall back per-segment to the same named token.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/palettes/brows` · C-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The card's primary action (expand/collapse — the only route to the swatches, the slug and every per-colour affordance) is mouse-only: a `<div role="article">` with `@click`, `cursor-pointer`, no `tabindex`, no `@keydown`, no `aria-expanded`. WCAG 2.1.1 Level A.

**Mechanism.** A disclosure control was implemented as a clickable container. The `role="article"` justification in the header comment (PaletteCard.vue:2-4) is correct for a container that is not itself a control, but this one owns @click, cursor-pointer and a press animation.

**Evidence.**

```
`cardStructure: [{tag:"div", role:"article", tabindex:null, ariaExpanded:null, cursor:"pointer", label:"Palette: Ember Rose"}, …]` (PaletteCard.vue:5-27). 22 real Tab presses across the populated wall: `tabReachedArticle: false` — the sequence reaches the card's descendants ("5 votes, click to vote", "Palette menu") but never the card. `el.focus()` → `{cardFocusable:false, activeTag:"body"}`. Compounding: glass-ui `useLiquidPress-BOxuDkKa.js` returns `onKeydown`/`onKeyup` (with an explicit `e.key==="Enter"||e.key===" "` leg) and `onBlur`; PaletteCard.vue:24 binds all eight handlers to that unfocusable div — three are structurally dead.
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe2.mjs — read `tabSequence` / `tabReachedArticle`; node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe3.mjs — read `cardStructure`, `keyboardEnter`.

**Proposed cure.** Put a real `<button aria-expanded>` on the card's own header row (title + colour count), keep `role="article"` on the container, and delete the container `@click`. Fixes 2.1.1, gives `useLiquidPress` a legitimate focusable host, announces the state (C-15), removes the MixSourceSelector wrapper-button hack (C-14), and cures the title dead zone (C-9) for free.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/palettes/brows` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** "Rename" from the card menu opens a text input that is immediately focus-stolen by reka's DropdownMenu focus-restore, so the caret never lands in the field and the user's first Enter/Space re-opens the menu. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/palettes/Brows` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The browse wall is non-functional in every Safari matrix, and the pane surfaces a false diagnosis: a client-side JSON-parse failure is rendered as "The commons is unreachable." `request()` returns `res.json()` unguarded (no content-type check) and `loadRemotePalettes` discards the typed error, replacing it with one constant string for all four distinguishable failure classes.

```
audit/visual/REPORT.json — /#/browse, 4/4 matrices: consoleWarnings ['Failed to load remote palettes: SyntaxError: The string did not match the expected pattern.'], bodyTextLength 280/124; shots/safari-desktop-light/browse.png renders the error plate, zero cards. probe-C-webkit-json.mjs: `== WebKit ==  /good PARSED OK · /empty|/html|/trailing SyntaxError: The string did not match the expected pattern.` `curl -D - http://localhost:9000/palettes?limit=50&sort=newest` → `HTTP/1.1 200 OK / Content-Type: text/html`. Sites: demo/platform/transport/client.ts:118, demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:79, demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:62-67.
```

Confirmed: 4/4 captured matrices + the WebKit message-identification probe + the curl showing a 200 text/html body on the palette path.

**Proposed cure.** `request()` guards the parse (content-type check → throw a typed ApiProblem/ApiMalformedResponse carrying status + a body excerpt); `browseError` becomes `Ref<ApiProblem | Error | null>`; the EmptyState `detail` slot renders the real machine truth (the DevMisconfig message is already written to be actionable and currently dies in the console).

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/palettes/Brows` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `loadingMore` is stranded TRUE for the session whenever any reload supersedes an in-flight cursor continuation. The load-more affordance dies permanently and two developing plates sit at the foot of the wall forever; palettes 51+ become unreachable.

```
demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:112 `finally { if (gen === loadGeneration) loadingMore.value = false; }` — the generation guard is correct for the append and wrong for the flag; :98 then rejects every future click and nothing else ever writes the flag false. The button never returns for the rest of the session. Reproduced live and in 2 unit probes.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/palettes/browse` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Concurrent-expand race: `toggleUserExpand` writes `userPalettes` from an awaited fetch with no request-generation guard, so a late response for user A renders inside user B's open disclosure — and the admin delete then destroys A's palette while decrementing B's count.

**Mechanism.** Value not bound to its key — `expandedUserSlug` and `userPalettes` are two independent cells joined only by wall-clock order; nothing records which request a resolved value belongs to.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:352-365 (`userPalettes.value = await pm.loadUserPalettes(slug)`; `finally` clears loading first-to-settle) and :150 (`@admin-delete="emit('adminDeleteUserPalette', $event, user.slug)"`). probe-impl-c3.json, BOTH engines identical: `t_betaSettled: {openRow: "beta-drifter-00022Pale", disclosure: "BETA-PALETTE-BBB 2 0"}` then `t_alphaLanded: {openRow: "beta-drifter-00022Pale", disclosure: "ALPHA-PALETTE-AAA 2 0"}`, `RACE_REPRODUCED: true`. probe-impl-c3b.json: `deleteRequests: ["http://localhost:9077/admin/palettes/alpha-p-1"]`, `VERDICT: {betaBadgeBefore:"2", betaBadgeAfter:"1", alphaBadgeBefore:"4", alphaBadgeAfter:"4"}`. useAdminUsers.ts:118-121 decrements the owner passed by the row. Frames: frames-impl/C3b-{chromium,webkit}-beta-shows-alpha.png.
```

**Reproduction.** VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:9077 npx vite --port 9077 ; node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-impl-c3.mjs (race, 2 engines) ; node .../probe-impl-c3b.mjs (the destroying DELETE + badge deltas). Serve alpha's /admin/users/*/palettes with 1500ms delay and beta's with 40ms; click alpha, wait 300ms, click beta.

**Proposed cure.** Do not add a sequence counter to the current shape — the shape is the defect. Express the disclosure as the keyed resource it is: a colocated `useAdminUserPalettes(slugRef)` driven by `watch(slugRef, …)` with an AbortController cancelled on key change, returning `{ palettes, loading, error }` bound to the key they were fetched for. A response for a stale key then has nowhere to land — the race becomes unrepresentable rather than policed. Side effects: supplies C-4's missing `error` cell, and removes userPalettes/removeUserPalette/updatePaletteTier/clearUserPalettes from the :389 defineExpose (the adjudicated L-1/L-2 inversion) as a consequence rather than as separate work.

This will permanently delete 1 user with 0 palettes and their sessions. This cannot be undone."`. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-4 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** RTL fabricates identifiers. The hand-rolled two-span tail-priority slug split has no bidi isolation, so `empty-ghost-account-aaaa-33` renders on screen as `aaa-33empty-ghost-account-a` — a string that does not exist. The row and its own delete confirmation then display two different identities for the same account.

**Mechanism.** An identifier composed by string concatenation across two DOM nodes instead of rendered as one typed, direction-isolated value.

**Evidence.**

```
AdminUsersPanel.vue:97-101 (two sibling spans) + :246-252 (slugHead/slugTail). Probe C under dir=rtl: {"headText":"an-extremely-long-…-2","headL":1010.5,"headR":1194,"tailText":"f9a-33","tailL":950,"tailR":1010.5,"tailRenderedLeftOfHead":true}. Frame frames-D2/C-populated-rtl-desktop.png shows `aaa-33empty-ghost-account-a`, `aaa-77empty-ghost-account-a`, `bbb-11empty-three-b`. The dialog quotes the raw unsplit slug at :169. The count line likewise renders "empty 3 · users 6" (from :8-13). Law verbatim, VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:133 — slug/ID must keep "identical domain meaning inside an LTR-isolated value … no custom bidi reinterpretation"; :154 — "slugs, IDs and provenance | render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose".
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-D2.mjs (section C), or set document.documentElement.dir='rtl' on a populated #/admin/users. Also visible without data in the shipped capture docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/rtl-desktop/adminusers.png ("users 0").

**Proposed cure.** Delete the split entirely. Head-elision with a protected tail is one CSS declaration on one LTR-isolated text node (`direction: rtl; text-overflow: ellipsis` inside a `<bdi>`), not two spans and two string functions. That single transposition also removes the viewport-dependent ellipsis gap artefact (390: `empty-ghost-acco…  aaa-33` with a visible inter-token gap; 1440: no gap).

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-01 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** One Retry click permanently blanks the pane body. Transition mode="out-in" on the three-state container makes DOM presence a function of a 200ms animation clock, while the state machine settles synchronously; the pending enter never mounts and the pane is left as a void under the search field with no error, no empty plate, no skeleton and no recovery.

**Mechanism.** Animation clock owns DOM presence — branch identity is animated with mode="out-in" across an async boundary that can settle faster than the leave duration.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:40 (`<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">`); demo/platform/transport/availability.ts:188-195 (assertApiAttemptAllowed throws synchronously, unconditional for `misconfigured`). Live Playwright/WebKit 1440x900, sampled every 25ms from the click: t=0 n=1 h=224.5 "The commons is unreachable.Failed to load palettes"; t=28 n=1 vj-morph-leave-from|vj-morph-leave-active; t=227 n=1 vj-morph-leave-active|vj-morph-leave-to; t=251 n=0 h=12.0 ""; t=1202 n=0 h=12.0 "". Second clean-page run, 6s tail: {wrapChildren:0, wrapH:12, paneText:"BrowseDiscover palettes from the community."}; after typing into the search field: {wrapChildren:0, same paneText}. Screenshots: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/evidence/D-browse-before-retry.png vs D-browse-after-retry-6s.png.
```

**Reproduction.** 1) `http://localhost:9000/#/browse` at 1440x900 (dev server without VITE_API_URL, so the misconfigured latch is armed — the state all 60 audit captures show). 2) Wait ~3.5s for the error plate. 3) Click Retry once. 4) The state container's element children go 1→0 at ~251ms and stay 0 indefinitely; wrapper height 224.5px→12px. Typing in the search box does not restore it.

**Proposed cure.** Stop animating branch identity. Keep one persistent state region whose CONTENT cross-fades (default simultaneous mode), or drop the Transition on the state container entirely and let the individual plates own their entrance. A v-if guard inside mode="out-in" only narrows the window; it does not close the class.

**Defect.** The application's ONLY login-failure copy is imperatively pushed into this orphan through a template ref that is never bound to any element. A wrong slug in the live dock therefore fails completely silently — no message, no announcement, no visual state.

Chain, each link verified: (1) demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:83-87 routes all four failure strings into `slugBarRef.value?.setError(...)`. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-4 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** RTL fabricates identifiers: the two-span slug split reorders under bidi, so `empty-ghost-account-aaaa-33` renders as `aaa-33empty-ghost-account-a`. Zero `<bdi>` on the page.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** Inverted dependency: the domain/server-state composable `useAdminUsers` imports the SFC, holds a template-ref to its instance, and mutates the component's private state through 5 `defineExpose`d members. Latent module cycle; 5 optional-chain masking fallbacks.

**Mechanism.** Split ownership: `expandedUserSlug`/`userPalettes`/`loadingUserPalettes` (AdminUsersPanel.vue:236-238) are stored in the view but every mutation originates in the state layer, so the state layer must reach across the layer boundary through an instance handle.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:14 `import type { AdminUsersPanel } from "./browser/admin";` · :27 `const adminUsersPanelRef = ref<InstanceType<typeof AdminUsersPanel> | null>(null);` · :95 `adminUsersPanelRef.value?.updatePaletteTier(...)` · :117 `?.removeUserPalette(...)` · :132/:146 `?.clearUserPalettes(...)` · demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:123 `admin.adminUsersPanelRef.value?.onPruneDone(pruned);` · demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue:27,:134 · AdminUsersPanel.vue:389 `defineExpose({ removeUserPalette, updatePaletteTier, clearUserPalettes, onPruneDone, userPalettes })`. Measured: `grep -rn --include='*.ts' 'from "[^"]*\.vue"' demo/ | wc -l` = 25, of which 24 are barrel re-exports — useAdminUsers.ts:14 is the sole state module importing a component. `grep -rn --include='*.vue' defineExpose demo/` = 14 sites; this is the largest (5) and the only one whose consumer is a composable. tsconfig.base.json:8 `verbatimModuleSyntax: true` is why the cycle erases.
```

**Reproduction.** AdminPane.vue:26 mounts the panel under `v-if="subView === 'admin-users'"`. Call `useAdminUsers.onDeleteUser(slug)` (:140-150) and switch the admin sub-view during the `await deleteUser(token, slug)`; `adminUsersPanelRef.value` is then null and the `?.` at :146 silently swallows `clearUserPalettes(slug)`. The panel remounts with the deleted user's `userPalettes` never cleared. Same swallow at all 5 call sites.

**Proposed cure.** Lift the three refs into a `useAdminUserPalettes()` composable colocated with `useAdminUsers`; the panel receives them as props and emits `toggleUserExpand`. Then delete AdminUsersPanel.vue:352-389 (4 state fns + defineExpose), useAdminUsers.ts:14/:27 and the 4 `?.` call sites, usePalettePorts.ts:123/:197, AdminPane.vue:27/:134. Net: −5 exposed members, −1 port member, −1 inverted import, −1 latent cycle, −5 masking fallbacks.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** PaletteCard feeds arbitrary user/API color strings into `certifyAccentInk`, a demo-side wrapper that converts the library's typed Result error into a thrown exception during render. Any palette color carrying alpha < 1 destroys the whole hosting pane via the error boundary; zero cards render and the poison is persisted in localStorage.

**Mechanism.** Ownership inversion at the library boundary: the library owns 'certification may fail, here is a typed error'; demo/color-session/ink.ts unilaterally re-declares it as 'cannot fail' and PaletteCard consumes that re-declaration on untrusted data. A total function was made partial at the wrong layer.

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteCard.vue:226 `firstColor = props.palette.colors[0]?.css ?? …`; PaletteCard.vue:229-230 `const { safeCss } = useSafeAccentFn("well"); const safeFirstColor = computed(() => safeCss(firstColor.value))`; demo/color-session/ink.ts:78 `if (!result.ok) throw new Error(`Ink certification failed: ${result.error.code}`)`; src/color/operations.ts:213-214 `if (accent.alpha !== 1 || surface.alpha !== 1) return err({ code: "color_invalid_input" })`. node against the served dist: `lab(50% 20 10 / 82.7%) => safeAccent ERR color_invalid_input`, `oklch(0.7 0.1 200 / 0.5) => ERR color_invalid_input`, `#e11d48 => OK`. Live: pane shows `This panel hit an unexpected error. / color_non_finite`, articles: 0. The app's own persisted state held `color-picker = {"inputColor":"lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)"}`, i.e. it mints alpha'd colors itself.
```

**Reproduction.** With the dev server live at http://localhost:9000: (1) in the page, `localStorage.setItem('color-palettes', JSON.stringify({version:1,palettes:[{id:'p',slug:'p',name:'Probe',isLocal:true,colors:[{css:'lab(50% 20 10 / 82.7%)',position:0},{css:'#0ea5e9',position:1}]}]}))`; (2) full reload of `/#/palettes`, settle 2s. Observed `{url:'http://localhost:9000/#/palettes', boundary:true, bodyHead:'…This panel hit an unexpected error.\n\ncolor_non_finite…', articles:0}`. Repeats with `lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)`. Control with `['#e11d48','#0ea5e9']` → no boundary. (Exact throw site among ink.ts:47/59/78 is a hypothesis; the Result-to-throw class is confirmed.)

**Proposed cure.** Make `certifyAccentInk` TOTAL on dynamic input — return the input css (or the muted-ink token) for every non-certifiable value, exactly as it already does for unparseable input at ink.ts:136, and add the alpha pre-condition the library states at operations.ts:214. Keep throws only for producer literals (ink.ts:53), which are build-time invariants. Then no ink consumer can crash a pane and PaletteCard needs no guard at all.

**Defect.** The state layer imports the view and drives it through a template ref. `useAdminUsers` (a server-state composable) imports the SFC's type, holds its INSTANCE, and mutates the component's private state via defineExpose'd methods; the instance handle is published on the app-wide ADMIN_PORT_KEY surface. Yields a type-level cycle (erased only by `import type` + verbatimModuleSyntax), five masking `?.` swallows, and mutators that see one list but not the other.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:14 `import type { AdminUsersPanel } from "./browser/admin";` · :27 `ref<InstanceType<typeof AdminUsersPanel>|null>` · :95/:117/:132/:146 `adminUsersPanelRef.value?.<method>()` · demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:123 `admin.adminUsersPanelRef.value?.onPruneDone(pruned)` · :197 publishes the handle on adminPort · demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue:27 `ref="adminUsersPanelRef"` + :134 `const adminUsersPanelRef = pm.adminUsersPanelRef` (the pane BORROWS the composable's ref) · AdminUsersPanel.vue:389 defineExpose of 5 members incl. mutable `userPalettes`. ### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-16 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** useHoverPopover reads `e.currentTarget` inside a nextTick callback — i.e. after event dispatch has completed, when the DOM spec guarantees it is null. Every swatch hover throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getBoundingClientRect')` and the popover's position is never applied. The `as Element` cast is the masking assertion that hid it from vue-tsc.

**Mechanism.** Hand-rolled floating positioning inside a demo composable, duplicating @mkbabb/glass-ui/popover which the same component already imports and uses on its other branch. A dual path (edict 2) reimplementing a design-system primitive (edict 4); the `as Element` cast (edict 2 — masking fallback) let the null flow through typecheck.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHoverPopover.ts:30 — `nextTick(() => positionPanel(e.currentTarget as Element));`. Live capture with an unhandledrejection listener: {"captured":["REJ:TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getBoundingClientRect')"],"inline":"top: 0px; left: 0px; transform: translateX(-50%);"} — the inline top/left are still the reactive initial 0px, proving positionPanel never completed. Spec: DOM Standard §2.2 — "The currentTarget attribute … When an event is dispatched, this is set to the object whose listener is being invoked, and reset to null afterwards."
```

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The Tags filter is inert — the component binds `:checked` / `@update:checked`, an API glass-ui 7.0.0's Checkbox does not have. The control is left uncontrolled: it ticks visually, never emits anything the parent listens for, and never resets when the filter state is cleared.

**Mechanism.** Consumer speaks a retired design-system API; Vue admits unknown attrs as fallthrough and unknown on* handlers as native listeners, so the prop/emit rename is silent at both runtime and typecheck.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:51-55. Spec: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/checkbox/Checkbox.vue.d.ts:4-12,19 declares `modelValue?: CheckedState | null` and `"update:modelValue": (value: CheckedState) => any`. Measured runtime: props=["modelValue","defaultValue","disabled","value","id","class","asChild","as","name","required"] emits=["update:modelValue"]. `grep -rl "update:checked" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` → no matches. Mount probe output: EMITTED: ["update:modelValue"] · DOM: <button data-slot="checkbox" … checked="false" role="checkbox" … data-state="checked"> (the `checked` prop landed as a raw fallthrough attribute; data-state flipped from the control's own internal state). `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → EXIT=0. Identical defect at demo/palettes/browser/search/TagEditPopover.vue:27-30 (the tag WRITE path) — the demo's only other Checkbox usage.
```

**Reproduction.** npx vitest run --config <scratch cfg pointing root at repo>; probe file mounts glass-ui Checkbox with {checked:false, 'onUpdate:checked', 'onUpdate:modelValue'}, clicks [role=checkbox], asserts the emit ledger → EMITTED: ["update:modelValue"]. In-app: open /#/browse ⋮ → Tags, tick a tag; the badge stays 0 and the wall does not change; then Clear all filters and the tick remains.

**Proposed cure.** Controlled v-model shape: `<Checkbox :model-value="selectedTags.includes(tag.name)" @update:model-value="() => toggleTag(tag.name)" />`, same at TagEditPopover.vue:27-30. Architecturally: make the class of defect impossible — FilterMenu becomes stateless over one `v-model:query` object (see L-4 cure), so no local/uncontrolled state can desynchronise from the wall; and close the gate that let glass-ui 7 land un-migrated (a vue/no-undef-properties-class rule for glass-ui components, since vue-tsc exits 0 on all of these today).

### `L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, depende` · L-1 · L

**Defect.** The state layer imports the view and drives it through a template ref. `useAdminUsers.ts:14` imports the SFC type; `:27` holds its instance; `:95/117/132/146` + `usePalettePorts.ts:123` mutate component-private state through a 5-member `defineExpose` (`AdminUsersPanel.vue:389`). The handle is published on the app-wide ADMIN port (`usePalettePorts.ts:197`) and the mount site BORROWS it (`AdminPane.vue:134`). Type cycle: useAdminUsers -> browser/admin/index.ts -> AdminUsersPanel.vue -> usePalettePorts -> useAdminUsers. Consequence: `onAdminDeleteUserPalette` (`useAdminUsers.ts:112-125`) updates the panel copy and the server but NEVER `deps.remotePalettes` — while its sibling `onAdminDeletePalette` (`:101-110`) does — so Browse renders a deleted palette until reload.

**Mechanism.** Inverted ownership: one concept ('the palettes of the expanded admin user') has its STORAGE in the view (AdminUsersPanel.vue:236-238) and its MUTATORS in the composable, bridged by a broadcast instance handle. The lower layer depends on the higher one.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:14,27,95,117,132,146; demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:123,197; demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue:27,134; demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:389. Divergence re-read this pass at useAdminUsers.ts:112-125 (no `deps.remotePalettes` write) vs :101-110 (filter present).
```

Behavioural reproduction (NOT executed — needs an admin token and the step is destructive; this seat is read-only): authenticate as admin -> #/browse, note palette P -> #/admin/users, expand P's owner -> delete P from the row -> #/browse: P is still listed.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/picker/ColorPic` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The hero readout renders `contenteditable="true"` on a span whose children Vue owns and patches (`.fig-int`/`.fig-frac`). Any user edit replaces those nodes; every later patch writes into detached nodes and silently no-ops, so the cell is permanently orphaned from the vdom and displays a value that is not the color.

**Mechanism.** Vue-controlled subtree made user-writable: contenteditable lets the browser mutate DOM that the virtual DOM believes it owns, so vnode-held element references go stale and patching becomes a no-op.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/picker/display/ColorComponentDisplay/ColorComponentDisplay.vue:21-39. Live Playwright probe against http://localhost:9000/#/ returned: {"afterTyping":["45","20.1","10"],"afterTypingInnerHTML":"<b>45</b>","afterSliderDrag_cells":["45","20.1","10"],"afterSliderDrag_innerHTML":"<b>45</b>","afterSliderDrag_meter":["43.8%","20.1","10.0","100.0%"],"url":"http://localhost:9000/#/?space=lab&color=lab(43.8%25+20.05+10)"} — URL, page title and channel meter all say 43.8; the hero readout says 45. The `<b>` wrapper proves the browser destroyed Vue's two child spans (and that the field accepts arbitrary rich text/paste).
```

**Reproduction.** 1) Open http://localhost:9000/#/ . 2) Click the `l` readout cell, press Cmd+A, type `45`, wait 1200ms. 3) Focus the L channel slider thumb (`.channel-slider [role="slider"]` first) and press ArrowLeft 12 times. 4) Read `document.querySelectorAll('.readout-fig')[0].innerText` (= "45") against `location.href` and `.channel-meter` (= 43.8%).

**Proposed cure.** Architectural transposition, already half-ordered by W48 §Work-1: delete the contenteditable path entirely; render the tuple as a read-only numeric headline and put editing in real `<input type="number">` controls. A Vue-controlled subtree may never be contenteditable — there is no patch that makes it safe. Also strengthen W48's completion gate: its `agree in one settled routed frame` check is single-frame and would pass with this defect fully present; it must edit a cell, then change the color by an independent path, then assert agreement.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/picker/ColorPic` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** All five channels share ONE 500ms debounce timer instance, so a numeric edit to channel A silently cancels a pending edit to channel B. User edits are lost with no error and no visual signal.

**Mechanism.** Debounce over a multiplexed argument: the primitive assumes successive calls express the same pending intent, but the `component` argument makes each call a distinct intent, so coalescing them is data loss rather than throttling.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-session/useColorPipeline.ts:209 (`const updateColorComponentDebounced = debounce(updateColorComponent, 500)`) over the single-timer closure at demo/shared/utils.ts:22-44; both ColorPicker.vue:51 and ColorPicker.vue:233 route every channel through that one instance. Unit repro via `npx tsx`: an `l` write at t=0 and an `a` write at t=100ms produced `applied writes: [[80,"a"]]` — the `l` write never executed. Live repro from `lab(80% 20 30)`: typed `30` into `l`, then 120ms later `10` into `b`; final `url":"http://localhost:9000/#/?space=lab&color=lab(80%25+20+10)"` — b took 10, l is still 80, the `30` is gone.
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/#/?space=lab&color=lab(80%25+20+30) . Click the `l` readout cell, Cmd+A, type `30`. Within 500ms click the `b` cell, Cmd+A, type `10`. Wait 1.5s and read location.href — it reads lab(80% 20 10); the l edit is discarded.

**Proposed cure.** Key the debounce per channel (`Map<string, debounced>`) — or, KISS and preferred with C-1's cure, drop the debounce entirely: real `<input>` editors commit on change/blur and need no coalescing. Note W48 §Work-3 makes 'W21 numeric fields the sole editors' without noticing this, so landing those fields on the same shared instance would reship the defect in new markup.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/picker/ColorPic` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The window keydown listener is registered in `onMounted` while the component lives inside `<KeepAlive>`, so `onUnmounted` never fires on deactivation. The listener stays live on every other route and calls `e.preventDefault()`, hijacking Cmd+K app-wide.

**Mechanism.** KeepAlive lifecycle mismatch: mount/unmount hooks used where activate/deactivate hooks are required, so a global side effect outlives the component's visible lifetime.

**Evidence.**

```
ColorPicker.vue:376-385 (onMounted/onUnmounted) under demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:120-127 (`<KeepAlive :max="6">`), mounted at demo/color-picker/App.vue:101-110. Live probe after SPA-internal navigation to #/gradient: {"afterSwitch":{"hash":"#/gradient","pickerInDom":false,"gradientPresent":true},"events":[{"k":"Meta","meta":true,"dp":false},{"k":"k","meta":true,"dp":true}],"pickerExpanded":"absent"} — the picker is NOT in the document yet its handler still ran and still returned defaultPrevented=true. The correct idiom is used in the same directory: demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:246 uses onActivated() and explains why at :232-245.
```

**Reproduction.** 1) Load http://localhost:9000/#/ and wait for the picker to mount. 2) `location.hash = '#/gradient'` (SPA route change, no reload); wait 2.5s; confirm `document.querySelector('.title-row button')` is null. 3) Install a window keydown logger, press Meta+k. 4) The logged event has defaultPrevented === true. Cmd+K is now swallowed on /gradient, /browse, /extract, /mix, /generate, /atmosphere, /blob and all five /admin/* routes.

**Proposed cure.** Move the listener to `onActivated`/`onDeactivated`, and re-scope the shortcut off `window` onto the picker's own subtree so it cannot be a global keyboard claim in the first place.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/picker/ColorPic` · C-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `onStartEdit` calls the throwing `parseColor` on untrusted, API-sourced palette CSS with no guard, from inside a bare setTimeout that Vue's ErrorBoundary cannot catch. The throw leaves `preEditModel` populated and `editTarget` null — the edit machine wedges and the click is dead.

**Mechanism.** A throwing parse wrapper with no single enforced boundary: half the call sites remember to catch, half do not, and the unguarded ones sit in async callbacks outside the framework's error path.

**Evidence.**

```
ColorPicker.vue:282-289; `parseColor` -> `parsePickerColor` throws at demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:109-113. Call site is demo/color-picker/composables/usePaletteWiring.ts:113-122, inside `setTimeout(...)` — outside Vue error propagation, so `<ErrorBoundary>` (App.vue:50) cannot catch it. Measured parser behaviour via `npx tsx` against src/css/index.ts: "oklch()" THREW TypeError Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace'); "light-dark(#fff, #000)" NOT-OK; "color-mix(in oklab, red, blue)" NOT-OK; "currentcolor" NOT-OK; "#12345" NOT-OK. The same hole exists on the second exposed entry point: useColorPipeline.ts:182-188 (`applyExternalColor`) parses unguarded and usePaletteWiring.ts:122-123 calls it directly — while onPaletteAddColor/onPaletteApply/applyColorString (useColorPipeline.ts:212-257) DO try/catch, showing the guarding is inconsistent.
```

**Reproduction.** Parser class is reproduced directly: `npx tsx -e 'import {parseCssColor} from "/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/src/css/index.ts"; parseCssColor("oklch()")'` throws TypeError. End-to-end: a stored palette color of `color-mix(in oklab, red, blue)`, `light-dark(#fff,#000)`, `currentcolor` or `oklch()` returned by api.color.babb.dev, then clicking that swatch's edit affordance, hits ColorPicker.vue:286 unguarded. (Full end-to-end not driven live — the local API is CORS-blocked in this dev config per REPORT.md:17 — so the end-to-end arm is labelled a hypothesis; the parser arm is measured.)

**Proposed cure.** Collapse the parse boundary to one place: return the `Result` the library already produces and let call sites branch, instead of a throwing wrapper. Until then, guard onStartEdit and applyExternalColor and surface a real failure to the user rather than an unhandled window error.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-01 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The `contenteditable` numeric headline is an unguarded write path with no commit, cancel, clamp, or error semantics. Display, AT announcement, URL and document title disagree after a single keystroke, and the card-lock the whole reservation system exists to hold breaks mid-typing.

**Mechanism.** Editing job fused into the display job: one DOM node is simultaneously the reactive render target and the user's text-entry surface, and the model clamp/format lives at the pipeline seam, downstream of the paint. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 ("read-only contiguous numeric readout"), §4 ("editing occurs only in W21's semantic numeric fields"), PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.10 ("no duplicate contenteditable path").

**Evidence.**

```
demo/picker/display/ColorComponentDisplay/ColorComponentDisplay.vue:22-23 (contenteditable="true" role="textbox"); demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:223-235 (onComponentInput → parseFloat → updateColorComponentDebounced). Live Playwright transcript at 1440x900, route #/?space=lab&color=lab(50% 20 30): t0 cells ["50.0 % ,","20.0 ,","30.0"] sliders "a axis 20.0" title "lab(50% 20 30)"; t1 cells [...,"20.05 ,",...] ; t2(+900ms) cells [...,"20.1 ,",...] sliders "a axis 20.1" title "lab(50% 20.05 30)" url #/?space=lab&color=lab(50%25+20.05+30). Second run, insertText('9999999999'): before readout 441.8x122.4 card h 684.8 scrollW 442 = clientW 442; during readout 469.0x183.6 (+61.2px = one 1.12em line) card h 693.2 (+8.4px) scrollW 477 > clientW 469 (8px inner overflow); settled back to 122.4/684.8 with title "lab(50% 20.19999999999 30)".
```

**Reproduction.** Serve the demo (http://localhost:9000/), open #/?space=lab&color=lab(50%25%2020%2030) at 1440x900, wait for settle, focus the second [contenteditable="true"][role="textbox"] cell, collapse the selection to the end of its contents, document.execCommand('insertText', false, '5'), wait 900ms, then read the cell text, every [role=slider] aria-valuetext, location.hash and document.title. Repeat with '9999999999' while sampling .readout and the picker card getBoundingClientRect before / during / after.

**Proposed cure.** Transposition, not validation. Split the headline's three fused jobs: the route <h1> is owned by the shell, the readout becomes a pure projection (<output>, no contenteditable, no role=textbox, no tab stop), and editing moves whole into the domain-neutral axis composition over BI Slider that W48 already specifies — which owns commit/cancel/error and formats through the same cell the headline projects. One writer, one formatter, one truth. Do not add validation to the contenteditable; delete the writer.

### `design` · D-1 · design

**Defect.** In forced-colors mode the slider track's extent is 1.00:1 against the well (invisible) and the focus indicator disappears entirely, because both are expressed in the single channel forced-colors overrides.

**Mechanism.** Single-channel control semantics: the track's entire visual definition routes through `background` (a custom property), which forced-colors overrides to Canvas; no border and no painted range remain as a second channel. Focus ships as box-shadow with outline-style:none, and forced-colors strips shadows. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:84 ("Focus remains visibly distinct ... forced colors") and WCAG 1.4.11. `grep -rn forced-colors demo/scenes/` returns zero hits.

**Evidence.**

```
Chromium forcedColors:"active", /#/atmosphere 1440x900 (scratchpad/chD-csp-probe2.mjs -> forcedFocus): trackBg rgb(255,255,255) === wellBg rgb(255,255,255), trackEqualsWell:true, trackBorderWidth 0px, rangeBg rgba(0,0,0,0); outlineStyle:"none", boxShadow:"none". Frame: scratchpad/chD-csp-forced-focus.png shows three orphan pill outlines with no track. Cause: ConfigSliderPane.vue:202 `--slider-track-bg: var(--ink-muted, var(--muted-foreground))`. The tracked matrix shots/forced-colors-desktop/blob.png could not catch this — WebKit ignores Playwright's forcedColors, so that frame is byte-comparable to the ordinary light frame.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/chD-csp-probe2.mjs (Chromium arm); or Chrome DevTools -> Rendering -> Emulate CSS forced-colors: active -> http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere

**Proposed cure.** Fold into the F1 cure: retire variant="spectrum" so the producer's `.slider-range` paints the value, delete ConfigSliderPane.vue:202 and :204-206, and let glass-ui's Slider own a forced-colors arm — `border: 1px solid` on `.slider-track`, `.slider-range { background: Highlight; forced-color-adjust: none }`, and `outline` (not box-shadow) for :focus-visible. Producer change, not demo (edict 4).

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/shell/dock/Col` · R2-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The send button can never submit typed text: `onInputBlur` wipes the contenteditable back to the canonical colour, and because the UA moves focus on mousedown but fires click on mouseup, `onSubmitColor` always reads the already-wiped DOM and re-submits the stale colour.

**Mechanism.** DOM-as-source-of-truth: a mutable DOM node is both the draft store and the read-back channel, with two handlers writing and reading it in UA-imposed order.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:191 (`inputColorRef.value.innerText = formattedCurrentColor.value`) and :215 (`parseAndSetColor(inputColorRef.value.innerText)`). Live measurement: {"committed":"rgb(255 0 0)","typed":"rebeccapurple","afterBlur":"rgb(255 0 0)","afterSend":"rgb(255 0 0)"} in 292 ms total. Short-circuit that hides it: demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:69.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/ → dock → 'Toggle action bar' → 'Open color input'. Focus the field, type a new valid colour, click the arrow (send) button within 2 s. Nothing happens; ~2 s later the colour changes anyway.

**Proposed cure.** Retire the contenteditable as the source of truth. Hold the draft in a local `shallowRef<string>` written by @input, render from it, and let blur only decide whether to DISCARD the draft — never rewrite a node a pending click is about to read. `onSubmitColor` then reads the ref and the blur/click ordering is irrelevant. This is edict 7's synchronous-local-cache idiom, and it dissolves round 1's C-16 (six imperative innerText writers over three sources of truth) in the same stroke.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/shell/dock/Col` · R2-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The 2000 ms debounced parse is never cancelled by this component — not on blur, Enter, send, mode switch, or unmount (there is no onUnmounted at all) — so an abandoned edit silently overwrites a later, deliberate colour commit, and can mutate the global model after the component is destroyed.

**Mechanism.** A hidden timer owns pending state with no lifetime binding; combined with round 1's C-8 (the debounce is an app-wide singleton), the only `.cancel()` in the application belongs to ColorPicker's lifetime — so this component's pending parse is cancelled by the wrong unmount and by nothing else.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:92 (`debounce(parseAndSetColor, 2000)`); demo/shared/utils.ts:36-41 (`.cancel()` exists); `grep -rn onUnmounted demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue` → no matches; the sibling consumer DOES cancel at demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:383. Measured with real timers: `C1 committed #abcdef` → `C2 after committing #00ff00 color=rgb(0 255 0)` → `C3 2.3s later, nothing touched color=rgb(255 0 0)`. Unmount path: demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:153 `v-if="hasAnyActionBar"` and :156 `v-if="actionBar"`.
```

**Reproduction.** npx vite-node --config vite.config.ts <scratchpad>/parseprobe2.ts — scenario C. In the app: type a colour into the dock input, blur without committing, immediately pick a different colour by slider/swatch; ~2 s later the colour reverts to the abandoned text.

**Proposed cure.** Give the pending commit the component's lifetime and make it visible reactive state rather than a hidden timer: fold the debounce into the draft `shallowRef` of R2-1, cancel on every path that resolves the edit, and add `onBeforeUnmount`. Do not merely add a cancel call — the singleton ownership (C-8) is the same defect seen from the other side.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shell/dock/Acti` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Hand-rolled GlassDock keep-open token is unbalanced in both directions: tokens leak (never released on unmount or on the prop-driven close path) and tokens are released without ever having been acquired. Reimplements glass-ui 7.0.0's `keepDockOpen` Popover prop, badly.

**Mechanism.** refcount protocol reimplemented in a leaf component without the producer's two guards (idempotency flag + scope-dispose release), and keyed off an event that the producer only emits for internally-initiated state changes, so the prop-driven close path never reaches release()

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/ActionButton.vue:55,57,81-88 (no onUnmounted/onScopeDispose anywhere in the 137-line file). Producer primitive: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/popover/Popover.vue.d.ts:16 `keepDockOpen?: boolean` — "Hold an ancestor GlassDock open while this surface is visible"; dockContext.d.ts documents the idiom verbatim: "Hover-driven dock popovers compose <Popover trigger=\"hover\" keep-dock-open>". Producer impl (dist/popover-BQGYXZyO.js) watches the RESOLVED open computed, guards with a held flag, and calls onScopeDispose(release). `grep -rn "keep-dock-open|keepDockOpen" demo/` => no output. LEAK measured (counter read via the dock context provides table): [["A baseline",{"count":0}],["E hovered \"Reset\"",{"count":1,"states":["Reset=open",...],"popovers":["Reset"]}],["F second unmount-while-hovered",{"count":2,"states":["Reset=closed","Copy CSS=closed","Seed from palette=closed"],"popovers":[]}]] — count 2 with everything closed and the mouse parked off-dock 2.5s. OVER-RELEASE measured: [["baseline count",1],["after focus",{"count":1,"state":"closed"}],["after Enter",{"count":1,"state":"closed"}],["after blur +1.5s",{"count":0}]] — release() fired for a cycle with no keepOpen(). Consequence from dist/dock.js: the collapse timer, mouseleave, and document-pointerdown handlers each `if (keepOpenCount.value > 0) return`. Control at 1600x1000 (where Dock.vue:132 `:always-expanded="!isDesktop"` is off): count 0 => dock collapses on schedule (["C CONTROL: mouse away 7.5s",{"count":0,"dock":"collapsed"}]).
```

**Reproduction.** Park mouse at (2,2); goto http://localhost:9000/#/gradient; install the counter probe by walking el.__vueParentComponent.provides for Symbol(glass-ui:dock-context); hover a GenericActionBar ActionButton until its popover opens (count => 1); `location.hash = '#/mix'` (swaps the actions array, unmounting the hovered button); move mouse back to (2,2); wait 2.5s; read count => 2 with all data-state=closed and no popover content.

**Proposed cure.** Delete lines 55, 57 and the dock branches at 83-87 entirely; write `<Popover trigger="hover" keep-dock-open :open="isOpen" @update:open="onHoverOpenChange" …>` and reduce onHoverOpenChange to `emit("update:activeHover", v ? hoverKey : null)`. The producer then owns acquisition, idempotency, prop-driven closes and disposal. Architectural transposition: the hold protocol belongs to the design system, not a leaf button (edict 4 enforcing edict 1).
