### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shell/dock/Colo` · R3-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The custom-name round-trip is broken: `formattedCurrentColor` is a name-or-CSS union, and the component writes it into the contenteditable at five sites and reads it back into `parseAndSetColor` at three. Approved custom names are never registered with the parser, so the app's own canonical display text fails the app's own parser.

**Mechanism.** type-confused single value — one computed serves both 'label a human reads' and 'value a machine round-trips', so the DOM node that is the source of truth for submission is seeded with a value from the wrong domain

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-session/useColorNameResolution.ts:31-46 returns `findCustomName(...)` (an arbitrary user-proposed name) before ever reaching `serializePickerColor`. demo/color-session/useCustomColorNames.ts:61-66 resolves against a demo-side Map built from GET /colors/approved; `grep -rn registerColorNames src/ demo/ api/src` yields ONE hit, a comment at useCustomColorNames.ts:46. The parser's only name table is the frozen 148-entry NAMED_COLORS (src/css/grammar.ts:31,265; src/css/named-colors.ts:1). Writers: ColorInput.vue:191, :240, :265, :272, :278. Readers: :199, :208, :215. Measured: `model colour: rgb(20 60 200) / formattedCurrentColor: "babb-blue" / parseCssColor(displayed).ok: false / after re-submitting the displayed text -> parseError = true / model colour now: rgb(20 60 200)`.
```

**Reproduction.** VITE_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9/api npx vitest run --config docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-colorinput/probe.vitest.config.ts — test B in roundtrip.probe.ts. Drives the real useCustomColorNames + useColorNameResolution + useColorParsing; only globalThis.fetch is stubbed, and the stub name `babb-blue` is legal under the server's own zod schema (api/src/modules/color/schema.ts:8-19).

**Proposed cure.** Split the union at the pipeline, not with a guard at the call site. Expose `canonicalCssColor` (always serializePickerColor) alongside `displayLabel`; render the label, seed and submit the canonical. The custom name then becomes what it always should have been — presentation, exactly like the crown tooltip beside it. This also collapses R2-1 and C-16: with one canonical string source there is no reason for six imperative innerText writers or for blur to rewrite a node a pending click is about to read.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shell/dock/Colo` · R3-MT-F001 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** MT-F001 is SWALLOWED by this path and mislabelled as a user typo. A shipped-library TypeError is rendered byte-identically to a plain typo, reaches no telemetry, and leaves the field in a final state indistinguishable from working.

**Mechanism.** an undiscriminated catch converting a defect in a dependency into an accusation of user error, with a latch that then erases even that signal

**Evidence.**

```
Library leg re-measured against src/css/index: `"oklch()" "rgb()" "hsl()" "lab()" "lch()" "color()" "oklab()" "hsl(  )" -> THROW TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')`. Site: src/css/grammar.ts:178 guards `slash[1]?.trim()` with optional chaining while :180 asserts `slash[0]!.replace(...)` — the two adjacent indices of the same array handled with opposite rigour, one line apart. Path: ColorInput.vue:194 -> :199 -> useColorParsing.ts:60 -> :64 -> picker-color.ts:110 -> parseCssColor. Live (frames/probe-1.json B-f001-light): afterEnter badgeText 'not a valid color', inputBorder rgb(219,36,36), and pageErrors: []. Swallow site: useColorParsing.ts:84-87, a bare `catch` with no binding and no discrimination, so PickerColorError (which carries result.diagnostics per picker-color.ts:96-112) and a library TypeError render identically.
```

**Reproduction.** Test A in roundtrip.probe.ts for the library leg; frames/probe-1.json + frames/B-f001-error.png + frames/B-f001-after2s.png for the live leg. The tail nobody had recorded: after2s = {badge:false, text:'oklch()', border:'lab(92 88.8 20 / 0.827)'} — the invalid text remains, the error styling is gone, and previousInvalid is now latched to 'oklch()' so useColorParsing.ts:61 short-circuits and pressing Enter again produces nothing at all.

**Proposed cure.** Narrow the catch: `catch (e) { if (!(e instanceof PickerColorError)) throw e; ... }`. A genuine syntax rejection stays a quiet inline error; anything else reaches window.onerror, where MT-F001 would have surfaced on day one. ParseEchoReadout (ColorInput.vue:109) — already rendering astEcho and gamutVerdict from the same pipeline — is the natural home for the diagnostics the catch discards. The library-side `!` at src/css/grammar.ts:180 is a separate repair; route to the library seat, together with R2-7's adjacent false-accept of `oklch(0.5 0.1 250 / )`.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shell/dock/Colo` · R2-1-UPHELD · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** CARRIED AND STRENGTHENED — the send button is structurally incapable of submitting typed text, in every browser engine. I attempted to refute this as a Chromium-only focus artefact and the refutation FAILED.

**Mechanism.** DOM node as source of truth, mutated by an event that the UA guarantees fires before the event that reads it

**Evidence.**

```
ColorInput.vue:183-193 onInputBlur overwrites the field with formattedCurrentColor; :213-217 onSubmitColor reads that same node back. Cross-engine test of the exact three-part shape: chromium 148.0.7778.96 / webkit 26.4 / firefox 150.0.2 all produced `typed activeEl=ce` -> `mousedown activeEl=ce` -> `BLUR read="typed-value" -> overwrite` -> `CLICK read="CANONICAL"`. WebKit and Firefox indeed do not focus the button on mousedown, but they blur the contenteditable anyway — the distinction the refutation relied on does not exist for this shape.
```

**Reproduction.** scratchpad/blurorder.html + blurorder.mjs (session scratchpad; a 12-line static page, no app dependency). `node scratchpad/blurorder.mjs`. Round 2's live app measurement stands as the in-situ leg.

**Proposed cure.** Same cure as R3-1 and C-16, one stroke: hold the draft in a local shallowRef written by @input, render from it, and let blur decide only whether to DISCARD the draft — never to rewrite a DOM node a pending click is about to read. onSubmitColor then reads the ref and the blur/click ordering becomes irrelevant. This is the synchronous-local-cache idiom edict 7 already mandates for the defineModel round-trip; the hazard class is identical.

MOBILE 390x844:   clipboard="SENTINEL-NOT-TOUCHED"                                          pageErrors=[]
DESKTOP 1440x900: clipboard="linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(75% 0.15 145deg) 0.00%, oklch(7…" pageErrors=[]

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · R3-02 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** No cancel path exists, and a 2000 ms commit debounce means valid input typed and blurred inside two seconds is silently discarded with zero signal.

**Mechanism.** Two sources of truth (contenteditable text vs. model) reconciled only by a long debounce and an unconditional blur repaint, with no cancel gesture and no uncommitted-state affordance.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:92 `debounce(parseAndSetColor, 2000)`; ColorInput.vue:202-211 handles only `Enter`; :183-193 blur repaints from the model. ```

**Reproduction.** Open the field -> select all -> type `rebeccapurple` (valid CSS) -> press Escape (nothing happens) -> click elsewhere within 2 s. The value reverts to the previous colour with no error, no toast, no 'unsaved' mark.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The component hand-applies GlassDock's PRIVATE shell-pane classes (`.dock-layer` + `is-active`/`is-leaving`) to arbitrary consumer components. In Glass 7 the public face class is `.dock-face`; `.dock-layer` is emitted only by GlassDock's own two internal plates. Because every `.dock-layer` rule is scoped `:where(.glass-dock, .dock-layer-group) .dock-layer`, the counterfeit faces match the dock's private plate rules — including two that are actively hostile during a dock morph.

**Mechanism.** consumer styles itself from producer internals — a silent breakage contract, since no public API ever promised these class names

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:91. Scan of the producer bundle: `python3 -c "...re.finditer(r'dock-layer(?![-a-z])', open('dist/dock.js').read())..."` returns exactly two emission sites, both internal: `class: L(["dock-layer dock-layer--full", {...}])` and `class: L(["dock-layer dock-layer--summary", {...}])`. The public face component emits `class: L(["dock-face", { "is-active": ..., "is-le..." }])`. Hostile rules in layers.css: `.glass-dock[data-morphing] .dock-layer.is-leaving { opacity: calc(1 - var(--dock-morph-t)); }` and `.glass-dock[data-morphing] .dock-layer.is-active > * { opacity: var(--child-reveal); scale: calc(0.82 + 0.18 * var(--child-reveal)); }`.
```

**Reproduction.** grep the emission sites as above; then on the live page confirm the consumer nodes carry the class: the two `.dock-layer-grid` children report className `"flex items-center justify-around flex-1 dock-layer is-active"` and `"grid grid-cols-1 gap-y-2 p-0 m-0 dock-layer min-w-0"`. (The compound swap-during-dock-morph symptom is a HYPOTHESIS — the rules and the class match are both confirmed, but I did not capture a simultaneous frame.)

**Proposed cure.** Same transposition as D-1 — `<DockLayer>` faces inside `<DockCrossfade>` carry the producer's own `.dock-face` packaging, so the consumer stops naming producer internals at all.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-3 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The component's central mechanism is a fiction: the local `useLayerTransition` schedules a 260ms crossfade window for a crossfade that never runs. The sub-layer swap is a hard cut.

**Mechanism.** `ActionBarLayer.vue:53–94` reimplements a two-ref `currentLayer`/`leavingLayer` contract whose CSS counterpart was never a CSS opacity transition. `SUB_LAYER_CROSSFADE_MS = 260` (`:62`) buys only a 260ms delay before `visibility: hidden`.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The dock auto-collapses out from under the user mid-edit after 5 seconds of idle, expelling focus and discarding the typed slug.

**Mechanism.** A text-entry surface hosted inside an idle-collapsing container that never registers itself as a keep-open driver. The authors wrote a cleanup watcher for the collapse (`Dock.vue:76`) instead of a hold — i.e. the collapse was known and the data loss was not.

**Evidence.**

```
`demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:86` — `shouldKeepOpen = actionBarLayerActive || anyEditActive || isAnyOpen`; `slugEditMode` is NOT a driver. `Dock.vue:132` `:collapse-delay="5000"`. Measured (slug-probe6): `t=4000ms {slugFaceActive:true, faceOpacity:"1", groupW:285}` → `t=6000ms {slugFaceActive:false, faceOpacity:"0", groupW:56, sealVisible:true}` with `value:"brave-swift-red-fox"` still in the detached DOM. Inactive faces measure `{inert:true, ariaHidden:"true"}`, so focus is expelled. `Dock.vue:76` then clears `slugEditMode`; re-opening runs `SlugEditLayer.vue:16-17` whose first statement is `slugInput.value = ""`.
```

**Reproduction.** 1440x900 → `Login` → type `brave-swift-red-fox` → move the pointer away from the dock → wait. Between 4s and 6s the dock collapses to the 56px wax seal; the input is gone and the value is discarded on re-open. Desktop only (`always-expanded="!isDesktop"` exempts mobile; measured 8s idle at 390/320 leaves it intact).

**Proposed cure.** The producer already exposes the right primitive — GlassDock's ref-counted `keepOpen()/release()` pair, which `Dock.vue:87` already drives. Add `slugEditMode` to the `shouldKeepOpen` disjunction at `Dock.vue:86`. One word. (Moot under the gestalt cure — a Dialog does not evaporate on a wall-clock timer.)

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The failure-explicit Result contract is destroyed at the demo boundary, so a LIBRARY CRASH and a USER TYPO are the same event. src/css/grammar.ts:181 throws TypeError on eight inputs; demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:109-113 is a throwing facade that only handles `result.ok === false` and lets the raw TypeError escape past its own typed PickerColorError; demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:80-85 catches everything with a bare `catch {}` and renders the hardcoded literal 'not a valid color'. Re-derived and confirmed this pass; first filed by the prior pass.

**Mechanism.** Contract transposition, three hops, each lossy: Result → exception (picker-color.ts valueOrThrow/PickerColorError) → bare catch {} (useColorParsing) → a constant string literal (ColorInput.vue:88). The discriminant is erased at every hop. Two further silencers compound it: `initialParse` (useColorParsing.ts:83) suppresses a composable's first failure, and `previousInvalid` (useColorParsing.ts:62) makes any REPEAT of the same string a total no-op — the state a frustrated user reaches within two seconds.

**Evidence.**

```
Contract: src/css/types.ts:25-27 (`ParseResult<T> = {ok:true,...} | {ok:false, diagnostics:[ParseIssue,...]}`), package.json:4 ('failure-explicit'). Throw site: src/css/grammar.ts:181 `splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(/,/g," "), "space")` where splitTopLevel("","/") returns [] (grammar.ts:79,85). Measured against the exact dist the dev server serves (dist/subpaths/css.js, Jul 24 14:04, newer than src/css/grammar.ts Jul 17 14:48): all of oklch() rgb() hsl() lab() lch() color() oklab() 'hsl(  )' THROW `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')`, while 'oklch(' and 'notacolor' correctly return ok:false. Live at http://localhost:9000/#/ after typing oklch()+Enter: {"inputText":"oklch()","errorBadge":null,"borderColor":"lab(92 88.8 20 / 0.827)"} and browser_console_messages(level=error) → Errors: 0. Diagnostics loss is total: ParseIssue carries {code,start,end,expected,actual} (src/css/types.ts:10-24) and the only three demo readers of `.diagnostics` are internal-invariant sites with no human present (useGradientCSS.ts:128, useImageSampler.ts:60, useMarkdownColors.ts:33); the one surface where a human types CSS reads it never.
```

**Reproduction.** `npx vitest run --config docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-colorinput/probe.vitest.config.ts` → 5/5 green. The harness drives the REAL useColorParsing composable and the REAL picker-color facade against the PUBLISHED dist/subpaths/{color,css}.js and proves: (1) all eight throw while 'oklch(' returns ok:false — the crash is narrower than the failure path and therefore invisible beside it; (2) parsePickerColor re-throws a raw TypeError, not PickerColorError; (3) with the initialParse gate burned, all eight leave the model object-identical (toBe) and set the same boolean a typo sets; (4) the first parse of a composable's life leaves parseError===false; (5) a repeat of the same crasher early-returns on previousInvalid — no badge, no console, no model change. Live: the gesture chain above.

**Proposed cure.** Delete valueOrThrow and PickerColorError from picker-color.ts and every bare catch on the parse path. parseCssColor already returns the right shape — let it reach the component: `parsePickerColor(s): ParseResult<CssColor>`; `useColorParsing.commit(source)` returns it; ColorInput renders `diagnostics[0].expected` and marks [start,end] in the field. No try, no catch, no previousInvalid cache. An unexpected TypeError then has nowhere to hide — it becomes a page error the existing visual-audit harness already reports, so 'pageErrors — 0' becomes a real green instead of a manufactured one.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-30 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** A failed login is completely silent: the slug-edit layer closes as if it succeeded, and there are three independent, redundant reasons no error can reach the user. (1) `SlugEditLayer.vue:54` calls `pm.onSlugSwitch(...)` with no `await` inside a `try`, while `useSlugMigration.ts:51` declares it `async` — the `catch` at :57 is unreachable, and :55-56 close the layer synchronously before the network call resolves. (2) It would not matter: the callee catches everything itself (`useSlugMigration.ts:74-88`) and dispatches onto `slugBarRef.value?.setError(...)`, a permanently-null ref. (3) `slugError` is written at six sites in SlugEditLayer and rendered at zero — the template contains no reference to it. And the substring branches at :59-62 are a verbatim resurrection of the exact bug `useSlugMigration.ts:77-82` records as killed at S.W2 W2-6 (`ApiProblem` does `super(title)`, so `e.message` is the server title and can never contain '409'/'404'/'429').

**Mechanism.** error channel swallowed three ways: un-awaited async across a component boundary; callee catches into a null instance ref; error state with no template binding — plus a condemned string-sniff re-authored after its cure was recorded

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:54 (un-awaited) · :57 (catch) · :59-62 (substring sniff) · :13,18,43,49,59-62 (slugError writes) · `sed -n '74,119p' SlugEditLayer.vue | grep slugError` → no output (never rendered). demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:51 (`async function onSlugSwitch`) · :77-82 (the S.W2 W2-6 ruling comment) · :84-87 (correct typed path, dispatched into null). demo/platform/transport/api-problem.ts:22-33 (`super(title)`). LIVE REPRODUCTION (LDOCK-probe6.mjs, WebKit 1440x900, http://localhost:9000): after filling 'aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd' and clicking button[aria-label="Switch to slug"] — `[after submit] inputValue:"" layerInert:true layerAriaHidden:"true" errorish:[]`, dock still shows 'Login', console tail contains only the two boot lines, no error from the login attempt.
```

**Reproduction.** node LDOCK-probe6.mjs (scratchpad) against the live dev server at http://localhost:9000 — open the dock Login button, fill the slug input, submit; observe layer closes inert+aria-hidden, input cleared, zero error text anywhere in the DOM (`errorish: []`), clean console. The dev server's API is deliberately misconfigured (its own status lamp reads 'dev misconfigured'), so the attempt is guaranteed to fail.

**Proposed cure.** `onSlugSwitch` returns its outcome (`Promise<Result<void, ApiProblem>>`) instead of dispatching it onto a component instance; the layer awaits and renders the failure. One contract change removes all three swallows at once — awaiting makes it observable, returning kills the instance-ref channel, rendering kills the dead state. Rides L-6/L-24's move of the session port to `demo/platform/auth/`, so the login surface becomes a function with a typed result rather than a feature-owned side effect.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure: module boundaries, ownershi` · L-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The action ActionButton fires is a three-hop optional-chained dispatch through `Ref<any>` owned by the shell router, and it is structurally dead on the mobile layout: the mobile <PaneSlot> binds no :on-mount, so all three pane refs stay null. All nine generic dock actions are silent no-ops on phones while the button still plays its 400ms success animation.

**Mechanism.** Inverted ownership direction — a pane's own verbs are declared in the shell router, keyed by string, and dispatched onto the pane through a layout-specific template-ref capture. The capability becomes a function of which PaneSlot rendered the component, and every hop is an untyped `?.` that silently no-ops.

**Evidence.**

```
Chain: ActionButton.vue:98 `emit("action")` -> GenericActionBar.vue:28 `@action="act.handler()"` -> demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:196-222 e.g. :208 `handler: () => paneRefs.gradient.value?.reset?.()` -> demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientPane.vue:12 `reset: () => visualizerRef.value?.resetGradient?.()`. Untyped: usePaneRouter.ts:106-110 `generate: Ref<any>; gradient: Ref<any>; mix: Ref<any>`; App.vue:317-319 `ref<any>(null)`; eslint.config.js:70,184 `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any: off`. Layout asymmetry: demo/color-picker/App.vue:83-91 (mobile PaneSlot — NO :on-mount) vs :105 `:on-mount="onDesktopLeftMount"` and :131 `:on-mount="onDesktopRightMount"`; App.vue:315 comment 'Populated by the onMount callbacks on the desktop PaneSlots'. LIVE MEASUREMENT at 390x844 on #/gradient reading the App instance setupState: {"innerWidth":390,"innerHeight":844,"mq":false,"isDesktopSetup":false,"gradientPaneRef":"null","dockActionButtons":3}. Confirmation animation fires regardless: ActionButton.vue:92-99 sets isClicked for 400ms unconditionally.
```

**Reproduction.** 1) viewport 390x844. 2) navigate http://localhost:9000/#/gradient and reload; wait 5s. 3) evaluate: walk .glass-dock __vueParentComponent up to the App instance, read setupState.gradientPaneRef (unwrapping refs) -> null; matchMedia('(min-width: 1024px) and (min-aspect-ratio: 1.1)').matches -> false; document.querySelectorAll('button.action-button-wrapper').length -> 3. 4) open Tools and click Reset/Copy CSS/Seed — handler evaluates `null?.reset?.()`, nothing happens, no console error, icon still animates.

**Proposed cure.** Invert the dependency: add `demo/shell/dock/dockActions.ts` exporting a typed `DockAction { key, icon, title, description, rotateOnClick?, iconClass?, disabled?, active?, run: () => void }` plus `DOCK_ACTIONS_KEY` and `provideDockActions()`. Each pane calls provideDockActions([...]) in its own setup, closing over its own local functions — fully typed, no refs, no `any`, no `?.`, layout-independent. Delete PaneActionRefs, the three Ref<any>, the 27 lines of handler literals in usePaneRouter, both onDesktop*Mount callbacks in App.vue, and the pure-forwarding defineExpose shims in GeneratePane/GradientPane. The mobile/desktop asymmetry is then inexpressible.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The magnifier loupe renders blank on every first show and stays permanently blank on the touch path. `showLoupeAt` flips `loupeVisible` and calls `drawLoupe` in the same synchronous tick, but the canvas is behind `v-if="loupe.loupeVisible.value"`, so `loupeCanvasRef.value` is still null and the draw is silently skipped. **Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/composables/useLoupeCanvas.ts:55-60 (showLoupeAt) and :27-30 (drawLoupe early return); ImageEyedropper.vue:78-86 (v-if + canvas). MEASURED (probe2 §A): A_pinned {loupeVisible:true, loupeNonZeroPx:9604, di110:2} → Escape → A_tapNoHover {loupeVisible:true, loupeNonZeroPx:0, di110:2} → A_afterOneMove {loupeNonZeroPx:0, di110:2}. Independent replication (probe4): {"pointermoves":40,"getImageDataCalls":40,"loupeDraws":39} — the missing draw is the first. Visual: .playwright-mcp/eyedropper-live.png shows an empty green-ringed circle.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/extract → upload any image → click the preview to open the eyedropper → tap once WITHOUT moving the pointer first (i.e. any touch tap). The loupe appears and is empty; it never fills. Scripted: .playwright-mcp/probe2.js section A.

**Proposed cure.** Keep the loupe canvas permanently mounted and gate visibility on opacity/visibility instead of v-if. This kills the race by construction, lets the already-declared `.loupe { transition: opacity }` (ImageEyedropper.vue:270 — currently dead CSS) actually run, and removes a DOM create/destroy from the hover path. (`await nextTick()` before drawLoupe is the patch, not the cure.)

**Defect.** `justUnpinned` is a component-scope latch whose only exit is inside `onTap`; a drag never reaches `onTap`, so after pin → press-drag → release the flag stays true and the NEXT legitimate tap is silently swallowed.

```
ImageEyedropper.vue:123 (`let justUnpinned = false`), :151-155 (onTap's only clear), :176-185 (capture-phase pointerdown sets it); useInertiaGesture.ts:277-281 (onTap fires only when !hasMoved). ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches` · C1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Dragging (or shift+arrow nudging) a handle past a neighbour leaves `stops` non-monotonic: the rail's ramp positions descend so CSS clamps them into a flat band, the easing intervals now straddle inverted pairs, and the serialized CSS is refused by the app's own parser — the atomic round-trip contract is one-way only.

**Mechanism.** Sortedness is enforced on insert and merely coincidental on update — the position write is a raw array map, so an invariant the rest of the system depends on has no owner.

**Evidence.**

```
Live: after adding a stop at 50% and dragging the 0% handle right, DOM/model order = ["Gradient stop at 75%","Gradient stop at 50%","Gradient stop at 100%"]; editor text = `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 74.9%, oklch(70% 0.165 205deg) 50%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)`; rail background-image head = `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 74.9%, oklch(0.746875 0.150937 148.75) 73.34%, oklch(0.74375 0.151875 152.5) 71.79%, …)` (descending). `npx vite-node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence/parse-probe.ts` → `parseGradientCSS -> reject: stop positions must be non-decreasing (hard-stop reordering isn't modeled)` on that exact string. Code: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientModel.ts:127-131 (updateStop never sorts) vs :118 (addStop does); emit sites GradientStopEditor.vue:145 and :179; guard-on-input at demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/gradientParse.ts:284-290.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000 → dock → Gradient → click the rail at 50% → drag the 0% handle to ~75% → read the CSS box and the rail's computed background-image; paste that CSS back into the editor and the app rejects it.

**Proposed cure.** Make ordering a property of the operation, not of the array: one model action `setStopPosition(id, pos)` that maps then sorts, so sortedness is total by construction, paired with C2's identity-keyed intervals so the re-sort cannot scramble easing. Clamping the drag to (prev, next) is cheaper and strictly worse — it makes stops un-reorderable.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches` · C2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Easing intervals are keyed by array INDEX and synced by a length watcher that appends/truncates at the TAIL, while addStop inserts in sorted position — so inserting a stop silently moves the user's authored curve onto a different pair of stops and reverts the authored segment to linear.

**Mechanism.** An adjacency relation (which pair of stops a curve belongs to) is modelled as a positional array, and the sync watcher observes only `stops.length`, so it cannot know where the stop landed and always guesses 'at the end'.

**Evidence.**

```
Live: stops [0,50,100] with `steps(4, jump-end)` authored on segment 50→100 → readouts ["cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)","steps(4, jump-end)"], heads ["1 → 2linear","2 → 3steps"]. After clicking the rail at 25%: labels [0%,25%,50%,100%], readouts ["cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)","steps(4, jump-end)","cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)"], heads ["1 → 2linear","2 → 3steps","3 → 4linear"] — steps now governs 25→50; the authored 50→100 curve is gone. Code: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientModel.ts:89-100.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000 → Gradient → click the rail at 50% → open interval row 2 → click the `steps` specimen → click the rail at 25% → read `.readout-rail code` and `.interval-head` text.

**Proposed cure.** Hang the interval on the stop that OPENS it — `GradientStop { id, cssColor, position, easing }` (last stop's easing ignored) — so the curve travels with its own stop through any insert/remove/sort. That deletes the parallel array, the sync watcher, and all three `Gradient interval N is missing` throws (useGradientCSS.ts:189/240, GradientVisualizer.vue:77). Alternative: a Map keyed by the ordered stop-id pair.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches` · C-01 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** All three `back`-family specimen tiles crash the entire Gradient workbench on a single press. The catalogue mints overshoot curves whose eased progress leaves [0,1]; the gradient's color-mix contract rejects that, and the demo demotes the library's Result-err into an uncaught throw inside a computed on the render path, so the pane's error boundary swallows the whole bench (easing bench, gradient rail, CSS output, stop editor).

**Mechanism.** Domain contract violated across a module boundary, with a Result->throw demotion at the seam: the easing catalogue's codomain is R, the gradient sampler's domain is [0,1], nothing reconciles them, and the one mechanism that could report it politely (the Result) is discarded.

**Evidence.**

```
Live pane body after the click: "This panel hit an unexpected error. / Gradient color mix failed: color_progress_out_of_range". Measured fn ranges over t in [0,1] (65 samples, through the gradient's own easingFnOf): ease-in-back cubic-bezier(0.6,-0.28,0.735,0.045) fn(0.5)=-0.0636 min=-0.0969; ease-out-back cubic-bezier(0.175,0.885,0.32,1.275) fn(0.5)=1.0676 max=1.0868; ease-in-out-back cubic-bezier(0.68,-0.55,0.265,1.55) min=-0.0926 max=1.0927. No other tile leaves [0,1]. Direct invocation in-page: interpolateStopColors(c0,c1,fnIB(0.5),'oklch','shorter') -> "Gradient color mix failed: color_progress_out_of_range"; serializeCoalescedGradient(model with that css) -> same. Sites: src/color/operations.ts:65 (returns err, correct); demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientInterpolation.ts:37 (throws); demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:207 (throws); demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/useSpecimenRows.ts:53-59 (the throw inside a computed); easingCatalogue.ts:176-190 (mints the back tiles unguarded). The strip's own CSS comment at EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:172-179 explicitly renders headroom for these overshoot curves.
```

**Reproduction.** Fresh http://localhost:9000/#/gradient (default two-stop gradient, Easing row 1 open). Click [data-specimen="ease-in-out-expo"] -> OK, readout cubic-bezier(1, 0, 0, 1). Click [data-specimen="ease-out-circ"] -> OK, readout cubic-bezier(0.075, 0.82, 0.165, 1). Click [data-specimen="ease-in-back"] -> pane replaced by the error boundary. ease-in-out-back reproduces independently.

**Proposed cure.** Make the gradient's progress type TOTAL, once, at the ramp sampler — not in the catalogue and not as a try/catch. Introduce the [0,1] clamp at the single point where an eased t becomes a mix progress (useGradientCSS.easingFnOf's return, or a rampProgress(fn,t) helper beside it) so useSpecimenRows, serializeIntervalRamp and serializeCoalescedGradient all inherit it; this is the correct CSS-gradient semantic (an interval cannot produce a color beyond its endpoints, so overshoot MEANS hold-at-endpoint), a domain law rather than a masking fallback, and the repo already speaks the idiom (test/value-domain-clamp.test.ts). Then delete both throw sites (useGradientInterpolation.ts:37, useGradientCSS.ts:207) — with a total domain they are unreachable, and an unreachable throw on a render path is a liability. Deleting the back family instead is strictly worse: it removes curves the producer's own picker still offers and contradicts the strip's overshoot-headroom design.

Unclamped call sites: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:199-208 (sampleCoalescedStops), demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/useSpecimenRows.ts:52-59 (fn(0.5)), demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer.vue:78-85 (colorAtPosition). Measured ranges on the real sampling grid (vite-node against src/subpaths/easing): ease-in-back min=-0.0969 out-of-range 18/33 fn(0.5)=-0.0636; ease-out-back max=1.0868 out-of-range 19/33 fn(0.5)=1.0676; ease-in-out-back min=-0.0923 max=1.0927 out-of-range 21/33. Drag repro: `AFTER DRAG: {"literal":null,"crash":["...color_progress_out_of_range..."]}`. Catalogue built by blind enumeration: easingCatalogue.ts:178 `for (const name of Object.keys(bezierPresets))` with no compatibility filter; GradientEasingEditor.vue:73-76 emits with no validation.
```

**Reproduction.** 1. open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient (easing row `1 → 2` is open on arrival). 2. click the `back` family's `out` tile (`[data-specimen='ease-out-back']`). 3. the entire pane is replaced by the ErrorBoundary reading "This panel hit an unexpected error. Gradient color mix failed: color_progress_out_of_range". Scripted: node scratchpad/wbge-probe4.mjs ease-out-back ease-in-back ease-in-out-back. Recoverable via "Try again" (probe 7: crash 1 → 0, heads back to 1) but all pane state is lost.

**Proposed cure.** Progress into a color mix is a ratio on [0,1] and the sampling law is the ONE place that owns it. Add a private `rampProgress = (t) => Math.min(1, Math.max(0, t))` in useGradientCSS and route sampleCoalescedStops' easedT, useSpecimenRows' fn(0.5) and colorAtPosition's easedT through it — matching CSS's own behaviour (an overshoot timing function on a <color> interpolation clamps to the endpoint colour). The overshoot stays visible where it belongs: in the glyph, which samples the raw callable and needs no clamp, and in the authoring canvas. Do NOT delete the back family — the curves are legitimate and the picker authors them freely; the defect is the missing domain boundary, not the curves.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt: demo/workbenches/g` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The component's own stated "zero letterbox" law (O-17 clause 1) is dead code against glass-ui 7.0.0: the picker renders `svg[role="group"]`, not `role="img"`, so `syncVbRatio` no-ops forever and all three `:deep(svg[role="img"])` declarations select nothing. 59.4% of the authoring canvas renders nothing.

**Mechanism.** brittle-producer-dom-coupling: a consumer reaches into a producer's private DOM (an ARIA role attribute) to correct the producer's geometry, and hand-rolls a rAF mirror of state the producer already owns. The glass-ui 7.0.0 adopt changed the role; the coupling failed open and silent.

**Evidence.**

```
EasingAuthoringStage.vue:47-53 queries `svg[role='img']`; :104-115 styles `:deep(svg[role="img"])` with !important. Measured live DOM (probe 5, #easing-authoring-0): `{"svgs":[{"role":"group","aria":"Easing curve 1 → 2","viewBox":"0 -0.1 1 1.2000000000000002","box":{"w":410,"h":200}}],"stageStyleAttr":"--vb-ratio: 1.2;"}` — role is "group". Measured geometry via the oracle's own getScreenCTM method (probe 6): `{"elementBox":{"w":410,"h":200},"drawnPlot":{"w":166.7,"h":200},"letterbox":{"left":121.7,"right":121.7,"top":0,"bottom":0},"vbRatioVar":"1.2","svgComputed":{"aspectRatio":"1 / 1","blockSize":"200px"}}` — computed aspect-ratio is the PRODUCER's inline `1 / 1`, not the seat's `calc(1/1.2)`; block-size is the producer's 200px clamp, not the seat's `auto`. O-17 requires ≤1px on all four edges; measured 121.7px on two. Laws 1 and 2 DO still hold (gridCols "436px", cardShadow "none", cardBackdrop "none") — only the role-keyed law broke, and it broke with no console error, no type error, no exception.
```

**Reproduction.** 1. open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient. 2. press the sliders icon in the readout rail (`aria-label="Author a custom curve"`). 3. inspect `#easing-authoring-0 svg` — role="group", inline style `aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; block-size: clamp(200px, 38cqi, 320px)`. 4. its viewBox is 1×1.2 with preserveAspectRatio=xMidYMid meet in a 410×200 box → drawn plot 166.7×200 centred, 121.7px dead on each side. Scripted: node scratchpad/wbge-probe5.mjs and wbge-probe6.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** Retire the seat override entirely and take the geometry from glass-ui: the picker should expose its live viewBox ratio as a custom property on its own root (a `--easing-vb-ratio` alongside the `--easing-curve-accent` it already stamps, observed in the live DOM) and size its canvas from it. The component header already books this — "the overrides retire at the P7 adopt" — and the adopt has landed (@mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0 installed, W44 closed); this is the glass-ui-first edict, the fix belongs upstream. If the producer packet cannot land now, the interim seat must not be able to break in silence: bind to the stable contract (`[data-testid="easing-picker"] svg[viewBox]`) AND make the miss loud — syncVbRatio should console.error on a failed query rather than `return`, so the next producer bump surfaces on first boot instead of in an audit two tranches later.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/workbenches/gr` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** An ordinary edit in the CSS box (`oklch()` — the state you get by selecting the channel values and pressing Delete) destroys the entire Gradient pane and silently reseeds the model to defaults.

**Mechanism.** `applyCSS` is documented model-or-reject but is not total: `parseGradientCSS`→`isColorToken`→`parseCssColor` throws on an empty colour function (src/css/grammar.ts:181 non-null assertion). The throw crosses an emitted-handler boundary, so Vue's callWithErrorHandling routes it to onErrorCaptured; the boundary unmounts the subtree. Because `useGradientModel()` is instantiated INSIDE the component (line 32), the model's lifetime is the view's lifetime — any throw is a data-loss event.

**Evidence.**

```
GradientVisualizer.vue:102-108 (`onParseCSS`, no try); demo/color-picker/App.vue:50 + ErrorBoundary.vue:59-69. Live run, pasted: {"step0":{"handles":2,"easingReadout":"cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)"},"afterMain":"This panel hit an unexpected error.\n\nCannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')\n\nTry again","handlesAfter":0,"verdict":null,"editorStillThere":false}. Headless: `npx vite-node probes/visualizer-probe.ts` → `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue) → THREW TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')` (same for rgb()/color()). Screenshot: evidence/gradient-pane-destroyed-by-oklch-empty.png shows the auto-recovered pane holding the DEFAULT gradient, not the user's.
```

**Reproduction.** goto http://localhost:9000/, wait 1.2s, set location.hash='#/gradient' in-page, wait for [role=textbox][aria-label='Gradient CSS'], select all its text, insertText 'linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)', dispatch input, wait 2000ms → main.innerText is the error card, 0 stop handles, no verdict.

**Proposed cure.** Two independent moves: (a) make the grammar total — return a failure for an empty component list in src/css/grammar.ts rather than asserting slash[0] (a try/catch in the pane would be a masking fallback, edict 2); (b) transpose the ownership — hoist `useGradientModel()` to a route-scoped provide ABOVE the ErrorBoundary so the model outlives its view and 'Try again' remounts a view over surviving state.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/workbenches/gr` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Adding or removing a stop anywhere but the end silently re-hosts every authored easing curve one slot to the left and drops the last one.

**Mechanism.** Intervals are a parallel array keyed by index and reconciled by length; an insert at index k shifts the meaning of every interval ≥ k without touching the array, and appends a fresh linear at the end. Remove truncates the tail, not the removed adjacency.

**Evidence.**

```
GradientVisualizer.vue:90-92 (`onAddStop`) and :143 (`@remove`) wire into useGradientModel.ts:89-100, a watcher keyed on `stops.value.length` alone. My run: `before: 0,50,100 → cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1) | steps(4, jump-end)` / `after: 0,25,50,100 → cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1) | steps(4, jump-end) | cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)` — 'interval that was 50→100 (steps) now covers: 25→50'.
```

**Reproduction.** npx vite-node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-visualizer/probes/visualizer-probe.ts → section P2. In the UI: author steps(4) on the second easing row, click the rail at 25% to add a stop, watch the steps curve jump to the first quarter and the second half revert to linear.

**Proposed cure.** Stop modelling an adjacency relation as a parallel array. Carry the outgoing curve on the stop that begins the interval (one array, no synchronisation possible), or key intervals by the id pair `${a.id}:${b.id}` so an insert must SPLIT an interval explicitly.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/ext` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The instrument lies: the preview <img> and the extracted palette + '% of the image' readout can describe two different images. `onFile` writes `lastFile` synchronously but writes `previewDataUrl` after an un-sequenced `await readAsDataUrl(file)` (FileReader completion is size-ordered, not call-ordered), then calls `runQuantize()` which re-reads `lastFile.value` at await-resume time. ```
demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useExtractSession.ts:164-168. **Defect.** Camera MediaStream leaks when the component unmounts while the permission prompt is open. `cameraStream = await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia(...)` assigns after the await; `onBeforeUnmount(stopCamera)` can only stop an already-assigned stream, so the promise resolves into a dead component's closure and the tracks are never stopped. Directly re-litigates the P051 abrogation that names Generate as an execute site.

**Mechanism.** F1 — producer contract drift: glass-ui 7.0.0 landed the P051 removal while the consumer still writes the 6.x interactive-host idiom; Vue discards the unknown prop silently, so no typecheck, console warning or unit test fires.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:199-208 passes `tag="button"` + `:aria-label` + `@click`. Producer prop set is `{color,variant?,animate?,cycleDuration?,range?,seed?}` (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts) — no `tag`. Render fn (dist/watercolor-dot.js): `o("span", {"aria-hidden":"true", ... style: u([f.value,{...pointerEvents:"none"...}])})`. Live measure on /#/generate: `{tagName:"SPAN", ariaHidden:"true", ariaLabel:null, tagAttr:null, role:null, tabIndex:-1, pointerEvents:"none", cursor:"pointer", rect:{w:40,h:40}}`; `hitTestAtDotCentre:{tag:"DIV", cls:"px-3 pb-1 flex flex-wrap gap-1.5", isTheDot:false}`; `swatchRowFocusable:0`. `grep -rn "generate-swatch" demo/ src/` returns only GenerateControls.vue:205, foundation.css:689, foundation.css:834 — no pointer-events override exists. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:91 and OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:108 both abrogate the `tag="button"` host and name Generate an execute site.
```

**Reproduction.** Dev server live at localhost:9000. Navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/generate, then in the page: `const d=document.querySelector('.generate-swatch'); const r=d.getBoundingClientRect(); document.elementFromPoint(r.x+r.width/2, r.y+r.height/2)` → returns the parent `DIV.px-3.pb-1.flex.flex-wrap.gap-1.5`, not the dot. `d.tagName` → "SPAN"; `d.getAttribute('aria-label')` → null; `d.tabIndex` → -1; `getComputedStyle(d).pointerEvents` → "none". Clicking any swatch in the UI copies nothing.

**Proposed cure.** Architectural, per the canon's own prescription (OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:108): the dot becomes a noninteractive face inside a NAMED GEOMETRIC SEAT — a native `<button type="button">` at >=44px carrying the accessible name, the focus ring and the click, with the untouched organic dot as its child. Structurally identical to the Gradient stop treatment already specified at VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:206. This single transposition restores the copy verb, the accessible name, the keyboard path and the tap floor at once. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 (RC-1, RC-2, RC-3).

demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:199-208 (tag="button", :aria-label, @click). Producer d.ts node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/*.d.ts declares only {color, variant, animate, cycleDuration, range, seed} — no `tag`. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The sampled color is not the color displayed under the cursor — stage, loupe and sampler use three different resampling rules over the same bitmap, and the displayed color additionally changes with devicePixelRatio while the sample does not.

**Mechanism.** useImageSampler.ts:111-119 sampleAt takes one nearest source texel via Math.floor((rx-panX)/zoom); the visible canvas (ImageEyedropper.vue:69-75) has no image-rendering declaration so the compositor smooths; useLoupeCanvas.ts:40 sets imageSmoothingEnabled=false. No single sampling model.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured composited pixels from probe/shot-desktop-light-pinned.png: (300,560)=[127,0,128], (350,500)=[159,0,96], (301,561)=[183,0,72]. Readout at that location: lab(29.568301979097% 68.287364602547 -112.029709525105) = #0000FF. Measured stage zoom 0.4233. probe/shot-forced-colors.png shows crisp red/blue texels in the loupe and flat purple in the surrounding stage in ONE frame. DPR dependence: same region reads flat purple in shot-desktop-light-pinned.png (DPR 1) and resolved red/blue moire in shot-zoom200.png (DPR 2).
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-imageeyedropper/probe/probe.mjs (displayedVsSampled.zoom 0.4233, displayedCentrePixel [95,0,160]) then probe2.mjs (hoverReadout = pure-blue lab). Or by eye: probe/shot-forced-colors.png.

**Proposed cure.** One resampling law owned in one place. zoom>=1: stage paints image-rendering:pixelated so a texel is a visible square and the loupe is that same law magnified. zoom<1: the sample is the area-average over the 1/zoom x 1/zoom source box the pointer's display pixel actually covers. Stage, loupe, reticle and readout then read one SamplerModel instead of three.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Every second tap is a dead tap that also discards the pin, leaving the PREVIOUS color displayed as if it were the current sample. On touch this is the only sampling interaction.

**Mechanism.** ImageEyedropper.vue:176-185 adds a capture-phase pointerdown listener that unpins and raises `justUnpinned`; onTap (:151-155) consumes the flag with an early return. Touch has no hover, so half of all taps are no-ops while the readout keeps showing a color from a different part of the image.

**Evidence.**

```
probe2.mjs tapCycle: tap purple -> lab(29.5683...) pinned(3 buttons); tap grey -> readout UNCHANGED lab(29.5683...), unpinned(1 button); tap grey again -> lab(53.585013452169% 0 0) pinned; tap purple -> readout UNCHANGED lab(53.5850...), unpinned.
```

**Reproduction.** node .../probe/probe2.mjs — see tapCycle table.

**Proposed cure.** Delete justUnpinned and the second, never-removed event-binding mechanism (the composable already binds the element at useInertiaGesture.ts:327-350). A tap always samples and always pins; re-sampling the same texel is idempotent; unpin belongs to Escape/close, which already own it (:226-235).

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-3 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The magnifier loupe never draws a single pixel on touch — the user taps to sample and gets an empty ring with the raw image running straight through it.

**Mechanism.** useLoupeCanvas.ts:55-60 showLoupeAt sets loupeVisible=true then synchronously calls drawLoupe; the canvas is behind v-if (ImageEyedropper.vue:78-86) so loupeCanvasRef.value is still null and drawLoupe returns at :30. Every subsequent touch repeats it because the capture pointerdown handler calls hideLoupe(), unmounting the canvas again.

**Evidence.**

```
probe.mjs, WebKit 390x844 @3x hasTouch, after page.touchscreen.tap(): mobile.loupe.paintedPx = 0 of totalPx 12100. Visible in probe/shot-mobile-dark-tapped.png. Desktop after hover: paintedPx 9684 (the disc IS painted) — hover is the only thing masking it.
```

**Reproduction.** node .../probe/probe.mjs -> mobile.loupe.paintedPx: 0.

**Proposed cure.** The loupe canvas is a fixed 110px node — keep it mounted and drive visibility with opacity, which is what the CSS already animates (:270). The v-if buys nothing and costs the first frame, which on touch is the only frame.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-4 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The answer is truncated mid-number and cannot be recovered: 12 decimal places of Lab for an 8-bit sample, in a box half the width it needs, with no title attribute.

**Mechanism.** 12-decimal float serialization fed to a `truncate` span with no title and no expansion. The sibling file in the same feature solved this and says why — ExtractWorkbench.vue:134-141 'truncate may trim trailing digits ... the full readout rides title + select-all (never a lying readout)' — and adds :title. useImageSampler.ts:39-41 rounds to 4dp but only on the non-CSS path; the CSS path (:63-64 serializePickerColor) has no equivalent.

**Evidence.**

```
probe2.mjs readout: chars 55, clientW 275, scrollW 555, truncated true, title null, font 'Fira Code' 16.4px — 49.5% of the value is on screen. Mobile capture shows `lab(53.5850…`. At the audit's own 200% zoom simulation (720x450@2x) readoutClientW = 117px, about 7 Fira characters.
```

**Reproduction.** node .../probe/probe2.mjs — readout block.

**Proposed cure.** Quantize at the source (an 8-bit sample carries no information past ~3 Lab decimals) for every space, not only library spaces; then reserve the widest legal representation of the selected space per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4, and give the readout its own line when the space is verbose instead of sharing a 275px row with two action buttons.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-5 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** In RTL the specimen canvas is rendered 692px outside its own clipping stage and disappears entirely, while the sampler keeps returning values for an image nobody can see.

**Mechanism.** The canvas is an inline-level element positioned by static flow; its layout box is the full attribute width (1200px), so in an RTL block it right-aligns from the stage's right edge (1239-1200=39) and the transform is applied on top of an accidental origin. In LTR canvasX == stageX by coincidence, and viewportToImage (useImageSampler.ts:103-109) silently depends on that coincidence. Separately the readout inherits direction:rtl with unicode-bidi:normal (measured) for a string full of parentheses and minus signs.

**Evidence.**

```
probe4.mjs — LTR: canvasX 201, stageX 201, w 508 (aligned). RTL: stageX 731 but canvasX 39, w 508 — zero overlap, and the stage is overflow-hidden. Transform identical in both, matrix(0.423333,0,0,0.423333,0,139.04). rtlRead still returns lab(29.568301979097% ...).
```

**Reproduction.** node .../probe/probe4.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** State the specimen's origin instead of inheriting it from flow: absolutely position the canvas at the stage's physical top-left — exactly the frame viewportToImage already assumes. Add dir=ltr / unicode-bidi:isolate on the readout per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1.

**Defect.** Every interactive WatercolorDot in the component is inert; colors mode cannot accept a single color. MixSourceSelector.vue:148, :150, :164-176, :211-221. Live WebKit measurement (isolated, http://localhost:9000/#/mix, seeded 2-palette library), identical on light/1440, dark/1440, light/390: {"ghostTag":"SPAN","ghostAriaHidden":"true","ghostAriaLabel":null,"ghostPointerEvents":"none","ghostCursor":"pointer","plusPresent":false,"svgClasses":["watercolor-filter-host"],"hitTest":"DIV.swatch-row ...","focusablesInWell":0}; "clickAdd":{"before":0,"after":0}; "fromPalettes":{"firstSwatch":{"tag":"SPAN","ariaHidden":"true","ariaLabel":null,"pe":"none"},"chipsAfterClick":0}; "tabOrder":["BUTTON :: Colors","BUTTON :: Palettes","BUTTON :: From palettes2","BUTTON :: Color space","BUTTON :: Hue method"]

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** `object-contain` is defeated: the uploaded source image overflows its `overflow-hidden` container and is silently centre-cropped, so the preview contradicts the extracted palette in the same frame.

**Mechanism.** height:100% against an indefinite containing-block height resolves to auto, so the img takes its intrinsic aspect at the full 458px width; the max-height cap lives on the container, which then clips with justify-center splitting the overflow top/bottom.

**Evidence.**

```
probe-D-type-crop.json (400x1200 portrait, 1440x900): {"imgBox":{"y":-326.3,"h":1374,"bottom":1047.7}, "zoneBox":{"y":200.7,"h":320,"bottom":520.7}, "objectFit":"contain", "croppedTopPx":527, "croppedBottomPx":527, "visibleFractionPct":23.3}. probe-D-final.json (2400px square): img h=458 in dropMaxH "320px". Frame: frames-crop/portrait-crop.png shows a 6-band image rendering as yellow+green only, with the palette below reading purple/red/green/yellow/orange. Source: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageDropZone.vue:41 (`w-full h-full object-contain`) + ExtractWorkbench.vue:20 (`max-h-[min(320px,40dvh)]`).
```

**Reproduction.** node /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-workbench/probe-D-type-crop.mjs ; open frames-crop/portrait-crop.png

**Proposed cure.** REPLACE, not patch. The preview is a stage, not a capped flow child. Give the drop-zone root a definite block size (aspect-ratio, or an h-[clamp()] on the root rather than a max-h on a content-sized box) so object-contain has a real box to fit into, and let the specimen letterbox against the well ground. Cropping the protagonist to preserve a layout rhythm is the wrong trade for a colour-extraction instrument.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The `isProcessing` loading state never renders. During the entire compute window the UI shows the unchanged empty-state ghost and the caption "· undeveloped plate — feed it an image ·", instructing the user to do what they have already done.

**Mechanism.** `mode="out-in"` holds the entering branch until the leaving branch's transition resolves; by then isProcessing has flipped back to false, so the branch that wins is always the developed card. The out-in mode chosen to protect the skeleton is what makes it unreachable. The `role="status"` / aria-label="Loading palette" announcement is likewise never made.

**Evidence.**

```
probe-D-final.json, MutationObserver + per-rAF occupant sampler, Chrome CPU throttled 20x, 2400x2400 source: OCCUPANT TRACE = [[0,"ghost"],[2894,"card"]] — two occupants in 2.9 seconds; SKELETON never appears. Corroborated unthrottled in both engines (probe-D-focus-transition.json: ghost through t≈210ms, then card; no SKEL sample in 60 samples over 2.1s). Source: ExtractWorkbench.vue:102-107 (`<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` + `v-if="session.isProcessing.value"`). The claim it breaks is ExtractWorkbench.vue:92-99: "isProcessing swaps ghost → KNOWN-IMMINENT skeleton IN PLACE (same bones — a material change, not a layout jump)".
```

**Reproduction.** node /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-workbench/probe-D-final.mjs — read the OCCUPANT TRACE line.

**Proposed cure.** Collapse ShadowPalette and PaletteCardSkeleton into ONE plate component with state: "empty" | "working" | "developed", and drop mode="out-in" so the working register can cross-fade in. The 'same bones' promise then holds structurally instead of by hand-copy across two files (which already differ: ShadowPalette strip uses gap-px + flex-1, PaletteCardSkeleton uses no gap + width:100/count%).

### `CHALLENGE-D — design of demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVi` · D-3 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** On touch, tapping inside a SELECTED stop handle's own advertised hit region DELETES the stop. The remove chip (top-11, 44px below the rail) carries the same always-on hit inflation (--touch-target 2.75rem = 44px) as the handle, and the selected handle's scale(1.25) also scales its ::before expander to 55px, so the two invisible regions overlap with the destructive one on top (chip z-20 vs handle z-10). **Evidence.**

Hit map from p3.mjs T7: `handle-hit offsets -26 → 13 | chip-hit offsets 14 → 40` (offsets from handle centre); `expander 44px x 44px`. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design of demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVi` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** No ordering invariant: a drag can carry a stop across its neighbour, leaving stops[] non-monotonic. sampleCoalescedStops then emits DESCENDING percentages into a CSS linear-gradient, which the browser clamps into a hard band, and the per-interval easing curves silently re-pair because intervals are keyed by array index rather than by the stop pair.

**Mechanism.** an ordinal identity that exists in the UI vocabulary ('stop 2', '1 → 2') but has no representation the model defends

**Evidence.**

```
evidence/p4.mjs T10: `T10 stops after cross {"n":4,"pos":["0","29","8","100"],"centers":[235,362.6,270.6,675]}`; painted rail percentages `[…,26.36, 29, 27.1, 25.2, 23.3, 21.4, 19.5, 17.6, 15.7, 13.8,…]` with `descendingPairs=[[12,29,27.1],…,[21,11.9,10]]`. Screenshot evidence/D02-cross-drag-hard-band.png shows the resulting seam. Source: useGradientModel.ts:127-131 (updateStop never sorts; addStop at :118 does), useGradientCSS.ts:195-200 (pos = s0.position + t*(s1-s0), negative range), GradientVisualizer.vue:64-88 (colorAtPosition assumes sorted). Interval labels stay index-keyed: p2.log T3 `["1 → 2","2 → 3"]`.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence/p4.mjs — block T10

**Proposed cure.** The model owns the ordinal: re-sort on every position commit and re-key intervals to the stop PAIR, or clamp a dragged stop into (prev, next). Only then is VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2's explicit reorder grammar (Space grabs, 'position of total' announcement, Escape cancels) implementable at all.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design of demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVi` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The instrument has two different position axes for one domain quantity. The ramp is painted across the full border-box; handles, the add-ghost and the pointer inverse ride an inset [HANDLE_HALF, W-HANDLE_HALF] track. They agree only at 50%. The file's own doc-comment asserts they 'share one axis by construction'.

**Mechanism.** two coordinate systems for one domain quantity, neither derived from the other

**Evidence.**

```
evidence/p1.mjs: `BAR x=224.00 w=462.00`, handle 'Gradient stop at 0%' `centerX=235.00` (ramp paints 0% at x=224), handle 'Gradient stop at 100%' `centerX=675.00` (ramp paints 100% at x=686) → 11px = 2.38% of the ramp. evidence/p5.mjs (iPhone 14): bar w=324, centres 44/346 → 11px = 3.40%. evidence/p3.mjs T6: ten clicks at rail fractions .12 .20 .28 .36 .44 .52 .60 .72 .80 .88 produce `pos ["0","10","19","27","35","44","52","60","73","81","90","100"]` — click at 12.0% mints 10%, click at 88.0% mints 90%. Source: GradientStopEditor.vue:317-326 (.gradient-rail background-size 100% 100%, origin/clip border-box), useGradientCSS.ts:266 (linear-gradient(90deg,…)), GradientStopEditor.vue:55-57 (handleLeft), :75-81 (getPosition), :8-13 and :49-53 (the false claim).
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence/p1.mjs (geometry) and evidence/p3.mjs block T6 (click→position map)

**Proposed cure.** One axis, expressed once. Either paint the ramp on the inset track (background-position: 11px 0; background-size: calc(100% - 22px) 100% — the pill caps then hold flat terminal colour, which is what a 0%/100% stop actually means), or put the handles on the full-width axis and inset the rail's silhouette instead. HANDLE_HALF must be read from the rendered handle box rather than re-declared as a JS literal (D-13).

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The stop-ordering invariant ("positions are non-decreasing") has three owners with three contradictory policies: gradientParse REJECTS violations, addStop SORTS, and updateStop — the mutator this component drives on every pointermove and arrow key — does NOTHING. The result is a live model whose own serializer emits CSS that its own parser rejects, and a rail ramp with decreasing sub-stop positions that CSS clamps into a flat band.

**Mechanism.** unique-semantic-ownership violated — a model invariant enforced by whichever mutator remembers it rather than by the type that carries it

**Evidence.**

```
Owners: gradientParse.ts:284-290 (reject) vs useGradientModel.ts:118 (sort) vs useGradientModel.ts:127-131 (no policy); driven by GradientStopEditor.vue:94,145,179 -> GradientVisualizer.vue:94-96. LIVE (localhost:9000/#/gradient, fresh mount, add stop at 50% then drag first handle to 80%): handles = ["Gradient stop at 80%","Gradient stop at 50%","Gradient stop at 100%"]; CSS readout = `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 80%, oklch(70% 0.165 205deg) 50%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)`; computed --rail-ramp = `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(75% …) 80.00%, oklch(74.68% …) 78.13%, oklch(74.37% …) 76.25%, …` (DECREASING). Screenshot: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence-rail-after-reorder.png shows the rail as one flat green slab to ~78% with a hard band to blue. LIVE round trip: feeding that CSS back into [aria-label="Gradient CSS"] yields verdict "stop positions must be non-decreasing (hard-stop reordering isn't modeled)". HEADLESS: `npx vite-node` on the demo modules -> serialized `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 70%, oklch(0.7 0.16 200) 50%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)` -> re-parse REJECT with the same reason. Untested by the gates: e2e/smoke/views/gradient.spec.ts:161-172 drags only the MIDDLE handle to 75%, strictly between its neighbours.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/gradient -> click the rail at ~50% (adds a stop) -> drag the leftmost handle to ~80% -> read the CSS box: positions descend (80%, 50%, 100%). Retype that same string into the CSS box -> the destructive verdict appears. Headless equivalent: vite-node script calling updateStop-shaped mutation then serializeGradient -> parseGradientCSS.

**Proposed cure.** Brand the list. A model/stops.ts owns the ordering algebra and is the ONLY producer of an `OrderedStops` (readonly branded array): insertStop / moveStop (re-sorts, stable — the CSS-native behaviour a user expects from dragging past a neighbour) / removeStop. serializeGradient, sampleCoalescedStops and parseGradientCSS all take OrderedStops, so the parser's reject-branch becomes unreachable-by-construction instead of a runtime tripwire aimed at the app itself.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The published `@mkbabb/value.js/css` surface is NOT total: parseCssColor throws a TypeError on eight empty-argument colour functions instead of returning {ok:false}. The demo's entire "library-oracle" architecture (gradientParse.ts header lines 16-17: "validated by the LIBRARY's own parsers — the validity oracles; the demo never hand-validates a color") is therefore structurally unsound, and the throw escapes the model-or-reject contract as an uncaught TypeError.

**Mechanism.** a published API whose type says ParseResult<CssColor> and whose runtime says "or I throw" — partiality hidden behind a non-null assertion; every consumer written against the type is structurally wrong

**Evidence.**

```
Root cause src/css/grammar.ts:181 `const components = splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(/,/g," "), "space");` — the non-null assertion over splitTopLevel("","/") which returns []. Consumer gradientParse.ts:92-94 `return parseCssColor(token).ok`. node on working-tree dist/subpaths/css.js: oklch()/rgb()/hsl()/lab()/lch()/oklab()/hwb()/color() all -> `THROW: TypeError Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')`; rgb(1 2 3)/red/oklch(0.7 0.1 30) -> ok. node on the INSTALLED node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 -> same THROW (the bug is in the published package). In-browser dynamic import of the exact aliased module the demo runs -> {"oklch()":"THROW: …","rgb()":"THROW: …","oklch(0.7 0.1 30)":"ok"}. Through the demo parser (npx vite-node): `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)` -> UNCAUGHT TypeError; `linear-gradient(90deg, rgb(), blue)` -> UNCAUGHT; `linear-gradient(90deg, color(), blue)` -> UNCAUGHT; `linear-gradient(90deg, red, blue)` -> ok.
```

**Reproduction.** npx vite-node with `import { parseGradientCSS } from 'demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/gradientParse'; parseGradientCSS('linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)')` -> uncaught TypeError. Or type that string into the gradient CSS box on a mounted pane.

**Proposed cure.** Totality is the library's contract, not the consumer's try/catch. Replace the non-null assertions in parseFunctionalColor with an explicit empty-body reject (failure(source,"css_syntax",["components"])), and add a property test over {rgb,rgba,hsl,hsla,hwb,lab,lch,oklab,oklch,color} × {""," ","/",",,"} so the surface can never regress to partiality. Do NOT wrap isColorToken in try/catch — that moves the library's contract into its consumer.

That silently breaks value.js's headless gradient CSS parser, its serializers and its persisted model shape, none of which involve a picker.

**Proposed cure.** value.js `/easing` mints the record: `export interface AuthoredEasing { readonly mode: "bezier"|"steps"; readonly css: string; readonly fn: EasingFunction; readonly points: readonly [number,number,number,number]; readonly steps: number; readonly term: JumpPosition }`. Then `GradientInterval = AuthoredEasing` (no glass-ui import in the model at all) and glass-ui narrows to `export type EasingPickerValue = AuthoredEasing` — consuming the library's vocabulary, the direction its peerDeps already declare. The glass-ui type imports at useGradientModel.ts:12, easingCatalogue.ts:31-35 and GradientEasingEditor.vue:30 all collapse to `@mkbabb/value.js/easing`.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The stop-ordering invariant is homeless: three write paths into stops[] with three contradictory policies. addStop sorts (useGradientModel.ts:118); parseGradientCSS rejects violations (gradientParse.ts:284-290); updateStop — the path this component drives from drag (:94,:145) and keyboard (:179) — enforces nothing (useGradientModel.ts:127-131). The model's serializer therefore emits CSS its own parser calls unmodelable, and intervals[i], defined as the span between stops[i] and stops[i+1], ends up attached to an inverted span.

**Mechanism.** Unique semantic ownership violated — position semantics live in the leaf component (pixels/keys → number), array identity lives in the model, the ordering law lives in the parser. One concept, three homes; the invariant died in the seam. Root structural cause is L-3: hand-rolling a multi-thumb slider instead of consuming one.

**Evidence.**

```
Live at http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, fresh mount, keyboard only — 10x shift+ArrowRight on stops[0] then 10x shift+ArrowLeft on stops[1] yields labels ["Gradient stop at 100%","Gradient stop at 0%"] and CSS readout `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 100%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 0%)` with errs: []. Feeding that exact string to the app's own parser in-page: `import('/@fs/…/gradientParse.ts').parseGradientCSS(...)` → "REJECT: stop positions must be non-decreasing (hard-stop reordering isn't modeled)"; the ordered control case returns OK. Computed --rail-ramp came out with DECREASING positions (100.00%, 96.88%, …, 3.13%, 0.00%), which CSS Images 3 §3.4.3 colour-stop fixup silently repairs. Coverage: `grep -rn "non-decreasing|monotonic" e2e test` finds the invariant only in the parser and its unit test; e2e/smoke/views/gradient.spec.ts:144 drags but never asserts order.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → focus the 0% stop handle → shift+ArrowRight x10 → focus the other handle → shift+ArrowLeft x10 → read the CSS box. Positions descend. Retype that string into the CSS box and the destructive parse verdict appears.

**Proposed cure.** Do NOT add .sort() to updateStop — that makes a fourth policy holder. Transpose the instrument: bind stop positions to a multi-thumb glass-ui Slider (variant="stops"), where the invariant is already solved, shipped and installed one import line away — node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Slider/SliderRoot.js:124 calls getNextSortedValues on every commit, utils.js:8 sorts. Ordering becomes structurally unrepresentable rather than guarded.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/color-picke` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The mobile pane slot is the only slot with no `:on-mount`, so colorPickerRef / generatePaneRef / gradientPaneRef / mixPaneRef are permanently null at mobile viewports. Nine dock action-bar actions render, accept clicks, and silently do nothing; the picker's action bar and the dock commit/cancel-edit affordances are dead on mobile.

**Mechanism.** Ref capture is wired per-slot by hand and one slot was missed; every consumer then optional-chains (`?.`) into the nulls, so the structural gap degrades silently instead of failing. usePaletteWiring.ts:65-73/:121-127 add masking fallbacks (edict 2) that hide it further.

**Evidence.**

```
Same script, same selectors, two viewports: desktop-1440 /#/generate — dock button[aria-label='Regenerate'] scoped to nav.dock-band → palette seed 05a86311 → e84f5064 (works); mobile-390 /#/generate → seed f16915bd → f16915bd (dead), while the pane's own Regenerate on the same page changes it f16915bd → e04dde63 (control passes). At 390px on /#/ the picker's `.action-bar-toggle-inner` measures zero width (toggleVisible=false) vs true at 1440px. Code: App.vue:83-91 (mobile slot, no :on-mount) vs App.vue:105/:131; refs assigned only in App.vue:323-332; handlers optional-chain into null at usePaneRouter.ts:196-198/:208-210/:220-222; App.vue:38 and :41-42 read the null ref; usePaletteWiring.ts:37-58/:117 turns its 2s race-guard into the guaranteed path.
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/probe-actionbar2.mjs — goto /#/generate, click `nav.dock-band .action-bar-toggle-inner`, then `nav.dock-band button[aria-label='Regenerate']`, diff the `seed: <hex>` in main; run at viewport 1440x900 and 390x844.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the two currentConfig-name dispatchers. PaneSlot already owns `liveKey`: have it call `onMount(instance, liveKey)` and let App store into one `paneRefs` record keyed by pane name — one path for mobile and both desktop slots, with the slot (not a second source of truth) answering 'which ref'. Retires three `ref<any>` and the `any` callback params, and cures C-3 in the same move.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/color-picke` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The ref-capture callback fills the WRONG ref for one frame during a pane swap (a ColorPicker instance lands in generatePaneRef while colorPickerRef is nulled), and it re-fires on every unrelated parent re-render.

**Mechanism.** Two sources of truth for one identity: 'what is mounted' (the slot's liveKey) vs 'what the route says' (currentConfig.left), read in the window where they disagree. The `any` typing plus `?.method?.()` optional calls convert a wrong-instance assignment into silence rather than a TypeError.

**Evidence.**

```
jsdom repro using this repo's own vue, modelling the exact PaneSlot↔App contract (inline arrow :ref, one-rAF commit, `left === '…' ? el : null` dispatcher). Trace: after the config flip and before the rAF commit → `left=generate el=Picker -> picker=null generate=Picker`; one unrelated parent re-render → the callback fires again with the same instance. Code: App.vue:323-332 reads currentConfig.value.left (the incoming view) while PaneSlot.vue:86-97 delays the rendered triplet by one rAF; PaneSlot.vue:124 builds a fresh arrow `:ref` on every render; App.vue:317-319 declare `ref<any>` so no type error is possible.
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/ref-churn.mjs (jsdom + vue) — prints the callback trace; line `left=generate el=Picker -> picker=null generate=Picker` is the mis-assignment.

**Proposed cure.** Same as C-2: PaneSlot emits (instance, key); App keys the record off that name. Additionally hoist PaneSlot's `:ref` to a stable function so Vue stops re-running it on every parent-driven update.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** `<body>` is simultaneously the Vue mount container and the teleport/portal host — two roles collapsed onto one element, so the app root and every portal escape hatch are siblings with no intervening app container.

```
demo/color-picker/index.html:214 → `<body class="relative" id="app" data-paper-field></body>`. **Proposed cure.** Keep `data-paper-field` on `<body>` (it correctly must dominate the body-portaled dialogs — index.html:203-213 documents this) and give Vue its own container: `<body data-paper-field><div id="app" class="relative"></div></body>`, with `#app { position: relative; min-height: 100dvh }` in demo/styles/shell.css (the sheet that already owns `.app-layout` at :19). **Defect.** The "switch color space" operation has no home. The canonical pipeline command `updateToColorSpace` has exactly one caller — a watcher inside ColorPicker.vue. This component instead emits a state-write that each of its two hosts reinvents differently; the actual conversion is a side effect of the picker's watcher, so the About-side selector converts the color only because the Picker happens to be mounted.

**Mechanism.** a command modelled as a state-change-plus-watcher, with the effect owned by one of two peer hosts instead of by the domain — no unique home for the operation

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-session/useColorPipeline.ts:170-173 defines updateToColorSpace. `grep -rn "updateToColorSpace" demo/` returns exactly 4 lines: the definition (:170), the return key (:324), the destructure (ColorPicker.vue:214) and the sole call site (ColorPicker.vue:352, inside `watch(() => model.value.selectedColorSpace, …)` at :348-354). Two divergent host writes: ColorPicker.vue:43 `updateModel({ selectedColorSpace: colorSpace })` vs AboutPane.vue:24 `model = { ...model, selectedColorSpace: colorSpace }`. Shared single pipeline: App.vue:257 `provide(COLOR_MODEL_KEY, pipeline)`. Panes are KeepAlive'd: demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:120. Target architecture that breaks the coupling: ARCHITECTURE.md:41 "About is a quiet trailing destination, not Picker's permanent right-hand companion" with /about a first-class route.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE for the picker-free break — labelled HYPOTHESIS: I did not stand up a picker-free /about route, so the failure is predicted from the call graph. All call-graph facts above are verified greps.

**Proposed cure.** The component calls the pipeline operation directly — colorModel.updateToColorSpace(space) — and stops emitting a state-write for hosts to reinvent. Both host handlers die; ColorPicker's watcher at :348-354 dies. One command, one home, zero host-specific write mechanics.

### `DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D) — demo/color-picker/App.vue, the app sh` · D-9 · DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D)

**Defect.** App.vue's boot contract is split across a file it does not own and duplicated in two languages. It mounts onto `<body>` as a three-root fragment, depends on three host attributes declared in index.html (one of which is provably dead), makes the canon's required static boot-error region structurally impossible to preserve, and re-runs the prepaint script's URL/storage/default precedence a second time in TypeScript — which §6.2 forbids in those words.

**Mechanism.** split root ownership — the component's own root contract (positioning ancestor, material attribute, boot precedence) lives in the entry HTML, so it is untyped, untestable, invisible to the component, and duplicated

**Evidence.**

```
Measured (probe-app-D.mjs, all three matrices): mountHostIsBody=true, appLayoutParent="body", bodyAttrs=`class="relative" id="app" data-paper-field="" data-v-app=""`, groundState=null. The mount is demo/color-picker/index.html:205-213 (MT-F012's P0 inline module) ending `app.mount("#app")`, and `#app` IS `<body>` (index.html:226). App.vue is a 3-root fragment: div.app-layout (:2), comment nodes (:144-149), MigratePalettesDialog (:152). (1) `class="relative"` is DEAD: the atmosphere canvas (App.vue:9-17, `absolute inset-0`) is a descendant of `.app-layout` (App.vue:2) which is already `position: relative` (shell.css:25), so the nearest positioned ancestor is never `<body>` — a legacy positioning ancestor, owner edict 2. (2) `data-paper-field` is glass-ui's field contract governing App.vue's own descendants incl. portalled dialogs (index.html:222-226) yet is declared where App.vue cannot see it. (3) Mount replaces the host's children, so `<body>` can hold no `<noscript>` and no pre-rendered fallback — while VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:168 requires "A static semantic boot-error region already present in HTML becomes visible through that data state"; measured groundState=null confirms the whole §6.2 latch (data-ground-state / -schema / -store) is unimplemented. (4) index.html:180-200 runs URL/storage/default precedence in vanilla JS writing --saved-bg-0..N; App.vue:231 `resolveHydratedBootModel()` runs URL->storage->default AGAIN in TypeScript (boot/hydrate.ts:53-78) — VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:172: "The hydrated model consumes the frozen boot object ...; it does not repeat scheme/URL/storage precedence, reconstruct an initial palette in TypeScript, or repaint a second 'equivalent' ground."
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/probe-app-D.mjs  → every row: mountHostIsBody true, appLayoutParent "body", bodyAttrs 'class="relative" id="app" data-paper-field=""', groundState null. Then read index.html:205-213 (mount), :222-226 (data-paper-field rationale), :180-200 (prepaint precedence) against boot/hydrate.ts:53-78 (the second precedence engine).

**Proposed cure.** Take MT-F012's cure and finish it. Move the 8 lines to main.ts referenced via `src=`, with `<div id="app">` as the host. Then: `.app-layout` becomes the app's own root and already declares position:relative, so `class="relative"` is DELETED not moved; `data-paper-field` moves onto `.app-layout` — the element App.vue owns and documents; `<body>` regains the right to carry §6.2's static boot-error region and a `<noscript>`; and main.ts becomes the single reader of the frozen `window.__VALUE_GROUND_BOOT__`, handing it to `createApp(App, { boot })` so App.vue CONSUMES the boot object as §6.2 requires and `resolveHydratedBootModel`'s duplicate precedence engine is deleted outright rather than kept in sync. Necessary but insufficient: it does not fix the 3-root fragment, D-2, D-3 or D-4.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · C-21 · CHALLENGE-C

Re-run at HEAD 7cae8bd0: `grep -c 'plugin-vue\|plugins' vitest.config.ts` -> 0; `grep -rn 'from ".*\.vue"' test/ demo/test/ | wc -l` -> 0; `grep -rln '@vue/test-utils' test/ demo/test/ e2e/ | wc -l` -> 0; `grep -rln 'AdminUsers\|prune' test/ demo/test/ | wc -l` -> 0. vitest.config.ts declares no `plugins` key, so .vue is untransformable; @vue/test-utils and jsdom are devDependencies with zero importers.
