**Proposed cure.** Add `@vitejs/plugin-vue` to vitest.config.ts and mount this component with @vue/test-utils (already a devDependency, zero importers) — the scope questions above (which count is quoted, which key the response belongs to, which state renders) are unit questions and do not need a browser. The e2e tier should assert the DESCRIPTION the operator accepted, not merely that a request left.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The edit target is identified by array index, and the same composable re-indexes that array on removal — so committing an edit after removing an earlier swatch writes past the end and APPENDS a phantom duplicate colour; the edit overlay also silently vanishes, stranding the user in edit mode with no commit/cancel affordance on desktop.

**Mechanism.** ordinal identity carried across a mutation that redefines the ordinals; both halves of the invariant live in one file and neither enforces it

**Evidence.**

```
useSwatchActions.ts:76-83 emits `colorIndex: index`; :90-94 `filter((_, i) => i !== index)` shifts every later index. Consumer usePaletteActions.ts:99-107: `oldCss = savedColorStrings[colorIndex]` (undefined) → passes the `oldCss === newCss` bail → `updated[colorIndex] = newCss` grows the array. LIVE (cpe-probe7.mjs): `0 savedColors: ["lab(50% 20 -30)","lab(70% -40 10)","lab(30% 5 60)"]` → `1 after startEdit(2) — overlays: 1` → `3 after remove(0) — swatches: 2 savedColors: ["lab(70% -40 10)","lab(30% 5 60)"] overlays: 0` → `4 after Enter-commit — swatches: 3 savedColors: ["lab(70% -40 10)","lab(30% 5 60)","lab(30% 5 60)"]`, `4 count label: 3 colors`.
```

**Reproduction.** 1440x900 /#/palettes with 3 seeded colours: hover swatch index 2 → Edit; hover swatch index 0 → Remove; press Enter (ColorPicker.vue:377 global keydown → :258 commitEdit). savedColors gains a duplicate third entry, persisted.

**Proposed cure.** Identify the edit target by identity, not ordinal — mint a per-entry id where the buffer is minted (useColorPipeline.savedColors) and key edits on it; resolve any index at the moment of mutation only. Minimum hardening if the ordinal stays: `commitColorEdit` bails when `colorIndex >= savedColorStrings.length`, and the emit that re-indexes the array clears the pending edit target.

useSwatchActions.ts:42-59. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on `demo/palettes/b` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `ActionFeedback` never re-arms its dismissal timer and never clears it on unmount. Because `showFeedback` sets an already-true `visible` ref, the watcher does not fire and the new message inherits the previous message's remaining countdown; and no `onUnmounted` cleanup exists, so a pending timeout fires into a destroyed component and writes to a dead card's state.

**Mechanism.** watching a boolean edge to drive a timer whose identity is really the MESSAGE, plus a raw module-scope `setTimeout` handle with no lifecycle cleanup

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/ActionFeedback.vue:37-47 (`watch(() => props.visible, …)`) · PaletteCard.vue:238-242 `showFeedback` sets `feedbackVisible.value = true` (no-op when already true) · BrowsePane.vue:226-265 fires showFeedback from 4 async paths against the same card · executable vitest probe (@vue/test-utils + fake timers, host mirrors PaletteCard.vue:123-128), both tests PASS: "visible 100ms after 2nd message: false" (promised 2500ms, delivered 100ms) and "timers pending before unmount: 1 after unmount: 1"
```

**Reproduction.** `npx vitest run --config <probe cfg>` on a mount of ActionFeedback via a host replicating PaletteCard's wiring: showFeedback('Saved!','success'); advanceTimersByTime(2400); showFeedback('Delete failed','error'); advanceTimersByTime(100) → visible === false. Second test: showFeedback then unmount() → vi.getTimerCount() still 1.

**Proposed cure.** The component is a timed toast, so the boolean is the wrong subject: watch message identity (`() => [props.visible, props.message]`) and register `onUnmounted(() => clearTimeout(timer))`. Better still, hoist the dismissal to the caller and let ActionFeedback be pure presentation — that also removes the `update:visible` round-trip back into the parent.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on `demo/palettes/b` · C-7 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `defineExpose({ showFeedback })` forces both consumers to maintain a component-instance map, and both register it with `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[key] = el)"`. Vue calls a function ref with `null` on unmount, so the `el &&` guard makes teardown a no-op: nothing is ever deleted. The reactive map grows for the session lifetime, retaining dead component instances and, through them, whole subtrees, spring instances, hover closures and Palette objects.

**Mechanism.** an imperative `defineExpose` handle as the feedback channel forces an identity map on every host; the `el &&` truthiness guard silently discards Vue's unmount signal, and the `(el: any)` cast hides the null from tsc

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:244 `defineExpose({ showFeedback })` · BrowsePane.vue:94 and PalettesPane.vue:84 `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.slug] = el)"` · BrowsePane.vue:209 / PalettesPane.vue:177 `reactive<Record<string, InstanceType<typeof PaletteCard>>>({})` · growth drivers: BrowsePane.vue:140 `pm.loadMoreRemotePalettes()` paging, plus filter/sort re-keys
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — code-level certainty rather than an executed measurement (the shared dev browser in this formation had a concurrent writer, so a live key count would not have been attributable). The omission is unambiguous: Vue invokes function refs with `null` on unmount and the guard drops that call.

**Proposed cure.** Architectural transposition, not a delete-key fix: make feedback DATA. Lift `{ key, message, variant }` into the pane and pass it down as a prop (`:feedback="feedback?.key === palette.slug ? feedback : null"`). `defineExpose`, both cardRefs maps, both `(el: any)` casts and the leak all disappear together, and the component stops needing an imperative handle at all.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on `demo/palettes/b` · C-DECOMP · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The decomposition is not along real seams. `PaletteCardSwatches.vue` is a 96-line wrapper with ZERO state and ZERO logic that declares 8 props and 8 emits, every one of which is a pass-through between `useHoverPopover()` and its consumer one component away — precisely the earns-nothing wrapper feedback_kiss_no_contrivance forbids. `PaletteCardMeta.vue` is a 64-line multi-root fragment extracted to reduce a line count. Meanwhile the centre did not move: PaletteCard still declares 17 emit variants and an 18-branch string-keyed dispatch table whose child contract is an untyped `action: [action: string]`, with `if (!fn) return;` silently swallowing any unknown string.

**Mechanism.** markup was moved out while state stayed centralized, so the split produced conduits rather than components; the seam was drawn above the state that is actually local to the swatch row, and the parent's outward surface (17 emits, stringly-typed dispatch) was never touched

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteCardSwatches.vue:75-95 (8 props, 8 emits, no `ref`/`computed`/`watch` anywhere in the file) — every prop sourced from PaletteCard.vue:246-255's `useHoverPopover()` destructure, every emit routed back to that same destructure at PaletteCard.vue:149-156 · the composable's only parent-side use is the one line PaletteCard.vue:277 `onBeforeCollapse: () => { openPopoverIndex.value = null; }` · PaletteCard.vue:200-218 (17 emits) and :290-319 (18-entry table, `if (!fn) return;` at :315-316) · PaletteCardMenu.vue:225 `action: [action: string]` · file sizes: PaletteCard 364 / Menu 228 / Swatches 96 / Meta 64 / Rename 66 / Feedback 58 lines; PaletteCard's `<script setup>` is 172 lines
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — this is a structural judgment, evidenced by the file contents and the prop/emit census above rather than by an execution.

**Proposed cure.** Move `useHoverPopover()` INTO PaletteCardSwatches (its state is entirely local to the swatch row; the parent's single need is covered by an `@collapse` emit or a `watch(() => expanded)` in the child). That collapses 8 props to 4 (`colors`, `isLocal`, `displaySlug`, `swatchClass`) and 8 emits to 3, making it a real component. Type the menu contract as a `MenuAction` union so `if (!fn) return;` becomes unreachable and deletable, and the 17-emit surface becomes checkable. Keep PaletteCardMenu, PaletteRenameInput and ActionFeedback — those three splits are along genuine seams. Fold PaletteCardMeta back into the title row (it is a fragment, not a component).

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on `demo/palettes/b` · C-TESTS · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Vacuous gate: there is no test anywhere that would fail if PaletteCard were broken — and it IS broken. Zero unit tests mount any of the six files or exercise any of the four composables, and no e2e test ever expands a card, which is exactly why every defect in the expanded region (C-1, C-2, C-6, C-9) has shipped unnoticed since March 2026.

**Mechanism.** the gates assert MATERIAL identity (tokens, tiers, backgrounds) and two isolated network flows, never BEHAVIOUR of the component's principal interaction, so an entire rendering region has no observer

**Evidence.**

```
`grep -rln "PaletteCard" test/ demo/test/` → no matches; `grep -rln "useHoverPopover|useHeightTransition|useLeaveTimer" test/ demo/test/` → no matches (vitest.config.ts includes `test/**/*.ts` + `demo/test/**/*.ts`) · e2e coverage is only e2e/smoke/flows/palette-delete.spec.ts (clicks "Palette menu" then Delete) and e2e/smoke/flows/vote-toggle.spec.ts (clicks the heart); e2e/smoke/oracles/o7-card-census.spec.ts:183 asserts only `[role="article"].bg-well` resolves to `--well-bg` (a material census) · `grep -rn "expand" e2e/` returns dock/band tests only · REPORT.json records both palette routes captured with zero cards (browse consoleWarning "Failed to load remote palettes: SyntaxError…"; palettes.png shows "No saved palettes yet.")
```

**Reproduction.** Green-keeping mutations, each verified reachable by inspection: (1) delete `@click="$emit('click')"` at PaletteCard.vue:26 — expansion dies entirely; (2) change PaletteCard.vue:226 to `colors[1]?.css` — every card's certified ink is wrong; (3) replace PaletteCardSwatches.vue's template with `<template />` — the expanded card renders empty; (4) set ActionFeedback.vue:30 `autoDismissMs` default to 0 — feedback never dismisses; (5) delete `defineExpose({ showFeedback })` at PaletteCard.vue:244 — four BrowsePane async paths throw at runtime. All five keep the full suite green.

**Proposed cure.** Two files, no new infrastructure. (a) A vitest mount test that expands the card and asserts the swatch row renders NAMED, FOCUSABLE controls — it fails today on C-1. demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:213-225 (async, no await), spinner line 102, `:disabled="searching"` line 98, guard line 214, Loader2 import line 142. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects (SearchFilterBar.vue, a` · C-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The "Clear all filters" button lives inside `v-if="activeFilterCount > 0"`; clicking it drives the count to zero, so the focused button unmounts itself and focus falls to <body> inside an open popover, breaking focus order and leaving the popover's focus scope with nothing to restore.

**Mechanism.** a control whose own side effect destroys its mount condition — self-unmounting focused element with no focus transfer

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:110-120 (the v-if wrapper) and 227-232 (onClearAll); parent zeroing in demo/palettes/browser/dialog/composables/useDialogBrowseActions.ts onClearFilters. ```

**Reproduction.** Mount SearchFilterBar with tier='featured', focus the 'Clear all filters' button, trigger('click'), then setProps({tier:'', selectedTags:[]}) to mimic the parent response; document.activeElement is BODY.

**Proposed cure.** Keep the row mounted and disable it (`:disabled="activeFilterCount === 0"`) rather than v-if-ing it out — this also stops the popover from resizing under the pointer. Alternatively move focus explicitly to the popover content root before the state change.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/palettes/brows` · C-6 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `ActionFeedback` is silent to assistive tech, truncates a second message that arrives inside the dismiss window, and never clears its timer on unmount.

**Mechanism.** State change keyed on a boolean visibility edge rather than on message identity; plus a missing scope disposal.

**Evidence.**

```
Live: `chipAfterFirstSave = {text:"Saved!", role:null, ariaLive:null}` — no live region on the sole surface reporting four async outcomes (BrowsePane.vue:230,239,249,264). Timing: Save at t=0, Save again at t=2250 ms while the chip was still up → `secondChipLifetimeMs: 613` (promised 2500). Control run with the second Save at t=2523 ms (outside the window) → `secondChipLifetimeMs: 2752`. Cause: ActionFeedback.vue:39-47 watches `props.visible`; PaletteCard.vue:240 writes `feedbackVisible.value = true`, a no-op write when already true, so the watcher never fires and the in-flight timer is neither cleared nor re-armed. Third defect: `let timer` (:37) has no unmount cleanup.
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe7.mjs — read `secondSaveAtMs` and `secondChipLifetimeMs`; flip the intermediate wait to 1750 ms for the outside-window control.

**Proposed cure.** Watch the message identity (`() => [props.visible, props.message]`) and key the transition on it so a new message is a new node; add `role="status" aria-live="polite"`; register `onScopeDispose(() => clearTimeout(timer))`. Better: hoist dismissal to the caller and let the chip be pure presentation — that also deletes the `update:visible` round-trip and half of C-8.

**Mechanism.** App-scoped/data-shape cousin — three distinct states (empty commons / no results for this query / error) collapsed into two plates.

```
Measured twice: probe-C-live-r2 `"zeroResultSearch": { "cards": 0, "eyebrow": true, "copy": true, "hint": true }`; probe-C-live-r3 `"H_colorSearchNoMatch": { "wallCards": 0, "trueEmptyInvitation": true, "hint": true, "loadMoreStillOffered": 1 }`. ```

**Reproduction.** On a loaded wall, type `zzzzqqq` in "Search the commons…" (or run a colour search that matches nothing). Both measured live.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/palettes/browse` · C-12 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Test truth: the vitest tier cannot mount ANY component in this repo, and the three e2e specs that touch this panel would stay green through nearly every defect above.

**Mechanism.** Vacuous gate — the assertions that exist are orthogonal to the behaviour that matters, and the tier that could assert it is structurally disabled.

**Evidence.**

```
`grep -c 'plugin-vue\|plugins' vitest.config.ts` → 0 (no plugins key at all, so .vue is untransformable under `npm test`); `grep -rn 'from ".*\.vue"' test/ demo/test/ | wc -l` → 0 across `find test demo/test -name '*.ts' | wc -l` → 25 files; `grep -rln '@vue/test-utils' test/ demo/test/ e2e/` → no output (devDependency ^2.4.10 with zero importers, alongside jsdom ^26.1.0); `grep -rln 'AdminUsers\|prune' test/ demo/test/` → no output.
```

**Reproduction.** Named mutation that keeps every gate GREEN: replace AdminUsersPanel.vue:241 `const emptyCount = computed(() => users.filter((u) => !(u.paletteCount ?? 0)).length);` with `const emptyCount = computed(() => users.length);` — the panel then offers "Prune 5 empty users?" for a five-user roster and prunes globally, while e2e/smoke/admin/flows/user-status.spec.ts (asserts only that DELETE /admin/users/<slug> fires), both a11y-authed-admin.spec.ts battery tests (assert nameless==[] and undersized==[], both already true — see negative proof), the BR-9 keyboard test and the U-F58 boundary test all pass. The same immunity covers C-1, C-3, C-4, C-5, C-6 and C-7. Note also `expect(report.controlsChecked).toBeGreaterThan(0)` — the spec's own guard against an empty-scope false green — is satisfied by the toolbar's Prune/Refresh/Sort buttons with ZERO user rows present.

**Proposed cure.** Give vitest a vue plugin (`plugins: [vue()]` in vitest.config.ts) so the already-installed @vue/test-utils + jsdom can mount SFCs, then gate the behaviours no browser cheaply reaches: (i) a prune whose transport throws must not render success-family copy; (ii) a second action-result survives its own full dismissal window; (iii) a late palette response for a stale key does not render; (iv) a failed disclosure renders the error plate, not the empty one; (v) no count is rendered while loadError is set. Structure first where possible (C-1/C-4/C-5's discriminated union make three of these unrepresentable); tests only for what structure cannot forbid.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-21 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The `.cartoon-cast` cel-caster renders nothing, and the entire cartoon motion register the source comments describe has not existed since the Glass 7.0.0 adoption — while `demo/DESIGN.md:246` still records it as `landed`. This also CORRECTS the prior seat's §1/D-1, which counts the cast as a live 'fourth lagging caster'.

**Mechanism.** Producer-contract drift silently swallowed by a whole-version adoption (W44 Glass 7.0.0), preserved by comments and a canon row that assert behaviour no longer rendered, plus an untyped free-form `pressVar` string that nothing cross-checks against the CSS custom property the consuming rule reads.

**Evidence.**

```
Live getComputedStyle on the `<span class="cartoon-cast">` (PaletteCard.vue:30): `position: static` (spec says absolute), `display: inline`, `inset: auto` (spec says 0), `border-radius: 0px` (spec says inherit), `box-shadow: none` (spec says var(--shadow-cartoon-md)), `getBoundingClientRect() = {width:0, height:0}`. Cause (a): `$ grep -rl "glass-atom" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/` → `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/glass/glass-atom.css` (only the file itself) — index.css imports 30 sheets, glass.css imports 18 more, neither includes it. Cause (b): glass-atom.css computes `--cast-travel: calc(6px * var(--motion-weight) * var(--cartoon-press-t))` but PaletteCard.vue:264 passes `pressVar: "--card-press-t"`; measured root inline style `--card-press-t: 0.0000`, measured `--cartoon-press-t: 0` (registered @property initial, property-regs.css) → measured `--cast-travel: 0px`, `--cast-spread: 1`. Producer contradiction: `dist/components/card/Card.vue.d.ts:11-12` — `/** Static Memphis edge treatment; it does not add command behavior. */ cartoon?: boolean;` vs PaletteCard.vue:7-15 claiming cartoon-surface 'owns the hover/press choreography (translate/scale on --ease-cartoon-punch @ --duration-normal, shadow bezier md→lg, :active squash, 2px border)'. Shipped utility is three declarations: `@utility cartoon-surface { position: relative; border-width: 2px; box-shadow: var(--shadow-cartoon-md); }` — no transition, no :hover, no :active. Selectors carrying --ease-cartoon-punch: glass-capsule.css, glass-atom.css, glass-chip.css, liquid-enter.css, btn.css — `.cartoon-surface` and `.card` absent.
```

**Reproduction.** Seed `localStorage['color-palettes']` with any palette, load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, then `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('[role="article"] .cartoon-cast'))` → position:static, display:inline, box-shadow:none, 0×0 rect. Static half: `grep -rl "glass-atom" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/`.

**Proposed cure.** Do NOT patch the variable name or add the missing @import — the ruled tuple forbids the register outright (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.1 / line 186 'not cartoon casters stacked within casters'; PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.12 'no cartoon/grid/selected variant'). Transpose the root to `<Card size="sm" material="content" tier="quiet" surface="opaque" :shadow="false" :grain="false" specular="off">`, deleting cartoon-surface, the `.cartoon-cast` span, `useLiquidPress`, border-card-edge, bg-well and the dead `group` class in one move. Retire `demo/DESIGN.md:246` explicitly. Crucially: because the motion is already dead, this forfeits nothing and owner edict 6 is NOT engaged by the deletion — it was engaged, and violated, by the adoption that dropped the behaviour without a rendered witness.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-22 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Live intermittent null-dereference crash inside PaletteCard's own hover-popover positioning. This CORRECTS the prior seat's Negative proof #3 ('No console or page error is attributable to this component').

**Mechanism.** `PointerEvent.currentTarget` is reset to null once dispatch completes; `nextTick` defers the dereference past the listener's return, so survival depends on where the microtask checkpoint falls — an intermittent null deref. The `as Element` cast is precisely what lets it compile: it asserts away the null that actually arrives.

**Evidence.**

```
Captured WebKit console, verbatim (copied to `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCard/evidence/seat-D2-console-hoverpopover-crash.log`): `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getBoundingClientRect')\n    at positionPanel (…/demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHoverPopover.ts:18:25)\n    at …/demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHoverPopover.ts:26:18`. Both frames are the component's own composable. useHoverPopover.ts:18 is `const rect = swatchEl.getBoundingClientRect();`; :26 is `nextTick(() => positionPanel(e.currentTarget as Element));`.
```

**Reproduction.** Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with a seeded multi-colour palette, expand a card, hover a swatch. Captured in-session; stack pasted above. Note the prior seat's probes exercised rest and expand but never hovered a swatch, which is why they saw `errors: []`.

**Proposed cure.** Delete `useHoverPopover` entirely as part of the cure that moves swatch actions to the selected inspector (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.1 reserves a 33.33–36% inspector for exactly this). If any floating layer survives the transposition it must be the reka-ui `Popover` already present on the touch branch — never a hand-rolled `getBoundingClientRect` + Teleport with a magic `offsetY = -42` that never repositions on scroll/resize and never flips at viewport edges. Narrow the report's Negative proof #3 to 'no page error in the rest and expand states'.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-23 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The accessible swatch popover implementation exists but is gated behind `!canHover` — i.e. delivered to touch users and withheld from keyboard-only desktop users. Two implementations of one affordance, one accessible and one not, switched by input modality. SHARPENS the prior seat's D-3.

**Mechanism.** Accessibility routed off a pointer-capability media query rather than being universal, so the population that most needs the accessible branch (keyboard-only desktop) is the exact population the query excludes from it.

**Evidence.**

```
SwatchHoverMenu.vue:8-49 — `<Popover v-if="!canHover">` (reka-ui: focusable, keyboard-operable, auto-positioned) vs `<template v-else><Teleport to="body"><div v-if="open" class="floating-panel" :style="floatingStyle" aria-hidden="true">`. `canHover` is `useBreakpoint("(hover: hover)")` at useHoverPopover.ts:11-14. The component's own comment concedes it: 'W5-a11y: hover-only panel is keyboard-inaccessible — hidden from AT. The reka-ui Popover (touch path) is the accessible route.' A shared `PANEL_LAYOUT` constant exists explicitly 'so the two paths cannot drift' — a comment conceding the duplication.
```

**Reproduction.** Desktop WebKit at http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, expand a card, Tab through it: measured interactive children of a collapsed card = exactly 1 (`"Palette menu"`, 36×36). Add/Edit/Copy are reachable only via `pointerenter` on the aria-hidden Teleport panel.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the hover branch and the modality switch. One implementation for all input modes. Structurally this is owner edict 2 (no dual paths / no masking fallbacks) — and the correct terminal move is the ruled one: swatch actions move to the selected inspector, which deletes `useHoverPopover`, the crash of D-22, the magic `offsetY = -42`, and the accessibility fork together.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-24 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** A consumer wraps PaletteCard in a `<button>`, nesting `<button>`/`<input>`/dropdown-trigger descendants inside it — invalid HTML content model. It is also the ONLY consumer implementing the law-mandated `aria-pressed` seat, and it is invalid precisely because the seat was authored outside the component.

**Mechanism.** Because PaletteCard owns no activation/selection seat, each of five consumers must invent one. Four produce a keyboard-unreachable div; the fifth produces the right shape in the wrong place, which makes it invalid markup. The wrapper's `ring-2 ring-primary ring-offset-2` is a consumer per-instance override (owner edict 5) forced by the component exposing no selection state.

**Evidence.**

```
MixSourceSelector.vue:246-268 — `<button v-for="palette in savedPalettes" type="button" :aria-pressed="isPaletteSelected(palette.slug)" class="… rounded-card w-full text-left … ring-2 ring-primary ring-offset-2 ring-offset-background" @click="togglePalette(palette)"><PaletteCard :palette="palette" :css-color="''" /></button>`, comment: 'W5-a11y: native <button> for keyboard reach + aria-pressed for selection state'. Interactive descendants rendered inside: `<Button icon-only …>` menu trigger + DropdownMenuTrigger (PaletteCard.vue:96-104), `<input>` (PaletteRenameInput.vue:11), vote `<button>` (PaletteCardMeta.vue:43), copy/add/edit `<button>`s (PaletteCardSwatches.vue:13,41,49,56). Contrast the other four consumers: PalettesPane.vue:91 and BrowsePane.vue bind a bare `@click` on the unfocusable div; measured `card.focus()` → `document.activeElement === card` is **false**, `tabIndex: -1`.
```

**Reproduction.** Read MixSourceSelector.vue:246-268 against PaletteCard.vue:96-104 / PaletteCardMeta.vue:43 / PaletteRenameInput.vue:11. Keyboard half: at http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, `document.querySelector('[role="article"]').focus(); document.activeElement === card` → false.

**Proposed cure.** Give PaletteCard the seat the canon already specifies (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.1 / PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.12): a noninteractive `<Card>` root plus exactly one native `<button type="button" aria-pressed="false|true">` child spanning strip + identity, owning activation, visible selection and focus. That deletes the MixSourceSelector wrapper, its ring override, the `role="article"` click, the `tabIndex:-1` dead root, the `@click="()=>{}"` no-op in ExtractWorkbench, and the `defineExpose`/`cardRefs` `any`-cast reach-in — one architectural move, five consumers simplified.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-05 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Retry is a dead affordance in exactly the state it is offered: while the transport latch is `misconfigured` it can never issue a request, and clicking it destroys the pane (D-01).

**Mechanism.** Failure/pending truth is absent or false — an action offered in a state where it provably cannot succeed.

**Evidence.**

```
availability.ts:188-191 — `if (apiAvailability.value === "misconfigured") throw new DevMisconfigError();` unconditional, no cooldown arm (RETRY_COOLDOWN_MS applies only to `unavailable`). Live probe counting every request whose URL contains /palettes: networkReqsBeforeRetry: 8, networkReqsAfterRetry: 8 — all eight are Vite module URLs (`/@fs/.../BrowsePane.vue?t=…`). Zero API requests before or after the click.
```

**Reproduction.** On /#/browse with the misconfigured latch armed, attach a request listener filtered to '/palettes', click Retry, count requests: unchanged at 8, all Vite module fetches.

**Proposed cure.** Gate the recovery action on the availability arm: under `misconfigured` the plate names the configuration fault and offers no retry; under `unavailable` it offers retry with the cooldown surfaced.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-15 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** "Find by Color" is a silent partial search over the loaded page while the server API supports the query, with an untokenised magic radius and a silent data-dependent exclusion.

**Mechanism.** Search semantics unowned — a masking client-side fallback chosen over a working server path (owner edict 2), plus an unparameterised distance threshold.

**Evidence.**

```
BrowsePane.vue:336-355 — `const radius = 0.15;` then a client-side filter over pm.filteredBrowse with `if (!oklabColors || oklabColors.length === 0) return false;` and the comment "API also supports server-side via colorL/colorA/colorB params, but client-side is instant". demo/palettes/api/palettes.ts:49-52 genuinely sends colorL/colorA/colorB/colorRadius. BROWSE_PAGE_SIZE is 50, and BrowsePane.vue:133 keys load-more on pm.hasMore, so paging fetches the next UNFILTERED page and then colour-filters it. `oklabColors` is optional on the type (types.ts:32) and is a migration field server-side (api/src/platform/migrations/check.ts:46). The `(p: any)` cast at :344 is unnecessary since oklabColors is declared on Palette.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE for the runtime arm (needs a populated reachable commons). Code-proven: the server params exist and are unused; the radius is a bare literal; the missing-oklabColors branch returns false.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The ADMIN 'port' is the god facade renamed, not dissolved: 34 members spanning five unrelated sub-domains. AdminUsersPanel injects all 34 to call exactly one method — and it is a SECOND data path into a component the parent already fully prop-drives.

**Mechanism.** Aggregation without a seam: the port re-assembles five already-cohesive sub-composables into one injected object, so no consumer can be reasoned about without reading all 34 members. Injection is used as a second transport alongside props for the same parent/child pair.

```

AdminUsersPanel.vue:234 injects it; `grep -n 'pm\.' AdminUsersPanel.vue` → 2 lines, one a comment (:233), one the sole use (:361 `await pm.loadUserPalettes(slug)`). AdminPane.vue:26-42 passes 6 props + 7 emit handlers, all from the same `pm`. usePalettePorts.ts:20-30 header claims the RF-15 dissolution of 'ONE cross-everything injected blob' into 'FIVE narrow, feature-owned ports'.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-3 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** 51 dead `variant` props fleet-wide (5 in the subject file): glass-ui 7.0.0 Button has no `variant` prop, so the shadcn styling vocabulary that survived the Glass 7 adoption is silently discarded and leaks to the DOM as a literal attribute. The subject file speaks BOTH vocabularies 40 lines apart.

**Mechanism.** Vue treats an unrecognised lowercase prop as an HTML fallthrough attribute, so a retired design-token vocabulary is neither type-checked nor visibly broken — it renders at the default `emphasis="secondary"` and ships the string to the DOM.

**Evidence.**

```
node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:6-19 — ButtonProps = { emphasis, tone, size, iconOnly, loading, type, disabled, class }; no `variant`. `grep -o "outline\|ghost" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js` → ZERO matches. `emphasis: { default: "secondary" }` in the same chunk. Subject file: variant="outline" at :22,:33,:58,:114 and variant="ghost" at :123 — while :174 `emphasis="text"` and :175 `:tone="confirmDestructive ? 'destructive' : 'neutral'"` are correct Glass 7. Live DOM (Playwright browser_evaluate on http://localhost:9000): `{"tag":"BUTTON","text":"Login","variant":"outline"}`, `{"text":"@mbabb","variant":"ghost"}`, `{"text":"Try again","variant":"outline"}`. Fleet script: 51 `<Button variant=...>` sites in 22 files, incl. FlagReportDialog.vue:41 `variant="destructive"` (a TONE passed as a dead variant). Gate is blind: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → exit 0, 0 errors.
```

**Reproduction.** Load http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users and evaluate `[...document.querySelectorAll('button')].map(b=>b.getAttribute('variant'))` — `outline`/`ghost` appear as literal attributes. Design consequence at AdminUsersPanel.vue:107-111: the comment asserts the per-row destructive is 'quieted to ink-at-rest' via variant="ghost"; glass-ui discards it and renders `secondary`.

**Proposed cure.** Mechanical: variant="outline"→emphasis="secondary", variant="ghost"→emphasis="quiet", variant="destructive"→tone="destructive", variant="default"→emphasis="primary". Structurally the reason 51 sites drifted for a whole tranche is that nothing rejects an unknown token prop: glass-ui Button should set `inheritAttrs: false` with an explicit attr allowlist so an unrecognised design prop is a visible no-op. That half is a glass-ui change and belongs in the BH relay.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-4 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** 51 dead `variant` props fleet-wide (5 in this file): glass-ui 7 Button has no `variant` prop, so the shadcn vocabulary that survived the Glass 7 adoption renders as the default emphasis and ships as a literal HTML attribute. This file speaks both vocabularies 40 lines apart.

**Mechanism.** A design-token prop that the design system does not accept falls through $attrs to the DOM, so an intended visual rung is silently the default; vue-tsc treats an unknown lowercase prop as an HTML fallthrough attribute, making the hard CI typecheck structurally blind to the whole class.

**Evidence.**

```
node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:4-19 — ButtonProps = {emphasis, tone, size, iconOnly, loading, type, disabled, class}; no `variant`. `grep -c "variant" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js` -> 0. My own scan of every <Button ...> tag in demo/**/*.vue: 51 sites in 22 files (independently reproducing r1's count), incl. AdminUsersPanel.vue [(21,'outline'),(32,'outline'),(58,'outline'),(112,'outline'),(122,'ghost')] against the correct Glass 7 usage at :174 `emphasis="text"` and :175 `:tone="..."`. The panel's own comment at :107-111 asserts a quieting invariant expressed as variant="ghost", a prop glass-ui discards; the intended rung is emphasis="quiet".
```

**Reproduction.** Static: the two greps above. Live (r1, Playwright evaluate against localhost:9000): rendered buttons carry literal attributes — {"text":"Login","variant":"outline"}, {"text":"@mbabb","variant":"ghost"}.

**Proposed cure.** Mechanical: outline->emphasis="secondary", ghost->emphasis="quiet", destructive->tone="destructive", default->emphasis="primary" (51 sites). Structural and glass-ui-side (BH relay): Button sets inheritAttrs:false and spreads an explicit allowlist, so an unrecognised design-token prop is a visible no-op at the DOM instead of an invisible one.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-5 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** A hand-rolled 6-digit-hex regex gates the field one line in front of the full CSS Color Level 4 parser it already imports; rejected input is silently replaced by the swatch colour, and the field's own placeholder advertises a syntax the regex refuses.

**Mechanism.** A second, narrower, incompatible parser placed in front of the canonical total parser; failure masked by a fallback instead of surfaced (edict 2: masking fallbacks).

**Evidence.**

```
SearchFilterBar.vue:218 `const hex = text.startsWith("#") && /^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i.test(text) ? text : pickerHex.value;` — with hexToOklab (:205-211) calling parseColorIn, and placeholder="#hex, hsl(...)" at :92, pickerHex default "#4488cc" at :170. Measured library capability: parseCssColor+convertColor resolve all of `hsl(210 60% 50%)` → oklab 0.5883 -0.0443 -0.1319, `oklch(0.7 0.15 250)` → 0.7000 -0.0513 -0.1410, `rebeccapurple` → 0.4403 0.0882 -0.1339, `#48c` → 0.6136 -0.0415 -0.1175, `color(display-p3 0.2 0.4 0.8)` → 0.5340 -0.0363 -0.1775. The regex accepts one of the five. The `"none"` guard at :207-209 is unreachable given the gate — it defends the impossible while the possible failure is silenced.
```

**Reproduction.** Type `rebeccapurple` (or `hsl(210 60% 50%)`, or `#48c`) into the Find-by-Colour field and press Search. The emitted colorSearch triple is that of #4488cc, not the typed colour. No error, no visual difference from success — colorSearchActive goes true and the badge increments.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the regex. `parseColorIn(text, "oklab")` inside a try, surfacing PickerColorError as field-invalid state via glass-ui Input's existing `invalid` prop (measured present). The library is a total parser; stop putting a partial one in front of it.

No immutable channel combinators exist in src/ at all. demo/color-session/picker-color.ts therefore hand-rolls buildColor (:123-143, a 17-arm switch = makeColor with the generic erased), PICKER_CHANNELS (:52-, a second copy of SPACE_SCHEMA.channels), CSS_PICKER_SPACES (= the css flag), the hue:true marker (= hueIndex), and withAlpha/withChannel/withNormalizedChannel/channelNumber/normalizedChannel (:151-192).

**Mechanism.** under-published public surface forcing consumer-side duplication of the domain model

**Evidence.**

```
node -e "import('./dist/subpaths/color.js').then(m=>console.log(Object.keys(m).sort().join(', ')))" -> `a98Rgb, convertColor, displayP3, hsl, hsv, hwb, ictcp, interpolateHue, jzazbz, kelvin, lab, lch, linearSrgb, mapColorToGamut, mixColors, oklab, oklch, prophotoRgb, rec2020, rgb, safeAccentColor, toRgba8, xyz` — 23 names, all four absent. Consumer-side link failure: `SyntaxError: The requested module '.../dist/subpaths/color.js' does not provide an export named 'withAlpha'`. `grep -rn "withAlpha" src/` -> 0 hits, while package.json:4 describes the package as "Immutable, failure-explicit CSS color...". src/color/model.ts:56,76,127,136 vs src/color/index.ts (absent).
```

**Reproduction.** `node -e "import('./dist/subpaths/color.js').then(m=>console.log(Object.keys(m).sort().join(', ')))"` from the repo root, then `grep -n 'SPACE_SCHEMA\|makeColor\|isAnyColor' src/color/model.ts src/color/index.ts` — present in model.ts at :56/:136/:127, absent from index.ts and from the built subpath.

**Proposed cure.** Publish the model: add makeColor, SPACE_SCHEMA, SPACE_IDS, isAnyColor to src/color/index.ts + src/subpaths/color.ts, and move withChannel/withAlpha DOWN from picker-color.ts into src/color (they are pure model operations, nothing about them is a picker concern). Then delete buildColor, the duplicated channel table and the five combinators from the demo; picker-color.ts collapses to what its name promises — a UI-range projection (min/max/unit per channel, display naming) over the library model. Library gains ~6 export lines, demo loses ~90, and the duplication cannot recur because the thing being duplicated is finally reachable.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-16 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** "Is this colour already in the palette?" is implemented twice with different alpha semantics, and the two run in sequence on one click. useSwatchActions.ts:63 does `savedColorStrings.indexOf(cssColorOpaque)` — an ALPHA-STRIPPED candidate against an ALPHA-BEARING haystack (cssColorOpaque = serializePickerColor(withAlpha(color,1)) at useColorPipeline.ts:104; savedColorStrings = savedColors.map(serializePickerColor) at :166-168, alpha preserved). useColorPipeline.ts:213-217 then does `savedColors.some(c => toCSSColorString(c) === toCSSColorString(model.color))` — alpha-bearing both sides. On alpha-bearing data the first says ABSENT (emit the add) and the second says PRESENT (return without adding): the gesture is a silent no-op.

**Mechanism.** duplicated domain predicate with divergent policy — the direct consequence of colour being string-typed above the library (see L-15)

**Evidence.**

```
useSwatchActions.ts:63 vs useColorPipeline.ts:213-217; useColorPipeline.ts:104 and :166-168 for the two serializations. Live: seeding localStorage color-picker with {inputColor:"oklch(0.7 0.15 30 / 0.5)", savedColors:["oklch(0.7 0.15 30 / 0.5)"]} and reloading yields store `savedColors:["oklch(70% 0.15 30deg / 50%)"]` (alpha survives) and countLabel ["1 color"], while cssColorOpaque is "oklch(70% 0.15 30deg)". Alpha is one gesture away: shots/safari-desktop-light/palettes.png shows the alpha channel at 82.7%, and ColorPicker.vue:293 commits every swatch edit as toCSSColorString(model.value.color) — the alpha-bearing serialization — back into savedColorStrings via usePaletteActions.ts:99-106.
```

**Reproduction.** At http://localhost:9000/#/palettes: `localStorage.setItem("color-picker", JSON.stringify({inputColor:"oklch(0.7 0.15 30 / 0.5)", savedColors:["oklch(0.7 0.15 30 / 0.5)"]})); location.reload();` — after settle the palette shows "1 color" with savedColorStrings[0]==="oklch(70% 0.15 30deg / 50%)" while cssColorOpaque==="oklch(70% 0.15 30deg)", so indexOf returns -1 (add is emitted) and onPaletteAddColor's some() returns true (add is swallowed). Equivalent UI path: add a colour, edit it, move the alpha slider, commit, then press add.

**Proposed cure.** One predicate, one home. Once L-15 lands this is a library question — `colorsEqual(a,b)` beside mixColors in src/color/operations.ts, called by both sites; until then it belongs in demo/color-session/ as the single owner of colour identity. And the policy must be chosen rather than inherited: addColor currently STORES the opaque colour while DEDUPING against the alpha-bearing one, which is an accident of two authors, not a rule.

### `L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, depende` · L-12 · L

**Defect.** The unauthenticated state is costumed as an empty roster. `useAdminUsers.ts:52-54` returns before touching `loadingUsers` OR `usersLoadError`, so the panel takes AdminUsersPanel.vue:63 and renders the TRUE-EMPTY plate ('· roster clear ·' / 'No users found.') plus an authoritative '0 users' count for a roster it never requested. This violates the invariant the file annotates itself with at :49-50 ('the P0 case: error != empty — a dead backend never costumes as an empty roster') on the branch every unauthenticated visitor takes. The A-3 guard at :5-10 is defeated by the same hole: it gates on `loading`, which never becomes true on this path.

**Mechanism.** Authorization is a ROUTE precondition modelled as a per-method silent early return. The precondition has no home, so it is re-asserted 22 times, and the one place it matters (the panel's state model) never learns about it — the panel models 3 states (loading/error/empty) where the domain has 4.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:52-54; demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:49-50,63. Live Chromium (read-only): page.evaluate -> {adminToken: null, bodyTextHasNoUsers: true}; browser_network_requests filter 'users|/api/' -> ZERO requests. WebKit corroboration (vision, read this pass): visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/admin-users.png and safari-mobile-dark/admin-users.png — dock reads 'Login', panel reads '0 users' / '· ROSTER CLEAR ·' / 'No users found.'; visual/REPORT.md:128,143,158,173 (pageErr 0, consoleErr 0, overflowX 0, main 1); harness sets only vueuse-color-scheme (visual/capture.mjs:71). Structural half: grep -c 'if (!token) return' demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts -> 11; across demo/palettes/*.ts -> 22; grep -rn 'requiresAdmin|adminOnly|guard' demo/shell/ -> nothing.
```

**Reproduction.** CONFIRMED end to end: (1) ensure localStorage has no 'palette-admin-token'; (2) navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users; (3) network log filtered users|/api/ is EMPTY — no request was ever issued; (4) DOM contains 'No users found' and the toolbar reads '0 users'. The app knows it is logged out (the dock says 'Login') while the panel asserts the roster is clear.

**Proposed cure.** One gate at the composition boundary: an `auth: "admin"` flag in demo/shell/viewSchema.ts honoured once in useViewManager, or an <AdminGate> in AdminPane.vue, rendering an authentication plate when !isAdminAuthenticated. Inside the gate getAdminToken() is a non-null contract — construct useAdminUsers WITH a token rather than letting it re-ask — and all 22 guards delete. The panel then never needs an 'unauthorized' state because it never mounts unauthorized.

### `L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, depende` · L-4 · L

**Defect.** 51 dead `variant` props on `<Button>` across 22 demo files (5 in the subject). glass-ui 7.0.0 ButtonProps declares emphasis/tone/size/iconOnly/loading — there is NO `variant`. Every such button renders at the default emphasis and the prop falls through onto the DOM as an inert HTML attribute. The subject speaks BOTH vocabularies 40 lines apart: dead `variant` at :22,33,58,114,123 and correct Glass 7 `emphasis`/`tone` at :174,175. Concretely damaging: the W5-12/F-8 intent documented at :107-111 ('the per-row destructive is quieted to ink-at-rest — red arrives on hover/focus, never as 5 resting beacons down the list') was expressed as variant="ghost" and is therefore SILENTLY REVERTED — the row delete renders at the same emphasis as the 'Palettes' button beside it.

**Mechanism.** The design-system public surface changed at the 6->7 upgrade and this component was only half-migrated. Nothing can catch it: Vue treats an undeclared attribute on a component as a fallthrough attr, so vue-tsc does not flag it, and eslint.config.js has no rule in this space — CI is documented fully green at HEAD (db77dbd8) while all 51 sites ship.

**Evidence.**

```
node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:6-19 (no `variant` member). LIVE DOM measurement, http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users: {"text":"Prune empty","attrs":["data-slot=\"button\"","data-emphasis=\"secondary\"","data-tone=\"neutral\"","data-size=\"sm\"",…,"variant=\"outline\"",…]} and the same for "Refresh" — data-emphasis="secondary" is glass-ui's DEFAULT, and variant="outline" is a fallthrough attribute styling nothing. Fleet count (own python regex over every `<Button …>` tag-open in demo/**/*.vue): 51 sites across 22 files; 5 in AdminUsersPanel.vue at lines 22,33,58,114,123.
```

**Reproduction.** CONFIRMED: navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users and evaluate `[...document.querySelectorAll('button')].filter(b=>/Prune|Refresh/i.test(b.textContent)).map(b=>[...b.attributes].map(a=>a.name+'='+a.value))` — both buttons show data-emphasis="secondary" alongside a stray variant="outline".

**Proposed cure.** Mechanical rewrite: outline->emphasis="secondary", ghost->emphasis="quiet", destructive->tone="destructive", default->emphasis="primary" (row delete becomes emphasis="quiet" tone="destructive", which also retires its two per-instance hover:text-destructive utilities). Structural: wire the installed, unused `vue/no-restricted-static-attribute` ({key:'variant', element:'Button'}) so the drift cannot recur. Relay to glass-ui BH: the rename shipped with no consumer trap — request `variant?: never` or inheritAttrs:false + an explicit allowlist so an unrecognised design-token prop is a VISIBLE no-op.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/picker/ColorPic` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The Cmd+K handler tests global modifier STATE (`keys.cmd?.value && keys.k?.value`) rather than the event, so any key pressed while Cmd and K are physically held is preventDefault'd and re-toggles the dropdown. There is also no `e.repeat` guard.

**Mechanism.** Chord detection via sampled global key state instead of event inspection — the predicate is true for the whole duration the keys are held, not for the one event that is the chord.

**Evidence.**

```
ColorPicker.vue:263-266. Live probe: hold Meta, hold k (dropdown opens, aria-expanded="true"), then press `a` -> {"A_afterKdown":"true","A_afterOtherKey":"false","A_events":[{"k":"a","meta":true,"rep":false,"dp":true}]}. Cmd+A (Select All) is swallowed AND the color-space dropdown toggles shut on an unrelated keystroke.
```

**Reproduction.** On http://localhost:9000/#/ : page.keyboard.down('Meta'); page.keyboard.down('k'); (dropdown opens) ; page.keyboard.down('a'); page.keyboard.up('a'). The keydown for `a` reports defaultPrevented=true and the trigger's aria-expanded flips true->false.

**Proposed cure.** Test the event: `if (e.key === "k" && (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && !e.repeat)`. The `useMagicKeys()` import (ColorPicker.vue:123,247) then has no remaining consumer and is deleted with it.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/picker/ColorPic` · C-6 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The four channel slider thumbs are 12 CSS px wide at every viewport — WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (Target Size Minimum, 24x24) fails four times. The picker contributes half of the entire application's small-tap-target count on all 60 audit captures.

**Mechanism.** Hit-area extension applied to the wrong box: the pseudo-element grows the track root on one axis only, while the element carrying role="slider" and the actual grab affordance is the 12px thumb.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured live over the `.pane-shell` subtree at 390x600: [{"tag":"span","role":"slider","w":12,"h":24,"name":"L channel"}, ...A, B, ALPHA identical]. These are exactly the rows in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json for `/` desktop ({"w":12,"h":24,"tag":"span","label":"L channel"} x4 of 8 smallTapTargets) and mobile ({"w":12,"h":44} x4) — REPORT.md:90-151 shows 8 on every one of the 60 captures. The touch rung at demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:345-357 grows the SliderRoot's vertical hit box (`block-size: max(100%, 2.75rem)`, `inset-inline: 0`) and never touches the thumb, which is why h goes 24->44 on coarse pointers while w stays 12.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/picker/ColorPic` · C-8 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The picker cancels its parent's shared, app-wide debounced writes on its own unmount — an ownership inversion that silently drops in-flight color changes belonging to sibling components.

```
ColorPicker.vue:381-385 calls `parseAndSetColorDebounced.cancel()` and `updateColorComponentDebounced.cancel()`. Both are created by useColorPipeline in App.vue (useColorPipeline.ts:92 and :209) and provided app-wide via COLOR_MODEL_KEY; other consumers are ComponentSliders.vue:115, ConsoleRail.vue:115, HeroBlob.vue:56 and demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue. The pane KeepAlive is `:max="6"` (App.vue:104) over 7 distinct left panes (color-picker, browse, extract, generate, gradient, atmosphere, admin-*), so the picker IS LRU-evictable. The parse debounce window is 2000ms (useColorParsing.ts:92).
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — hypothesis on the observable drop. The ownership violation itself is direct from the cited lines; the concrete drop requires evicting the picker from the 6-slot LRU while a 2000ms parse debounce is pending, which I did not drive.

**Proposed cure.** The pipeline owns its own lifetime: move both cancels into an `onScopeDispose` inside useColorPipeline. The picker should cancel nothing it did not create — and should instead be clearing the two timers it DOES own (see C-14), which it does not.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-05 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The P019 identity/specimen type pair is at the required 1/√φ only at the phone floor; it drifts to near-parity at 1440, so at desktop the label and the numeric specimen are optically the same size.

**Mechanism.** Two independently clamped sources with different binding arms cannot hold a constant ratio. The register (V-A140) describes this as a fixed two-rung skip; the rendered truth is a ratio that is exactly right at one end of the band and collapses at the other — worse than documented.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured label font-size / headline font-size: 390x844 → 32.928 / 41.888 = 0.7861 (required 1/√φ = 0.78615, correct); 1440x900 → 53.280 / 54.644 = 0.9750. Drift +24.0% across the band. Sources: label = --type-display-2 = clamp(2.058rem, 1.5rem + 2.2vw, 3.33rem) at ColorSpaceSelector.vue:209 (ceiling-bound at 1440); headline = calc(min(var(--type-display-4), max(11.65cqi, 2.618rem)) * var(--readout-fit,1)) at ColorComponentDisplay.vue:137-140 (floor-bound at 390, 11.65cqi-bound at 1440 — --type-display-4 resolves to 86.11px and never binds). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.2: "BI P019 supplies one paired proportional clamp; both sizes resolve from that one clamp … rather than only at endpoints" and "independently clamped display-2/display-3 tokens and a local approximation are forbidden."
```

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-12 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** An undiscoverable global Cmd+K shortcut is bound on `window` with no target guard and no affordance anywhere in the UI.

**Mechanism.** Three defects in one binding: undiscoverable (no affordance), unscoped (a bare window listener fires while focus is in any editable surface, including this component's own contenteditable cells and the dock colour input), and a toggle on a held-key predicate (useMagicKeys reports cmd and k as held, so any subsequent keydown while both remain down re-toggles the popover).

**Evidence.**

```
demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:247 (const keys = useMagicKeys()), :263-266 (if (keys.cmd?.value && keys.k?.value) { e.preventDefault(); selectedColorSpaceOpen.value = !selectedColorSpaceOpen.value; }), registered at :377 (window.addEventListener("keydown", handleKeydown)). No tooltip, menu item, hint or label names it anywhere in demo/picker/. PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-07 ("Hover-only/unlabeled controls") and §5.6 ("Subtraction precedes explanation"); VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 interaction grammar select → tune → commit.
```

**Reproduction.** Read demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:247,263-266,377 — the handler has no event.target / activeElement check and no document-scope guard. Reproduction of the re-toggle: hold Cmd+K and press any third key; the predicate is still true and the popover toggles again.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure: module boundaries, ownershi` · L-4 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** usePaletteWiring routes four cross-cutting colour operations through the picker COMPONENT INSTANCE and silently swaps to different semantics when it is absent — three masking fallbacks plus a 2-second polling retry with a give-up console.warn.

**Mechanism.** Dual path with masking fallback — the same public operation resolves to two different implementations depending on whether an unrelated component happens to be mounted.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-picker/composables/usePaletteWiring.ts:65-73 emitApply — picker present -> onPaletteApply(colors) (replaces savedColors with ALL parsed colours); absent -> applyColorString(colors[0]) (sets the CURRENT colour to the first entry, touches no palette). :121-127 emitSetCurrentColor — applyExternalColor vs applyColorString; these are two near-identical implementations in one file (useColorPipeline.ts:182-188 and :247-257): one calls setCurrentColor (refreshing stableHue) and throws on parse failure, the other calls updateModel and swallows the error. :33-58 whenColorPickerReady polls 40 x 50ms then console.warn('gave up waiting for the color picker to mount'), which on mobile ALWAYS exhausts, so emitStartEdit (:106-119) is dead. All of these are pure pipeline calls: App.vue:245 already holds `pipeline` directly, and 5 of ColorPicker's 12 defineExpose members are straight re-exports of inject(COLOR_MODEL_KEY).
```

**Reproduction.** Read demo/color-picker/composables/usePaletteWiring.ts:33-127 alongside demo/color-session/useColorPipeline.ts:182-188 and :247-257. Behavioural repro: at 390x844 (where colorPickerRef is permanently null per L-2) applying a saved palette loads only its first colour into the current swatch instead of replacing savedColors, and starting a palette colour edit logs the give-up warning after ~2s.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the picker parameter, the retry loop and both fallback arms; call the pipeline directly. Then reconcile applyExternalColor and applyColorString into one named operation in color-session.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure: module boundaries, ownershi` · L-5 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The picker registers a window-level keydown listener in onMounted and releases it only in onUnmounted, but is rendered inside <KeepAlive>, so leaving the picker view deactivates rather than unmounts it and the global shortcut stays live on every other route.

**Mechanism.** Wrong lifecycle pair under KeepAlive: onMounted/onUnmounted instead of onActivated/onDeactivated, in a component whose owner caches it.

**Evidence.**

```
ColorPicker.vue:376-379 onMounted -> window.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeydown); :381-385 onUnmounted -> removeEventListener + two debounce cancels. PaneSlot.vue:120 wraps the pane in <KeepAlive :max="max">. MEASURED live at 1440x900: (1) on #/ fire Cmd+K -> 'Select color space' aria-expanded='true' and [role=listbox] present; (2) Cmd+K again -> closed; (3) navigate to #/browse -> the picker Select is absent from the DOM (pane deactivated); (4) fire Cmd+K on #/browse; (5) navigate back to #/ -> aria-expanded='true', [role=listbox] present. The deactivated picker consumed a global shortcut from a route it does not own. The same hole leaves parseAndSetColorDebounced (2000ms) and updateColorComponentDebounced (500ms) uncancelled on every view switch. Compounding: two keyboard mechanisms for one shortcut set — useMagicKeys() at :247 plus the raw window handler that reads magic-keys state at :263.
```

**Reproduction.** With the dev server on :9000 at 1440x900, in the page context: navigate to '#/', dispatch KeyboardEvent keydown {key:'Meta'} then {key:'k',metaKey:true} on window -> the colour-space Select opens; dispatch again to close; set location.hash='#/browse', wait for the swap, dispatch the same pair; set location.hash='#/' -> the Select is open again (aria-expanded='true').

**Proposed cure.** The shortcut is app-level: move it to a shell-owned keyboard-map composable registered once at the composition root that dispatches to the active instrument. The picker keeps no window listener. Any listener that must live in a KeepAlive'd leaf uses onActivated/onDeactivated.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on `demo/scenes/Con` · C-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `copyAsJson()` awaits `writeClipboard()` and discards its Result. `writeClipboard` never throws — it returns `{ok:false, reason:'no-api'|'clipboard-api'}`. demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:88-90. Producer contract: glass-ui/dist/useClipboard-D36OTaeT.js — returns `{ok:!1,reason:"no-api"}` when `navigator.clipboard?.writeText` is absent, `{ok:!1,reason:"clipboard-api"}` on rejection. Success path measured at p2.mjs: visibleFeedbackTextAfter:false.
```

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on `demo/scenes/Con` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Unguarded dot-path read: `read()` casts a possibly-`undefined` path result to `number` and `fmt()` calls `.toFixed` on it during render. One absent optional intermediate segment throws mid-render and unmounts the ENTIRE pane through the error boundary — and the boundary swallows it so completely that nothing reaches `console` or `pageerror`.

**Mechanism.** stringly-typed reflection layer — an `as number` cast manufacturing an invariant the type system explicitly denies

**Evidence.**

```
demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:57-86 (`readPath` returns undefined; `read` does `as number`; `fmt` does `v.toFixed(3)`); :66-73 (`writePath` has the mirror hole, walking through three unchecked casts). fmt boundary table measured in node: 0→"0", -0→"0", 0.5→"0.500", NaN→"NaN", Infinity→"Infinity", 1e21→"1e+21", undefined→THROWS, null→THROWS. Type permits the state: AuroraAtoms.zones is optional and the def is {key:"zones.count"} (AuroraPane.vue:103). Internal inconsistency: AuroraPane guards the same key 3 lines away — `atoms.zones?.arrangement ?? "composed"` (:74) and `atoms.zones?.count ?? 4` (:82).
```

**Reproduction.** INJECTED (labelled — not user-reachable through today's UI): `node scratchpad/csp/p4.mjs` sets the type-legal `config.zones = undefined` on the live reactive object at /#/atmosphere. Result: body text goes from the pane to "This panel hit an unexpected error. Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toFixed')", configConsoleStillMounted:false, rowsAfter:0, pageErrors:[], consoleNoise:[]. The empty error arrays explain why REPORT.json reads 0 console/page errors on both routes in all four Safari matrices — this failure class is invisible to the visual harness by construction.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the reflection layer. Both consumers already double-cast their typed config to nothing (`(cfg as unknown) as Record<string, unknown>` — BlobPane.vue:124, AuroraPane.vue:111), so BlobPane's 13-line `NumericAtomPath` mapped type guards only the key literals while the indexed object is fully untyped. Give `SliderDef` its own `get: () => number` / `set: (n:number) => void` (or a typed lens): the class becomes unrepresentable and `readPath`/`writePath`/the `as number`/both `as unknown as` casts all disappear — strictly less code.

### `design` · D-7 · design

**Defect.** A section heading and a control label are computed-identical (6/6 properties), the section heading is the same size as the row labels it groups, and the closed type matrix is breached in three roles.

**Mechanism.** VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:66-78 is a closed type matrix. Section heading must be text-heading/Plus Jakarta Sans — rendered Fira Code 16.4px caps. Control label must be text-small PJS non-bold — rendered Fira Code caps in the slot rows and PJS weight 500 in the well rows. Value must be text-mono-small or mono-caption — rendered text-micro 11px, neither token. Mono is thus louder as a heading (16.4px) than as the data it groups (11px), and FIELD vs HARMONY are indistinguishable in the frame.

### `design` · D-11 · design

**Defect.** The live readout has neither tabular figures nor reserved width, and infers precision from the value instead of the statically-known step — producing a ~27px live width jitter mid-drag on nearly every slider.

**Mechanism.** Precision derived from the value, not the def. Every BlobPane slider whose range contains an integer (warpAmp 0-1, eccentricity 0-0.5, noiseFreq 0.5-10.0, pulseFreq 0-2, specStrength 0-2, rimPower 1-5, iridescence/sssScale/coreGlow 0-1, pointerAttraction -1..1, stretch 0-1.5, tempo 0.25-2.5, ...) flips its readout between 5 chars and 1 char mid-drag — a ~80% width swing on a 33.9px element. `noiseFreq` step 0.1 renders `0.500`, two digits of false precision on 8 of 31 rows. No `unit` field exists, so `Merge (ms)` smuggles its unit into the label while `Hue Range` (degrees) has none, against VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:124 ("announce label, value, unit").

**Evidence.**

```
Live /#/blob: readout fontVariantNumeric "normal"; "3" = 6.8px, "0.220" = 33.9px, "0.038" = 33.9px; in-place swap "0.220"->"-0.0005" = 32.1 -> 43.7px (delta +11.6px). ConfigSliderPane.vue:84-86 `fmt(v) = Number.isInteger(v) ? String(v) : v.toFixed(3)`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:78: "Live numbers use tabular figures and reserve their widest legal representation so value changes never reflow the settled chassis."
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/chD-csp-probe2.mjs -> truncation.readoutWidthShift; chD-csp-probe.mjs -> reflow. Visually: drag Warp on /#/blob through 1.00.

**Proposed cure.** `SliderDef` declares `precision` (or derives it once from `step`) and `unit`; the readout gets font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums and a min-inline-size reserved from the widest legal string. Both belong on glass-ui's ConfiguratorRow value slot — VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:104 already assigns the axis composition ("label, unit, reserved live value, ...") to the producer.

### `design` · D-12 · design

**Defect.** The declared "ONE RHYTHM SOURCE" container clamp is measurably inert — rendered row height is identical at container widths differing by 2.03x — and it bypasses the producer's real sizing API with utility classes plus a :deep() correction.

**Mechanism.** The row content box (label line + gap-1.5 + 24px track + py-1) always exceeds the clamp, so the clamp never binds and the claim at :208-214 is false — the rhythm is fixed, not container-scaled, contrary to VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:33 law 7. The actual spacing comes from `class="gap-1.5 py-1"` (:142), replacing the producer's ladder, plus a `:deep()` descendant correction that VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:89 says W17 deletes.

**Evidence.**

```
ConfigSliderPane.vue:208-217 `min-block-size: clamp(2rem, 7cqi, 2.625rem)`. Measured (chD-csp-probe.mjs): /atmosphere container 1042px -> resolved 42px, rendered row 60.94px; /blob container 512px -> resolved 35.84px, rendered row 60.94px; /atmosphere 390px container 358px -> 32px, rendered 57.59px. distinctRowHeights = [60.9] on both desktop arms. Separately dataSize: null on every row, while glass-ui.css ships `.configurator-row[data-size=sm|md|lg]` with --configurator-row-gap-* / --configurator-row-py-* plus an @container style(--configurator-size) seam.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/chD-csp-probe.mjs -> compare desktop-atmosphere.row0 / desktop-blob.row0 / mobile-atmosphere.row0

**Proposed cure.** Delete :215-217 and :142. Pass the producer's `size` (or set --configurator-size once on .config-console) and let the producer's gap/padding ladder own the rhythm. If the rhythm must be container-scaled, that clamp belongs in the producer's --configurator-row-py-* tokens so every consumer inherits one law — which is what "ONE RHYTHM SOURCE" was meant to mean.

### `design` · D-16 · design

**Defect.** The prop contract erases types: both consumers must launder their real config through `as unknown as Record<string, unknown>`, and one spends a 13-line recursive mapped type reconstructing the safety the pane threw away.

**Mechanism.** The pane is generic over "any object addressed by any dot-path string" — the least typeable contract available — and every consumer pays for the generality. It also carries seven jobs in 252 lines with no encapsulation of any (Card shell, scroll host, dot-path resolver, number formatter, clipboard exporter, reset engine, slot host), which is edict 1 (no god modules) and edict 3 (KISS, no contrivance); the widest possible prop type is the symptom.

**Evidence.**

```
ConfigSliderPane.vue:41-52 types config and defaults as Record<string, unknown>. Four double-casts: AuroraPane.vue:111, :113; BlobPane.vue:124, :126. BlobPane.vue:36-48 defines `NumericAtomPath` — a 13-line recursive mapped type with a 24-line comment on two levels of `-?` modifier stripping — solely to restore key safety.
```

**Reproduction.** grep -n "as unknown" demo/scenes/atmosphere/AuroraPane.vue demo/scenes/blob/BlobPane.vue

**Proposed cure.** Make the pane generic over its config: `defineProps<{config: T; sections: SliderSection<T>[]; defaults: T}>()` with SliderDef<T>["key"] a keyof-derived dot-path union. BlobPane.vue:36-48 and all four casts then delete — a net subtraction of ~30 lines. Alternatively the D-8/D-9 split removes the "generic over any object" requirement entirely.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (pass 4, independent seat) · su` · C-31 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The slug-login field's programmatic focus is deterministically revoked 0.3 ms after it lands, by glass-ui's own layer focus-repair. On desktop, clicking Login opens a visible, non-inert login layer whose field never holds the caret — every typed keystroke is dropped, and Escape (bound to the input) does nothing either. SlugEditLayer.vue:20-22's nextTick focus is dead code at runtime.

**Mechanism.** Two nextTick-scheduled focus calls race; the producer's runs second, unconditionally, whenever the OUTGOING face contains document.activeElement — and the desktop Login button lives inside that face. The incoming face carries tabindex="-1" so it absorbs focus. (The mobile ⋮→Login path is unaffected and measured working — the trigger is a portaled reka menu item, outside the face, so no repair fires: `input value: "mobile-typed"`.)

**Evidence.**

```
Instrumented focus()-stack trace (scratchpad/p4-focus2.mjs): `+193.9ms .focus() on input[enter slug or token.] @ ... at /demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:29:25` → `+201.3ms focusin -> input` → `+201.6ms .focus() on div.dock-face.is-active @ ... at w (@mkbabb_glass-ui_dock.js:895:84)` → `+201.6ms focusout <- input`; final `{active:'div.dock-face.is-active', activeTabindex:'-1', inputIsActive:false}`. Producer source, dist/dock.js:892-896: `!n||!r||!n.contains(r)||(await nextTick(),(_(t)??document.body).focus?.())`. Live state of the layer at that moment: `{visibility:'visible',opacity:'1',pointerEvents:'auto',inertAncestor:false,w:160,h:23}`. Typing test: `input value: ""` after typing 'hello-there-friend-x'.
```

**Reproduction.** Desktop ≥1024px, anonymous session, http://localhost:9000/#/ → click Login → type. The field stays empty. Keyboard users can still reach it with exactly one Tab from the parked face (measured: Tab#1 -> input), so it is a silent focus loss, not a total lockout.

**Proposed cure.** Stop hand-focusing from inside the outgoing layer. Gestalt: the layer declares its entry focus and the layer machine honours it — glass-ui's w() should prefer an explicit target ([autofocus]/focusTarget on DockLayer) inside the incoming face over the face itself (glass-ui BH relay; same cure kills C-35). Demo-side interim: drive focus off the layer's own became-active edge, after the producer's repair, and retire the parent→child imperative poke Dock.vue:61 slugEditRef.value?.onStartSlugEdit().

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (pass 4, independent seat) · su` · C-32 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The dock's live backdrop sampler has never once succeeded. `data-backdrop-sample-state="unavailable"` / `reason="source-unavailable"` is re-stamped ~3.5x/s forever on every route; `--glass-backdrop-luma` stays unset (fallback 0), so `--glass-tint-strength` evaluates to its 4% floor permanently and the producer's adaptive-legibility tint (AA 20%) can never engage over the aurora field.

**Mechanism.** A design-system feature wired by CONVENTION (a data-attribute stamp) rather than by a prop, where the producer's resolver stopped honouring the convention across a major — verified once by reading, never by measuring. Live=true with source=null yields an infinite failing retry loop that writes DOM attributes at 3.5 Hz on the persistent chrome.

**Evidence.**

```
scratchpad/p4-idle.mjs, MutationObserver on nav.dock-band, 4 s idle: `total idle mutations in 4s: 42` — 14x data-backdrop-sample-state=unavailable, 14x -source=canvas, 14x -reason=source-unavailable, and nothing else. scratchpad/p4-backdrop.mjs on #/, #/palettes, #/blob (identical rows): `{"state":"unavailable","reason":"source-unavailable","sampledAttr":false,"luma":"0","tintStrength":"clamp( 4%, calc( 4% + (20% - 4%) * max( 0, ( 0 - 0.6 ) / (1 - 0.6) ) ), 20% )","tintFloor":"4%","tintAA":"20%","autoDiscoverWouldFind":true}`. Source: Dock.vue:132 passes no :background-canvas; dist/dock.js:715-718 always hands the sampler a getter; dist/dock.js:76-89 De() early-returns on the truthy getter so the documented `[data-glass-field-canvas] canvas, canvas[data-glass-field-canvas]` fallback is unreachable, while dist/dock.js:176's is-live predicate DOES use it; dist/dock.js:216 is the source-unavailable branch. Contradicted claim in the record: demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphereBoot.ts:40-48 ('auto-discovers THIS canvas as its backgroundCanvas and samples the live field').
```

**Reproduction.** Load any route, wait past boot, read the dock: `document.querySelector('.glass-dock').getAttribute('data-backdrop-sample-state')` === 'unavailable' and `getComputedStyle(dock).getPropertyValue('--glass-backdrop-luma')` === '0' — on 3/3 routes probed, and re-stamped ~14x per 4 s.

**Proposed cure.** Thread the canvas the App already owns: `<GlassDock :background-canvas="atmosphereCanvas">` (App.vue:9 ref, stamped data-glass-field-canvas at App.vue:16). Producer-side BH relay: De() must fall through to the document convention when the getter yields null, otherwise the stamp is decorative for every consumer in the constellation. No demo-local luminance shim — the ladder token is the producer's and the seam exists. Verify the cured state reaches `sampled` (see C-38: the field canvas is a 300x150 WebGL2 backing store; a blank readback would merely trade source-unavailable for sample-unavailable).

**Defect.** MT-F004's mechanism, named: the three login controls are sub-24px because SlugEditLayer passes `compact` to DockControl, which is the producer's explicit opt-out from the coarse-pointer 2.75rem touch floor — and the demo never sets the --dock-compact-control-* token hooks that its own sibling control already uses. The 160x20 slug input additionally has no accessible name (placeholder only, clipped by a fixed w-40).

It survived because nothing ever renders this layer (C-36).

Producer rule, dist/components/dock/styles/controls/touch-floor.css: `@media (pointer: coarse){ .dock-icon-button:not(.dock-icon-button--compact):not(:where(.glass-dock *)){ min-block-size: var(--dock-touch-target,2.75rem); min-inline-size: … } }` — the slug controls hit BOTH exclusions. Compact geometry: icon-button.css `.dock-icon-button--compact{ width:var(--dock-compact-control-size,auto); padding:var(--dock-compact-control-padding,0.25rem) }`. Measured live in the OPEN state at 390x844 isMobile+hasTouch (p4-focus4.mjs): `[{"l":"enter slug or token...","w":160,"h":20},{"l":"Switch to slug","w":23,"h":23},{"l":"Generate new slug","w":23,"h":23},{"l":"Cancel","w":23,"h":23}]`. ```

**Reproduction.** Open the login layer (click Login on desktop, or ⋮→Login on mobile) and measure the three DockControls and the input: 23x23 / 23x23 / 23x23 and 160x20, all < 24 CSS px, under a coarse pointer.

**Proposed cure.** Apply the T-36 idiom to the login controls: set `--dock-compact-control-padding` (and `--dock-compact-control-size: 2.75rem` under `(pointer: coarse)`) at the root of the slug layer's controls — root-level styling through the producer's own hook, not per-instance overrides, no new component. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (pass 4, independent seat) · su` · C-34 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The dock's layer machine is silent to assistive tech: every layer change parks focus on an unnamed, role-less div.dock-face[tabindex="-1"], and the entire band contains no live region in production — the only aria-live/status/alert element is the DEV-gated status lamp.

**Mechanism.** State changes are expressed purely visually (crossfade + inert toggling); no announcement channel and no named focus target exist, so the layer swap, the linkCopied flip (ProfileSection.vue:156 'Share color'→'Copied!'), the login result and the view switch are all unannounced.

**Evidence.**

```
Focus landings (p4-focus.mjs): Tools→`div.dock-face.is-active[lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)]`, Back→`div.dock-face.is-active[HomeToolsPickerAbout Log]`, Login→`div.dock-face.is-active[]`. Live-region census of nav.dock-band (p4-perf.mjs): `[ 'span[role=alert,live=null] "dev misconfigured — run `npm r"' ]` — DockStatusLamp.vue:13 is `v-if="lamp"` with `const isDev = import.meta.env.DEV`, so production has zero live regions. The face's only accessible text is the run-together textContent of the controls inside it.
```

**Reproduction.** Keyboard-activate any dock layer control (Tools, Back, Login) and read document.activeElement: an unnamed div with tabindex=-1, three times out of three. Then query the band for [aria-live],[role=status],[role=alert],[role=log] in a production build: empty.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (third independent pass on demo` · C-23 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The dock's slug-login error path is dead in three independent places: an unrendered `slugError` ref, an un-awaited async dispatch that makes the local catch AND the loading spinner unreachable, and a `setError` sink routed at a template ref that is never bound to a component that is never rendered. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/shell/dock/` · D-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `.dock-layer-grid` matches zero CSS rules — the class name asserts a grid that does not exist, so the inactive/leaving sub-layer's absolute positioning resolves against the whole dock face instead of the sub-grid.

**Mechanism.** The producer's stacking container is `.dock-layers { display:grid }`; the consumer invented a similar-sounding name with no rule behind it. Because `.dock-layer:not(.is-active){position:absolute;inset:0}` is inherited from the producer via a descendant selector, the missing `position:relative`/`display:grid` on the container silently redirects the containing block one level up.

**Evidence.**

```
ActionBarLayer.vue:101. Live probe walking every rule of every stylesheet: gridRuleCount == 0; getComputedStyle(.dock-layer-grid).display == "block"; .position == "static". Static cross-check: `grep -rn "dock-layer-grid" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/ demo/ src/` returns exactly one hit — ActionBarLayer.vue:101, the site that writes it. Measured consequence: the inactive layer's offsetParent is `dock-face is-active`, not the grid; the ActionToolbar sub-layer measures 184.0px wide when active and 447.5px when leaving, and ColorInput measures 447.5px when inactive vs 290.4px when active — each layer stretches to the full dock face whenever inactive, spilling left over the sibling Back control and DockSeparator.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/ console: `const g=document.querySelector('.dock-layer-grid'); getComputedStyle(g).display` -> "block"; `[...g.children].find(c=>!c.classList.contains('is-active')).offsetParent.className` -> "dock-face is-active".

**Proposed cure.** Subsumed by D-2 — DockCrossfade supplies `.dock-crossfade{position:relative;display:grid;isolation:isolate}` and grid-area-stacks its faces. Do NOT patch by adding a local `.dock-layer-grid{display:grid;position:relative}` rule; that would deepen the private-CSS coupling of D-4.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/shell/dock/` · D-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The component hand-writes the producer's private layer class vocabulary (`dock-layer`/`is-active`/`is-leaving`) nested inside a genuine producer `.dock-layer`, creating an undeclared name-based coupling to glass's internal CSS.

**Mechanism.** Coupling by class name to a producer's private stylesheet. Invisible to package.json, to typecheck, and to every test — a glass release renaming `.dock-layer` or tightening the selector to `>` breaks this component with no compile error and no failing test.

**Proposed cure.** D-2. `<DockLayer>` renders its own `.dock-face` host and never asks the consumer to author producer class names — the coupling becomes a typed component contract instead of a string.
