### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/shell/dock/` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `isAdminMode` is a one-way latch: the route watcher sets it TRUE and has no else-branch, and does not consult authentication. Any visitor landing on the public /#/atmosphere or /#/blob flips the dock into admin mode, and the false gold admin identity persists across every subsequent navigation until a full page reload.

**Mechanism.** Derived state (is this route an admin route, and is the user an admin) is stored as a ref and mutated by a partial watcher, so it can neither clear nor stay consistent with auth.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/composables/useDockAdminMode.ts:55-59 — `watch(() => viewManager.currentView.value, (view) => { if (adminViews.includes(view)) { isAdminMode.value = true; } })` with no else and no isAdminAuthenticated check. Consumed at DockViewSelect.vue:70 (`--dock-ring: isAdminMode ? var(--color-gold) : var(--accent-view)`) and :80 (`gold-shimmer-icon`). SHOT shots/safari-desktop-light/atmosphere.png shows the gold trigger icon beside a Login button.
```

**Reproduction.** 1) Load http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere unauthenticated. Live DOM read of .view-select-trigger: {"dockRing":"var(--color-gold)","iconClass":"lucide lucide-sparkles-icon … gold-shimmer-icon"}. 2) Pick "Home" from the menu. Re-read: {"hash":"#/","triggerText":"Home","dockRing":"var(--color-gold)","iconClass":"lucide lucide-house-icon lucide-house w-6 h-6 shrink-0 gold-shimmer-icon","goldShimmer":true} — still gold, still never authenticated.

**Proposed cure.** isAdminMode is not state: `computed(() => isAdminAuthenticated.value && currentRoute.meta.admin === true)`. Derived, it cannot latch, cannot desync from auth, and cannot be entered by an anonymous deep link; the ref, the watcher and one mutator all disappear.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/shell/dock/` · D-7 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Every `update:modelValue` reka emits is a committed history-pushing router.push. There is no highlight-vs-commit distinction, because a Select (a value control) is carrying navigation; reka's SelectTrigger implements native-<select> semantics in which arrow keys CYCLE THE VALUE when focus sits on the trigger.

**Mechanism.** A value-change channel wired directly to a destructive commit, with no separation between moving the highlight and choosing a destination — the category error at the root of the component.

**Evidence.**

```
DockViewSelect.vue:55 forwards the raw value change (`@update:model-value="(id) => emit('update:modelValue', id as string)"`); Dock.vue:174 binds it to onViewChange; useDockAdminMode.ts:66-74 calls viewManager.switchView(id as ViewId) → useViewManager.ts:78 router.push. **Reproduction.** CONFIRMED-ONCE, NEEDS RE-VERIFICATION ON AN UNCONTENDED BROWSER. Steps: load http://localhost:9000/#/, mouse-click the "Select view" combobox, confirm document.activeElement is the combobox, press ArrowDown once → location.hash becomes #/palettes while aria-expanded stays "true". The dev server is driven concurrently by other workflow seats (a foreign ?probe=3 query landed in my page mid-run), and a repeat on a fresh load instead left document.activeElement as BODY with the listbox open — focus placement after pointer-open was observed in three states (combobox / option / BODY), which is itself what makes the arrow path hazardous. The MECHANISM above is source-certain regardless.

Rows become <a href="#/browse"> in a menu/list — arrow keys move focus and commit nothing, Enter/click navigates, ⌘-click and middle-click finally work (today no href exists anywhere in the product's nav), and the current row is aria-current="page" (which HAS paint conventions, curing D-4). glass-ui already ships DropdownMenu primitives, so this is reuse, not a new component.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt: demo/shell/dock/Ac` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The double-rAF settle stamp writes `settled = true` without re-checking `visible`, so on 12/12 boots the slot rests as `is-settled` WITHOUT `is-visible`; the next arrival then releases the T-29 clip from frame 0 of the grow, painting 45.4px of control outside its own grid track.

**Mechanism.** A settle LATCH written from two independent deferred writers (a 2-frame-old rAF and a transitionend), neither of which re-validates the predicate it depends on, instead of a settle DERIVATION from state that is already in the DOM.

**Evidence.**

```
ActionBarToggle.vue:60-65 — the inner rAF sets `slotLive.value = true; settled.value = true;` with no re-read of `visible` and no cancel handle. STALE_boot_hit_rate: webkit {runs:6, stale:6}, chromium {runs:6, stale:6} — resting class list on a plain load of /#/browse is `action-bar-toggle-slot is-live is-settled` in all 12 runs. `is-live` proves the rAF branch ran; `settled` cannot come from onSlotSettled (ActionBarToggle.vue:71 assigns `settled.value = visible`, which is false) — the rAF at line 63 is the only possible writer. A/B control on the same page, identical arrival sampled at t=70ms: arm A (stale, pre-state `is-live is-settled`) → overflow VISIBLE, clip 62.1px, paint 107.5px, 45.4px overpaint; arm B (healthy, pre-state `is-live`) → overflow HIDDEN, clip 46.2px, correctly clipped. Frame samples arm A: t=30ms trackW=0px clipW=0 paintW=104.5 spill=121.5px; t=209ms trackW=93.3 spill=29.0px. This violates the component's own header invariant at lines 30-31 ('the stamp drops the moment presence drops') and lines 137-142 ('the clip returns ... during any width transition').
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-actionbartoggle/probe/C2-stale-settle-repro.mjs webkit (and chromium) — 6 fresh loads of http://localhost:9000/#/browse each, 6/6 stale on both. Harm A/B: node probe/C2-ab-control.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** Delete `settled` as an independently-written latch and let CSS own the clip release from state already in the DOM (`is-visible` + not-animating), which removes both writers and the whole race class. If the ref must stay: keep one `armFrame` id, `cancelAnimationFrame(armFrame)` on every watcher entry and in `onScopeDispose`, and guard the inner callback with `if (!visible) return;` before stamping.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt: demo/shell/dock/Ac` · C-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `aria-pressed` and `.is-active` are set only while the button sits under `aria-hidden="true"` + `inert` + `opacity: 0`, so the toggle's state is unobservable to both AT and sighted users; activation also destroys focus with no restoration and no live announcement.

**Mechanism.** A `role=button` + `aria-pressed` toggle pattern applied to what is structurally a disclosure that swaps a region — and hand-rolled in the consumer instead of using glass-ui DockControl's own `active` prop, which already emits aria-pressed + data-active + the glass-capsule register.

**Evidence.**

```
ActionBarToggle.vue:89 (`:class="{ 'is-active': active }"`) and :91 (`:aria-pressed="active"`). `active === true` is exactly the condition under which DockLayerGroup swaps the main layer out. Measured at the instant aria-pressed is "true": {btnAriaPressed:"true", btnClass:"... dock-tools-btn is-active", btnCS:{background-color:"color(srgb 0.994 0.96 0.926 / 0.8)", pointer-events:"none"}, hiddenAncestor:"dock-face"} with that face carrying inert + aria-hidden="true". Producer CSS node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/crossfade.css: `.dock-face { opacity: 0; pointer-events: none; }` and `.dock-face.is-leaving { opacity: calc(1 - var(--dock-t)); }` — the active register paints only during the ~300ms exit crossfade. Focus trace: B_tab_reached_tools → BUTTON.dock-tools-btn; B_after_enter_activeEl → DIV.dock-face is-active (unnamed, roleless, text "lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)"); B_after_back_activeEl → DIV.dock-face is-active (text "HomeToolsPickerAbout Login  @mbabb"). Focus is never returned to the trigger and no aria-live announces the swap.
```

**Reproduction.** Load http://localhost:9000/#/, expand the dock, Tab to `.dock-tools-btn`, press Enter; read `document.activeElement` and the button's `closest('[aria-hidden="true"]')`. Captured in probe-abt steps B_tab_reached_tools / B_after_enter_snap / B_after_enter_activeEl / B_after_back_activeEl.

**Proposed cure.** Speak the producer's API (edict 4): pass `:active` to DockControl and delete the hand-rolled class + aria-pressed. Re-shape the ARIA to the real behaviour — `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls` pointing at the action-bar layer — and add a focus contract: move focus to the action-bar layer's Back control on open, restore it to the Tools trigger on close.

**Defect.** `isAdminMode` is a latch: it is set true by a one-directional watcher and never cleared on the anonymous path, so one deep link disables the entire per-view chromatic voice for the rest of the session and tells an unauthenticated visitor they are an admin.

**Mechanism.** derived state stored in a `ref` and mutated by a one-directional watcher. There is no state here; there is only the route.

**Evidence.**

```
useDockAdminMode.ts:55-59 sets true only; the only clears are toggleAdminMode() (its row is `v-if="pm.isAdminAuthenticated.value"`, DockViewSelect.vue:122 — absent for anonymous users) and a non-immediate `watch(isAdminAuthenticated)` at :62 that cannot fire when the value was already false. The seed at :32 reads currentView at setup, before router.isReady() resolves (useViewManager.ts:41). Measured (probe/probe-dvs.mjs): "P2 after switching to Home": {"text":"Home","styleAttr":"--dock-ring: var(--color-gold); …","goldIcon":true}; "P3 after switching to Gradient": {"text":"Gradient","styleAttr":"--dock-ring: var(--color-gold); …","goldIcon":true}; control "P4 control fresh /#/gradient": {"styleAttr":"--dock-ring: var(--accent-view);","goldIcon":false}. Consumers in this file: :80 keeps gold-shimmer-icon on the glyph, :83 withholds `color: var(--accent-view)` from it.
```

**Reproduction.** Load http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere anonymously, then pick `Home` from the dock menu: the trigger icon stays gold and never returns to the view accent for the rest of the session.

**Proposed cure.** `const isAdminMode = computed(() => VIEW_MAP[currentView.value].group === "admin" && isAdminAuthenticated.value)`. The latch, both watchers and the ref all die; the flag becomes unfalsifiable by construction.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/shell/dock/Doc` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

```
demo/shell/dock/DockStatusLamp.vue:13 `v-if="lamp"`; the `unavailable` face returns `role:"status"` at demo/shell/dock/status-lamp.ts:57-60. The repo's own e2e proves the region never pre-exists: e2e/smoke/oracles/o22-status-lamp.spec.ts:40 `await expect(page.locator(".dock-status-lamp")).toHaveCount(0);` under a healthy backend, then :56-60 asserts it appears already carrying role and variant. Count 0 → count 1 with content.
```

**Reproduction.** Read e2e/smoke/oracles/o22-status-lamp.spec.ts:40 and :56-60 — the two assertions together establish the transition shape. Live: run the o22 spec's route-abort setup (page.route(/\/(colors|sessions|palettes|users)\//, abort 'connectionrefused')) and observe the region materialise fully-formed.

**Proposed cure.** Mount the region permanently and toggle only its text. The variant space makes this clean: `misconfigured` can only latch at module-eval (client.ts:34 → availability.ts:151-164, once, before mount) and markApiUnreachable refuses to overwrite it (availability.ts:169), so the faces are temporally disjoint. A permanently-mounted `role="status"` region with text `lamp?.label ?? **Defect.** The entire dock relayouts on every keystroke: the field declares no intrinsic width bound, so the dock's width tracks the typed string 1:1.

**Mechanism.** content-driven intrinsic sizing inside a shrink-to-fit container, so a per-keystroke text change becomes a per-keystroke layout+paint of a backdrop-filter glass surface

**Evidence.**

```
frames/probe-3.json typingReflow, 13 characters typed one at a time: inputWidths 61.5 -> 198.8, dockWidths 179.5 -> 316.8, inputWidthSpan 137.3, dockWidthSpan 137.3 — identical spans, 11.4px per character. Mechanism read from source: ColorInput.vue:16 `class="color-input w-full block ..."` on a contenteditable inside ColorInput's div.grid.grid-cols-1 (:2), inside ActionBarLayer's div.dock-layer-grid.flex-1 (:98). `w-full` against a shrink-to-fit chain resolves to max-content; the min-w-0 at ActionBarLayer.vue:118 caps the minimum, never the maximum.
```

**Reproduction.** frames/probe-3.json (controlled capture 2026-07-27 13:30). Attribution stated precisely in the report: the measurement is the D-seat's, the mechanism is read from this component's source — the field is the only element in the chain declaring a content-driven width.

**Proposed cure.** Give the field a fixed inline size in `ch` — its font is already monospace Fira Code (frames/probe-1.json A-rest-light.styles.fontFamily) — and let it scroll internally. The text-ellipsis + mask machinery at :16 and :300-306 already exists to handle overflow and is currently never exercised at rest because the box grows instead. This also fixes the usability half: the send button stops sliding 11.4px right per character.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shell/dock/laye` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `.dock-layer-grid` is a class with zero CSS rules anywhere; the container is display:block/position:static, so the producer's `position:absolute; inset:0` on the inactive layer resolves against `.dock-face` and the hidden layer is stretched across the whole dock face.

**Mechanism.** A class name copied from the producer's vocabulary that the producer never defined; the stacking contract (display:grid + a positioned container) is therefore absent, and the absolutely-positioned inactive layer escapes to the nearest positioned ancestor.

**Evidence.**

```
Live CSSOM walk of every rule in every stylesheet: gridRuleCount 0; getComputedStyle → display "block", position "static"; grid rect x=584.7 w=184.0. Both children report offsetParent "dock-face". Measured boxes: ActionToolbar active x=584.7 w=184.0 h=40; ColorInput inactive x=519.7 w=400.5 h=46; ColorInput active x=584.7 w=282.5; ActionToolbar leaving/inactive x=519.7 w=400.5. Overhang: 65.0 px left of the grid, 151.5 px right. Static: `grep -rn "dock-layer-grid" . --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=docs` → one hit, ActionBarLayer.vue:101 (the site that writes it); `grep -rn "dock-layer-grid" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/` → no output. The producer's real stacking container is `.dock-layers { display:grid; min-width:0 }` in dist/components/dock/styles/layers.css — a different class.
```

**Reproduction.** Console at /#/ with the action bar open: `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.dock-layer-grid')).display` → "block"; `[...g.children].find(c=>!c.classList.contains('is-active')).offsetParent.className` → "dock-face".

**Proposed cure.** Subsumed by C-2 — DockCrossfade supplies `.dock-crossfade{display:grid;position:relative;isolation:isolate}` and grid-area-stacks its faces. Do NOT patch by adding a local `.dock-layer-grid{display:grid;position:relative}` rule; that deepens the private-CSS coupling of C-4.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shell/dock/laye` · C-6 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `toolbarMode` is never reconciled when `canProposeName` flips false — the component can sit in "propose" for a color that cannot be proposed, and the exposed writable ref lets any caller enter that state while bypassing the entry gate.

ActionBarLayer.vue:37 gates entry on `actionBar.canProposeName.value`; nothing gates remaining. The file's only `watch` is line 71 (inside the shim, on `activeLayer`) — no watch on canProposeName. `canProposeName` is `!findCustomName(currentXYZString)` (demo/color-session/useColorNameResolution.ts:66-70), so it flips false the instant a proposal succeeds — the exact transition C-5 fails to report — and on any external color change. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design` · D-05 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The pressed state has zero rendered pixels and is pruned from the accessibility tree — a toggle whose 'on' is unobservable in both channels.

**Mechanism.** The only state in which the control reads 'on' is a state in which the control is not rendered. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 requires explicit role/name/state; §3 law 4 forbids the dock's state changes moving the scene.

**Evidence.**

```
Dock.vue:113 sets activeLayer='action-bar' exactly when actionBarLayerActive is true; glass-ui layers.css gives the non-active layer opacity:0; visibility:hidden; pointer-events:none — and the main layer hosts ActionBarToggle. Measured after clicking Tools (abt-probe-cr.json → A….active): ariaPressed="true", cls contains "is-active", and the live nav ariaSnapshot contains only Back / Reset / Copy CSS / Seed from palette — pressedInAx=false. Geometry corollary: while 'pressed' the control's rect is x790.6 w104.5 while the dock pill is x627.5 w185.0 (82.6px outside its own dock); dock rest x473.7 w492.6 → active x627.5 w185.0 = dx +153.8px, dw -307.6px, unanimated.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/.../abt-probe.mjs matrix A — after page.click('[aria-label="Toggle action bar"]'), re-read the element's attributes and page.locator('nav').first().ariaSnapshot().

**Proposed cure.** Either the toggle survives into the action-bar layer as the pressed seat that returns you (deleting the redundant `Back` at Dock.vue:154 and the whole two-arrow motif), or it drops aria-pressed and becomes what it behaves like — a one-way aria-expanded/aria-controls disclosure. Parent-seat ruling.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design` · D-06 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** On eleven of fifteen routes the control is a named ghost: 0 painted pixels, a full accessible name in the AT tree, and programmatically focusable.

**Mechanism.** 'Absent' was implemented as 'still mounted, just transparent and clipped'. opacity:0 + a 0px grid column removes it from sight and tab order but not from the accessibility tree, and element.focus() still succeeds — so any focus-restoration path can park focus on an invisible control (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.1).

**Evidence.**

```
/#/browse (abt-probe-cr.json → E-desktop-browse-absent): toolsPresent=true, toolsBox={w:104.5,h:32}, slot grid-template-columns="0px" opacity="0", inner overflow="hidden", tabindex="-1", clickable={hitIsSelf:false, focusable:TRUE}. Live nav ariaSnapshot on that route contains: `- button "Toggle action bar": - img - text: Tools - img`. Routes where visible is true: /#/generate, /#/gradient, /#/mix (usePaneRouter.ts:191,203,215) and /#/ (ColorPicker.vue:315) — the other 11 of 15 render the ghost.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/.../abt-probe.mjs matrix E — goto /#/browse, then page.locator('nav').first().ariaSnapshot() and in-page t.focus(); document.activeElement===t.

**Proposed cure.** Absence is v-if. Dock.vue:182 already computes hasAnyActionBar and passes it down as a styling prop instead of using it as a mount condition. With D-01's transform-based presence nothing requires the element to stay mounted.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design` · D-07 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The visible label is keyed to viewport width, so 200% zoom and every phone reduce the control to an unlabelled tinted glyph; and `compact` opts the control out of the producer's coarse-pointer 44px target floor.

**Mechanism.** A breakpoint fork (isDesktop = min-width:1024px, Dock.vue:71) used as a content gate rather than container-scaled layout, plus opting into a producer variant whose defined semantics include forfeiting the coarse-pointer floor.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured: desktop 1440 → 104.5x32, label "Tools", arrow 12x12, separator 1x27.5. 200% zoom (720 CSS px @2dpr) → 32x32, toolsLabelText=null, arrow 0x0, separator display:none. Mobile 390 → 33.3x33.3, label null, arrow 0x0. Confirmed visually in shots/zoom-200-desktop/gradient.png: the dock reads [rainbow ⌄] [bare magenta brush] [Gradient|Palettes] [⋮]. Producer floor: glass-ui/.../controls/touch-floor.css `@media (pointer: coarse) { .dock-icon-button:not(.dock-icon-button--compact):not(:where(.glass-dock *)) { min-block-size: var(--dock-touch-target, 2.75rem) …` — --compact is EXPLICITLY excluded; DockControl's own typing promises 'the HIT CELL stays the full --dock-control-size (≥44px on coarse)'. Measured 33.3x33.3 = 57% of 44x44 area. REPORT.json's smallTapTargets threshold is sub-24px so it passes silently on all four mobile rows.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/.../abt-probe.mjs matrices F (720x450 @2dpr) and I (390x844, isMobile, hasTouch) — read toolsBox, toolsLabelText, toolsSvgBoxes, seps.

**Proposed cure.** shape="tab" is auto-sized and label-bearing at every width — drop the isDesktop prop entirely and let the label live or wrap by container query. If the label genuinely cannot fit at 312px of dock aperture, the icon-only fallback must supply a visible boundary and meet the coarse floor, which shape="icon" WITHOUT compact does for free.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design` · D-08 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The focus indicator is a 1.65:1 hairline coloured by the user's own live seed, with outline-style: none; and in forced-colors the control has no boundary at all.

**Mechanism.** Producer control whose focus affordance is a low-alpha shadow rather than an outline, tinted from the live seed so its contrast is a function of whatever colour the user happens to be editing — an unguarded, user-variable focus indicator.

**Evidence.**

```
Clean keyboard focus, mouse parked at (20,700) (abt-probe2.json → focus): matchesFV=true, outlineStyle="none" (outlineWidth 3px declared then killed by .dock-icon-button{outline:none}), boxShadow = color(srgb 0.665504 0.000101 0.261748 / 0.3) 0 0 0 2px + /0.15 0 0 8px. Composited over the measured dock paper L 0.5131 that ring is 1.65:1 — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 requires ≥3:1. abt-focus.png shows a faint pink whisper at 2x DPR. Forced-colors (Chromium forcedColors:"active", abt-probe-cr.json → G.rest): background-color rgba(255,255,255,0), box-shadow none, no border — bare text, while Login/@mbabb (Button primitives) retain theirs. Coverage note: shots/forced-colors-desktop/*.png were captured on WebKit which ignores forcedColors emulation and are NOT forced-colors witnesses.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/.../abt-probe2.mjs — page.mouse.move(20,700); blur; Tab x2; read getComputedStyle(document.activeElement).{outlineStyle,boxShadow}; composite the ring colour at its alpha over the measured paper luminance and compute WCAG contrast.

**Proposed cure.** Producer-owned focus ring at the root (shape="tab" inherits .dock-tab-button's), never seed-derived; ≥3:1 against the dock in both schemes and a non-colour delta under forced colors.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-5 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** ~2.04s trailing debounce before any feedback, no live preview while typing at human cadence, and complete silence when the same invalid string is retried.

**Mechanism.** A trailing debounce an order of magnitude past the interaction-feedback threshold, combined with a stale-input dedup cache guarding a pure function, and an error truth that lives only on a 2s timer.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:92 `debounce(parseAndSetColor, 2000)`; :62 `if (!input || input === previousInvalid) return;`; :57 error auto-clears after 2000ms. Four measured live trials — T1 fresh `lab()` → badge at 2037ms; T2 SAME `lab()` retried → badge NEVER; T3 different `zzz(` → 2048ms; T4 `lab()` again after previousInvalid changed → 2041ms. Separately: driving the field at a 900ms cadence for 4s produced no badge at all, because every keystroke resets the 2000ms trailing timer.
```

**Reproduction.** At http://localhost:9000/#/ with the colour input open and focused: type `lab()` and wait — the badge appears at ~2.04s and vanishes 2s later. Now clear and type `lab()` again — nothing ever appears. Separately, type `oklch(0.7 0.1 200)` at roughly one character per second: zero live colour preview for the entire 18-character entry.

**Proposed cure.** Leading-edge debounce at ~120-200ms for the live preview; derive the error state from the current value so it PERSISTS while the value is invalid rather than flashing on a timer; delete `previousInvalid` entirely — it is a cache guarding a pure function and it is the mechanism that silences the natural human retry loop. PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-08 already rules this family ADD-AFFORDANCE.

Swallow site demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:63-89 (`try { parseColor(input) } catch { previousInvalid = input; if (!initialParse) flashParseError(); }`). **Defect.** The Crown indicator: its hover magnification never animates (transition names `transform` while Tailwind v4 writes the `scale` longhand), the hover is desktop-only, and its tooltip hangs off a non-focusable <svg> so keyboard and touch users can never read it.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D2-06 · CHALLENGE-D

**Mechanism.** useViewAccents resolves each view token through a gamut-map + WCAG-3:1 contrast re-guard; in the dark scheme the guard drives L to 0.958 and collapses C to 0.021, so hue becomes imperceptible. DockViewSelect.vue:40-42 already excised the per-row hue legend for carrying 'near-zero discriminative information' and then kept the identical mechanism on the trigger, ring and seal ('R1 SURVIVES', line 47) — the survivor now carries strictly less information than the deleted one.

Same probe: --accent-live light = oklch(47.118925176164% 0.188447570516 9.83402284231deg) — identical to --accent-view (viewSchema.ts picker accentHueShift:0). Rendered: scratchpad/D-dock-light.png (Login = crimson bold text in a crimson-bordered pill) vs scratchpad/D-dock-dark.png (Login and @mbabb are two identical dark slabs with white text).
```

**Reproduction.** node D-dock-probe4.mjs — two contexts colorScheme light/dark at 1440x900 on /#/, read getComputedStyle(documentElement) --accent-view/--accent-live and the computed color of .view-select-trigger svg, .dock-tools-btn svg/span and the Login button's color/borderColor.

**Proposed cure.** Stop encoding view identity as hue. Dock.vue:255-262 already argues the glyph is the stronger continuity carrier ('the same view icon exists at both morph endpoints… a stronger continuity read than a 1px rim') — finish that argument, delete accentHueShift and the --accent-view-<id> token family, and give the auth action its primacy through the design system's own primary-button variant, which is scheme-stable.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D2-07 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** RTL: the @mbabb wordmark bidi-reorders to `mbabb@`, and the dock's two directional affordances (Tools ArrowRight / Back ArrowLeft) do not mirror, so the enter/exit motif is inverted wholesale.

**Mechanism.** A handle beginning with '@' is a neutral-then-Latin run; in an RTL paragraph direction the neutral leading '@' resolves to the right of the Latin run. No dir="ltr"/unicode-bidi:isolate wrapper. Separately, the layer-swap affordance is drawn with physical arrow glyphs while its meaning ('forward into the layer' / 'back out') is logical.

**Evidence.**

```
docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/rtl-desktop/picker.png — the dock renders `mbabb@ | ← Login | → Tools 🖌 | 🏠 Home ⌄`; shots/rtl-mobile/picker.png shows the same wordmark break. Sources: ProfileSection.vue:140 (@mbabb text, no bidi isolation), ActionBarToggle.vue:103 (ArrowRight), Dock.vue:154 (ArrowLeft, 'Back'). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1: 'CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose'; 'chrome, navigation and layout follow logical inline/block direction'.
```

**Reproduction.** Open docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/rtl-desktop/picker.png and read the dock band; or re-run states.mjs matrix rtl-desktop (documentElement.setAttribute('dir','rtl') post-load, per its MT-F022 fix #1).

**Proposed cure.** dir="ltr" / unicode-bidi:isolate on @mbabb and on the slug pill (same family — ProfileSection.vue:75, MobileMenuDropdown.vue:50). Replace the two physical arrows with one logical chevron primitive that flips with `direction`: there are exactly two instances and they must always agree, so they should be one component, not two icon imports.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D2-08 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Three visible dividers for four visible seats — a line between every adjacent pair — in a row where every one of those four items already draws its own capsule seat.

**Mechanism.** Each dock sub-component ships its own DockSeparator as local furniture, so the count is the sum of independent decisions rather than one composition decision. The maximum possible duplication (n−1 lines for n seats) is reached exactly because no one owns the row.

**Evidence.**

```
D-dock-probe5.mjs·A at 1440x900: separators:7 in the nav subtree, visibleSeparators:3. Rendered scratchpad/D-dock-light.png: [Home ⌄] | [🖌 Tools →] | [Login] | [@mbabb]. Sources: ProfileSection.vue:49 AND :123 (a separator on both sides of the auth block), ActionBarToggle.vue:82. PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-05 terminal verb REMOVE/KEEP and §5 law 4: 'A divider is retained only when grouping would be ambiguous without it. Spacing plus material already expressing the same boundary makes the line duplicative.'
```

**Reproduction.** node D-dock-probe5.mjs — count nav .dock-separator total vs those with rect>0 and not inside [inert], at 1440x900 on /#/.

**Proposed cure.** Zero dividers in the main layer; the capsule seats already group and the dock's own gap token supplies the rhythm. Separator ownership moves to the layer composition (Dock.vue), never to the leaf components — a leaf cannot know whether its boundary is ambiguous.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D2-09 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Five operable height rungs (22/28/32/40/44) inside one dock, and ActionBarToggle's source comment asserts its box 'lands at the sibling controls' 2.5rem height' when the measured height is 32px and the named siblings are 40px.

**Mechanism.** ActionBarToggle.vue:155 sets `--dock-compact-control-padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem` — a consumer re-deriving the producer's box model from padding instead of consuming a height/density token. Padding-derived sizing cannot land on a target height because it does not know the content box. Violates PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 7 (glyph size, target size and reservation are separate quantities) and PR-12.

**Evidence.**

```
D-dock-probe5.mjs·A main layer at 1440: Select view 32 | Toggle action bar 32 | Login 28 | @mbabb 28. D-dock-probe3.mjs other layers: Save edit / Cancel edit / Back / Open color input = 40; action buttons = 32; slug controls = 22; mobile Back = 44. Claim under test: ActionBarToggle.vue:147-153 '…the box lands at the sibling controls' 2.5rem height' (2.5rem = 40px). Measured 32px — 8px wrong.
```

**Reproduction.** node D-dock-probe5.mjs — map every non-inert nav button with rect>0 to its accessible name and rounded height, at 1440x900 on /#/; then node D-dock-probe3.mjs for the other layers' heights.

**Proposed cure.** One dock control rung declared once as a producer token (a `density` prop / --dock-control-size) and consumed by every seat; the compact register is for genuinely secondary glyphs and must still clear 24px. Delete the --dock-compact-control-padding override. And delete the assertion in the comment: a comment that states a measurement must either be true or not exist.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D2-10 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** A dock layer swap jolts the pill 81px sideways and shrinks it 162px, unanimated — the persistent chrome jumps on a single click of Login.

**Mechanism.** GlassDock is instantiated with :fit-content="true" (Dock.vue:132) while hosting four DockLayers of very different intrinsic widths as grid-area:1/1 siblings. fit-content therefore tracks whichever layer is active, making the dock's inline size a property of the layer rather than of the dock.

**Evidence.**

```
D-dock-probe3.mjs at 1440x900: main layer dock {x:484.3, w:471.5, h:62}; slug-edit layer dock {x:565.5, w:309.0, h:62}. Δx = +81.2px, Δw = −162.5px. glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/crossfade.css cross-fades opacity only ('.dock-crossfade > .dock-face {opacity:0} … .is-active {opacity:1}'), so the box change is instantaneous. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3 law 4: the dock owns a reserved band and its expanded/collapsed/mounted states do not move the scene.
```

**Reproduction.** node D-dock-probe3.mjs (matrix B) — 1440x900, goto /#/, read .glass-dock rect, click Login, wait, read .glass-dock rect again.

**Proposed cure.** The dock's inline size is a property of the dock. Either size the container to the max of its layers (they are already coincident grid siblings, so `grid-template-columns: max-content` over all faces gives it for free), or drive width on the producer's morph spring so the change is a motion rather than a jump. Drop :fit-content on a multi-layer dock.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D2-16 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** CARRIED AND SHARPENED from r1 D-5: the open view menu has zero visual selected-state marking in either scheme, and the one lawfully coloured row (Palettes) therefore impersonates the selection.

**Mechanism.** hide-indicator strips the producer's SelectItem indicator gutter and the weight marker was deleted at P4-R4, leaving selection expressed only through aria-selected. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1: 'Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only' — here selection is not even colour, it is nothing; §4.2's ColorSpaceSelector rule ('deletes hide-indicator and consumes the sole producer SelectItem indicator/gutter') is the same mechanism, unapplied here. Menu rows are also Fraunces (DockViewSelect.vue:91), against §4's 'control or label, INCLUDING dropdown options → Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold'.

**Evidence.**

D-dock-probe7.mjs, both schemes: all 7 options report fontWeight "400", backgroundColor "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" and one <svg> child each (the view icon, not an indicator); only Home carries aria-selected "true". Rendered scratchpad/D-viewmenu-light.png: Home is typographically identical to Browse/Extract/Mix/Generate/Gradient, and the only visually marked row is Palettes (the Q5-sanctioned pastel ramp). Sources: DockViewSelect.vue:97 and :127 set hide-indicator on every SelectItem; :99-109 records that the font-semibold marker was retired.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-05 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Every keystroke resizes the dock (137.3 px of travel while typing one 13-character colour name), and because the field grows instead of clipping, the mask/ellipsis/text-center apparatus — the most bespoke CSS in the file — is unreachable dead code.

**Mechanism.** unreserved content-sized field inside a reserved band

**Evidence.**

```
Measured (frames/probe-3.json, typing `rebeccapurple` char by char): input width 61.5 -> 198.8 px (span 137.3); dock width 179.5 -> 316.8 px (span 137.3, 1:1). Measured (frames/probe-1.json, C-focus-dark.longValue) for a 46-char value: {scrollW:586, clientW:586, overflowing:false}. Dead declarations: ColorInput.vue:16 (overflow-hidden, text-ellipsis, whitespace-nowrap, text-center), :300-301 (mask-image, --input-action-width:2.5rem), :303-306 (:focus mask cancel). Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:30 (§3 law 4 'the dock owns a reserved band... do not move the scene'), :78 (§4 'reserve their widest legal representation so value changes never reflow the settled chassis').
```

**Reproduction.** Open the field, select all, type `rebeccapurple` one character at a time and watch the dock pill collapse to ~61 px then inflate 137 px; measure `.dock-face` width per keystroke.

**Proposed cure.** Give the field a reserved `inline-size` sized to the widest legal serialization (`color(display-p3 ...)`) plus `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`; the band stops moving and the mask/ellipsis/text-center machinery can then be deleted outright rather than kept as dead ornament.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-06 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Re-submitting the same invalid string produces no feedback whatsoever — no error, no success, no change — because a memo short-circuits ahead of the try/catch.

**Mechanism.** transient-only truth plus a memo that suppresses the retry signal

**Evidence.**

```
Source: demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:62 `if (!input || input === previousInvalid) return;` returns before flashParseError() (`previousInvalid` set at :85). Measured (scratchpad/DD-probe4.mjs, guarded on aria-label==="Enter a CSS color"): submit1_badge true; badgeGoneAfter2s true; textAfter2s "oklch()"; submit2_badge false; submit2_badge_late false; pageErrors []. Debounce is 2000 ms (useColorParsing.ts:92).
```

**Reproduction.** Open the field -> select all -> type `oklch()` -> Enter (badge appears) -> wait 2.4 s (badge gone, text still `oklch()`) -> press Enter again -> nothing happens, ever.

**Proposed cure.** The parse verdict must be derived state on the current input, not a one-shot timer with an invalid-input memo. Recompute validity on every commit; clear it on correction, not on a clock.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-09 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The Crown reveal animation cannot run: the inline `animation: crown-appear ...` in the template names a keyframe that Vue's scoped-style compiler renamed away, so the entire four-stop gold choreography is dead.

```

Served CSS (curl of the Vite style URL, scoped=55dadc03) contains only `@keyframes crown-appear-55dadc03`. Live CSSOM (frames/probe-1.json): crownKeyframeNames: ["crown-appear-55dadc03"] — no un-suffixed name exists. The `:key="crownKey"` remount (demo/color-session/useColorNameResolution.ts:64) exists solely to restart an animation that cannot start.

**Reproduction.** curl 'http://localhost:9000/@fs/<repo>/demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue?vue&type=style&index=0&scoped=55dadc03&lang.css' | grep crown  -> only `crown-appear-55dadc03`. Then in the live page, walk document.styleSheets for KEYFRAMES rules matching /crown/ -> same single suffixed name.

**Proposed cure.** Move the animation declaration into the scoped `<style>` block (a `.crown-appear` class on the element) so the compiler rewrites the name, and delete the inline style attribute — which is also an owner-edict-5 per-instance override.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-17 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Propose-mode success and failure are both silent: failure is a `console.warn`, success emits nothing, and the comment 'Signal parent to exit propose mode' describes an emit that does not exist — the SFC has no defineEmits at all.

ColorInput.vue:230-247: `await session.ensureSession()` (silently mints an account), `catch (e: any) { console.warn("[ColorInput] Failed to propose name:", e?.message); }`, and the comment at :238 above a line that only rewrites innerText. Repo grep: no `defineEmits` in the file. glass-ui 7.0.0 exports `./toast`. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:101 (§5 'Persistent operation state stays with the entity/workspace'); PALETTE-CONTRACT.md:172 states the identical principle absolutely for the sibling export path — 'a visible terminal/retryable operation state — never a partial download or `console.warn`-only result'.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · R3-05 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Assistive technology is told the control is a multi-line rich-text editor, and it exposes no invalid state even while the error badge is on screen.

**Mechanism.** `contenteditable="true"` (not `plaintext-only`) under `role="textbox"` with no `aria-multiline` — the computed AX role resolves to multiline richtext, while the component hard-prevents Enter at :203-204. Announced affordance and real affordance disagree.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured via CDP `Accessibility.getFullAXTree`, frames/r3probe2.json -> ax: `{"role":"textbox","name":"Enter a CSS color","value":"color(display-p3 0.5 0.2 0.9)","props":["focusable=true","editable=\"richtext\"","settable=true","multiline=true","readonly=false","required=false"]}`. No `invalid` property present. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 'Role, accessible name, state/value and associated error/status are explicit.'
```

**Reproduction.** Open the field, attach a CDP session, `Accessibility.enable` then `Accessibility.getFullAXTree`, filter for name 'Enter a CSS color'. Read `editable` and `multiline`.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the contenteditable and consume glass-ui's `Input` — a native single-line `<input type="text">` resolves to a correct textbox role, cannot hold markup, and is the element `useUserInvalidAria` (glass-ui's own `:user-invalid` -> `aria-invalid` bridge) binds to.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · R3-06 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Spellcheck is enabled on the field, so every CSS colour token carries UA red wavy underlines — in the same red the component uses for its own error state.

**Mechanism.** `contenteditable` inherits spellcheck=true; nothing in the component opts out. An unowned, unstylable red-for-wrong system paints over correct input, competing with the owned red for the same meaning.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured, frames/r3probe.json -> maskGeometry: `"spellcheckIDL": true, "spellcheckAttr": null, "contentEditable": "true", "autocapitalize": null`. The component's only error signal is `--destructive` (border at :163, badge at :348-366).

**Reproduction.** Open the field and focus it; the tokens `oklch`, `lab`, `display-p3`, `rebeccapurple` are all non-dictionary words and receive red squiggles. Confirm with `document.querySelector('.color-input').spellcheck === true`.

**Proposed cure.** `spellcheck="false"` (plus `autocorrect="off"`, `autocapitalize="off"`, `enterkeyhint="go"`) on a real `<input>` — all of which are declared props on glass-ui's published `InputProps`, and none of which a contenteditable span accepts meaningfully.

**Defect.** Typing translates the dock's sibling controls +/-166 px: the commit arrow recedes from the pointer as the user types toward it.

**Evidence.**

```

**Defect.** The failure badge hides 89.9% of the value it is judging and the entire commit button, and carries no programmatic semantics.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · C-03 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** CONFIRMED (round-2 D-23): MT-F001 is swallowed by an undiscriminating bare catch, so a shipping parser TypeError is permanently indistinguishable from a user typo.

**Mechanism.** One untyped catch renders 'the grammar rejected your string', 'the parser threw a TypeError' and any future RangeError as the same sentence, so the application can never surface, count or report MT-F001.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured live: typing `oklch(` `)` + Enter yields `"f001PageErrors": []` and the badge text 'not a valid color'; the only console error on the route is the unrelated dev VITE_API_URL misconfiguration notice. Source: src/css/grammar.ts:181 `splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(...))` — the non-null assertion is false for an empty function body; demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:84 catches it with a bare `catch {}` and calls `flashParseError()`. Owner edict 2 forbids masking fallbacks.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/ -> Tools -> Open color input -> select all -> type `oklch(` then `)` -> Enter. The user sees a red slab covering 89.9% of their text and the whole retry arrow; no crash, no console error, no distinguishable signal.

**Proposed cure.** Discriminate at the boundary: the parse boundary returns a typed result (`{ok:true,value} | {ok:false,reason:'grammar'|'internal'}`) rather than throwing; 'internal' is reported (and countable) rather than rendered as 'not a valid color'. Fixing grammar.ts:181 is necessary but not sufficient — the swallow is the design defect.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D3-02 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** MAJOR (OVERTURNS r2 D-22, carried by two prior rounds as 'the wax seal has never been observed rendering'): the seal does render. Its gate is pointer history, not elapsed time. The dock therefore has two resting geometries for one idle page, and the collapsed rest is a 56px unlabelled circle that hides all four navigation controls.

**Mechanism.** A resting state selected by input device rather than by design. The producer's collapse timer is armed by pointerenter/leave, so a keyboard-only, touch-only or never-hovered desktop session sees a different dock than a mouse session.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured (dockprobe2/3/4): fresh load, no pointer, 7s idle → `.glass-dock … expanded`, pill 471x62; same at 20s idle → still expanded 471x62; mouse.move(700,45) then mouse.move(700,700), 7s → `.glass-dock … collapsed`, pill 56x56, `.dock-seal` 40x40, opacity 1; same cycle but with a prior focus() inside the dock → still expanded. Site: Dock.vue:132 `:collapse-delay="5000" :start-collapsed="false"`. Reads against VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:178 'The dock is its own top band, fully visible, focusable' and PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-16/PR-07 (terminal verb for hover-only/unlabeled controls = ADD-AFFORDANCE / REMOVE). Note the band floor DOES hold: .dock-band height constant 72px in both geometries at every viewport.
```

**Reproduction.** 1440x900 WebKit, load http://localhost:9000/#/, wait 20s without moving the pointer — dock stays 471x62 expanded. Reload, move the pointer over the pill then away, wait 7s — dock is 56x56 with `.dock-seal` visible and all navigation gone. Script: dockprobe3.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** Pick one resting state and make it unconditional. If the seal is the rest, set start-collapsed=true and capture the π frame the tranche has never had; if the pill is the rest, delete collapse-delay, the #collapsed slot, .dock-seal* and the ~95 lines of essay above them (Dock.vue:229-268, :309-328). Do not leave a magic 5000ms dwell outside the producer's spring register.

Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:19 'Glass earns its blur by revealing live content; otherwise it is a neutral well' and §4.1 'Text, focus, boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier; a token name is not evidence.' Same frame also shows r2 D-20's type-jurisdiction break — options at a display rung, not §4's `text-small`.
```

**Reproduction.** iPhone 14 Pro emulation, http://localhost:9000/#/, click `nav.dock-band button[aria-label="Menu"]`, screenshot. GitHub's glyph sits above its label; page numerals show through the copy. Script: dockprobe5.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** Move the composition onto glass-ui's menu tier (edict 4 — variants/primitives belong in glass-ui, not demo/ui). The row layout, the control type family and the material tier resolve together from one producer decision.

If the two cannot be made unambiguous inside one 44px row, the ramp coordinate yields, not the selection marker — PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:71 puts subtraction before explanation, and the Library heading already carries the identity a second time.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-9 · CHALLENGE-D

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-5 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Activating the toggle translates it ~64px out from under the pointer that just clicked it: the box is never reserved, so each sub-layer swap re-measures and re-morphs the whole centre-anchored dock.

**Mechanism.** No peak-size reserve exists on the sub-layer container; the dock's `fit-content` measurement re-runs per swap, and the local 260ms timer is on an entirely separate clock from the dock's morph — two clocks for one moment.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured WebKit 1440×900: `--dock-expanded-px` 471px (main) → 326px (actions); dock measured 466.8px in input. `.dock-layer-grid` rect x/w: 634.0/184.0 (actions) → 563.6/324.8 (input) — a +140.8px content change on a centre-anchored dock, so the left edge moves −70.4px and the toggle moves from x=831 to ≈895 (+64px). Figures `D2-desktop-light-actions.png` vs `D2-desktop-light-input.png`. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:30 (the dock band is reserved).
```

**Reproduction.** WebKit 1440×900, open Tools, record `[aria-label="Open color input"]` boundingBox, click it, record the new toggle box. Displacement ≈ +64px on x.

**Proposed cure.** `<DockCrossfade reserve="inline">` — the producer measures the peak face width once (documented as "MEASURE-ONCE `min-block-size` (a running max — NOT a per-swap FLIP)"), so the band never changes width and the control never moves.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-6 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The focus law is half-designed: the actions→input leg leaves focus on `<body>`, while the input→propose leg focuses correctly — two legs of one three-state cycle obeying two different laws.

**Mechanism.** The component owns the mode machine but delegates focus by accident: only the child's own prop-watcher happens to focus, and only on one of the two transitions. The handle needed for the missing leg is declared, bound, and unused.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured across the actions→input swap: focusBefore `<body class="relative" id="app" …>`, focusAfter `<body class="relative" id="app" …>`. Across input→propose: `document.activeElement` = `<span contenteditable role="textbox" aria-label="Propose a color name" …>`. The propose focus comes from `ColorInput.vue:252–262` (`requestAnimationFrame(() => inputColorRef.value?.focus())`), not from this component. `ColorInput.vue:283` exposes `focus: () => inputColorRef.value?.focus()`; `ActionBarLayer.vue:28` declares and `:116` binds `colorInputRef` — and never reads it. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:115.
```

**Reproduction.** WebKit 1440×900, open Tools, click `[aria-label="Open color input"]`, read `document.activeElement` → `<body>`. Click again into propose, read again → the contenteditable span.

**Proposed cure.** Stop re-deriving focus per leg: inherit the producer's documented law — `<DockCrossfade>` "transfers focus to its successor, else the body (un-inert-before-focus is load-bearing)" — so every face swap has one focus rule instead of one per branch.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-7 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The 260ms swap window is a JS timer and is not armed for `prefers-reduced-motion`; reduced motion does not resolve directly to the final geometry.

**Mechanism.** `SUB_LAYER_CROSSFADE_MS` is enforced by `setTimeout` at ActionBarLayer.vue:76–78; reduced motion is a media fact, so a code timer can never be its arm. Result: an invisible 443px `visibility: visible` element is held over the dock for 260ms before final geometry.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured with `reducedMotion: "reduce"` (WebKit): t=0 leaving 0 vis visible/hidden; t=30 leaving 1 visible/visible; unchanged through t=245; t=275 leaving 0, vis hidden/visible. Byte-identical to the normal-motion run. `demo/styles/animations.css:183–192` neutralises CSS transitions/animations app-wide but cannot touch a `setTimeout`. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:144 "Reduced motion resolves directly to the final geometry and stable chromatic state."
```

**Reproduction.** WebKit 1440×900 with `reducedMotion: "reduce"`, open Tools, click `[aria-label="Open color input"]`, sample `is-leaving` presence every 30ms — present t=30..245, cleared by t=275, identical to normal motion.

**Proposed cure.** Adopt the producer spring via `<DockCrossfade>`, which honours the query internally; delete the timer. Generally: motion duration belongs to the design system's clock, never to a consumer's magic constant.

**Mechanism.** Size was set on the glyph and the operable target was left to fall out of it — the inverse of law 7 ("Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities"). Owner edict 5 (root-level styling) is violated twice: an inline custom property for hover accent and a Tailwind size utility, both per-instance overrides of a root that owns both.

DockControl.vue.d.ts states the violated contract verbatim: "the HIT CELL stays the full --dock-control-size (≥44px on coarse via the density clamp) — hit box ≠ paint box". REPORT.md corroborates: smallTapTargets = 8 on /#/ in all four matrices, on a route whose dock is still closed.
```

**Reproduction.** Open the action bar; document.querySelectorAll('.action-button-wrapper') → getBoundingClientRect() = 32×32 each; document.querySelectorAll('.dock-icon-button')[0] → 40×40.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the entire <style scoped> box model and the bare <button>; the seat becomes <DockControl :active :disabled>. This single transposition dissolves D-1 through D-5 together and inherits hit-box≠paint-box, the ≥44px coarse clamp, aria-pressed, the glass hover face and the interruptible spring press for free.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-5 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The annotation is orphaned from what it annotates: at one viewport its interval to the dock pill measures 56.2px, 230.6px and 426.2px depending on the dock's own morph — pure residue, oscillating 195.6px per collapse/expand — and it reserves no space at all.

**Mechanism.** `position: absolute; inset-inline-end: 0` on `.dock-band` anchors the lamp to the band's edge, not to the pill; the interval is therefore `viewportWidth − dockWidth`, an accident. DockStatusLamp.vue:38-42 claims it 'reads as an instrument annotation etched into the chrome' — there is no chrome at the band's inline-end to etch into. Breaches PROPORTION-AUDIT §1 ('every element earns its ... interval and material from its job relative to the local protagonist') and §5.8 ('real rendered relation wins over token intent'). Dock.vue:124's T-31 claim that occlusion is 'impossible by construction — grid rows do not overlap' does not cover an absolutely-positioned child inside row 1.

**Evidence.**

```
Live at 1440x900, .glass-dock rect vs lamp rect in the same second: resting/collapsed pill [689.2,750.8] w=61.6, lamp [1177,1424] => gap 426.2px; expanded pill [493.6,946.4] w=452.8 => gap 230.6px; expanded nav layer pill right=1120.8 => gap 56.2px. Lamp never moves. Lamp occupies 17.5% of the 1408px band and is the only content in its right third (frames/band-1440-light.png). Collision threshold measured at 1024x768: band 992px, lamp 247px => any dock layer wider than 498.1px overlaps the pill; signed-out nav layer is 309px (94.5px clearance), but measured dock widths across states range 258.7-452.8px and the action-bar/slug-edit layers are wider.
```

**Reproduction.** Live: measure .glass-dock and .dock-status-lamp rects at 1440x900 before and after the 5s collapse. Reproduced 2026-07-27. The overlap sub-case (a >498px dock layer at <=1100px) was NOT reproduced and is filed as a hypothesis; the zero-reservation design is the defect and is proven.

**Proposed cure.** Seat it inside the pill (C-1): the interval to the protagonist becomes zero because the lamp IS the protagonist's chrome — no absolute positioning, no residue, no unreserved overlap, and the dock's own layout owns the reservation.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-8 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The pending state is structurally unreachable, and the disabled state is opacity-only.

**Mechanism.** A pending affordance authored against an imagined `await` that was never written — the state exists in the diff as reassurance and cannot exist at runtime. The disabled treatment is a post-hoc alpha attenuation, the degenerate case of color-only state.

**Evidence.**

```
Pending: `SlugEditLayer.vue:97` renders `Loader2` on `slugSwitching`, but `:42` sets it true, `:54` fires an un-awaited promise and `:64`'s `finally` sets it false — all in one synchronous execution, so Vue never paints between. MutationObserver armed across the whole submit (probe2 §A5): `{"sawSpinner":false,"spinnersNow":0}`. Disabled: measured `disabled {opacity:"0.5", color:"color(srgb 0 0 0 / 0.8)", bg:"rgba(0,0,0,0)", boxShadow:"none", cursor:"default"}` vs `enabled {opacity:"1", color:"color(srgb 0 0 0 / 0.8)", bg:"rgba(0,0,0,0)", cursor:"pointer"}` — the entire rendered difference is alpha 0.5 vs 1.0. Under forced-colors the disabled control still measures `opacity: "0.5"` with `forced-color-adjust: auto`, so opacity (not a forced-colors property) survives and the rescue mode does not rescue it. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 "Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only."
```

**Reproduction.** Open the layer, fill the input, arm a MutationObserver for `.animate-spin`, click `Switch to slug`, wait 1.2s: the spinner is never inserted. Separately, screenshot the submit control empty vs filled: the only delta is opacity.

**Proposed cure.** Await the port so the pending state can exist, and give disabled a non-alpha channel (shape/boundary/glyph change) at the producer root so every `DockControl` inherits it — not a per-instance override here.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-12 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The crown entrance animation never runs, on any device, in any browser, and never has. ColorInput.vue:36-39 binds `animation: crown-appear ...` in an INLINE style attribute; ColorInput.vue:369-376 defines `@keyframes crown-appear` inside `<style scoped>`. Vue's SFC compiler hash-suffixes scoped keyframe names and rewrites animation declarations within the same style block, but does NOT process template style attributes. The inline reference resolves to nothing. NEW this pass — it also refutes the first pass's negative proof line 654, 'The animation law is honoured.'

**Mechanism.** Wrong home for a keyframe, forced by a per-instance inline style. A scoped @keyframes is consumable only from a class rule in the same block; an inline style attribute is consumable only against a GLOBAL keyframe. Pairing the two is unsatisfiable by construction — no combination of the two halves can ever resolve. Violates edict 6 (an animation deleted by construction rather than by decision) and edict 5 (per-instance inline override where a root-level class belongs).

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:38 (inline `animation: crown-appear var(--duration-panel) var(--ease-decelerate) forwards;`) vs :369 (`@keyframes crown-appear`). Compiled sheet served by the dev server: `curl -s "http://localhost:9000/@fs/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue?vue&type=style&index=0&scoped=55dadc03&lang.css"` → contains `@keyframes crown-appear-55dadc03 {...}` and, for contrast, the class-driven sibling correctly rewritten: `.color-input-mode-flash[data-v-55dadc03] { animation: input-mode-flash-55dadc03 ... }`. Live document keyframe census (all stylesheets, all CSSKeyframesRule names): {"exactCrownAppear": false, "crownLike": ["crown-appear-55dadc03"], "totalKeyframes": 54}. No global fallback: `grep -rn "crown-appear" demo/` returns exactly 3 hits — ColorInput.vue:38, ColorInput.vue:369, demo/DESIGN.md:213 (prose). demo/styles/animations.css does not contain it.
```

**Reproduction.** 1) `curl -s "http://localhost:9000/@fs/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue?vue&type=style&index=0&scoped=55dadc03&lang.css"` — observe the definition is emitted as `crown-appear-55dadc03`. 2) In any live page at http://localhost:9000, evaluate: `[...document.styleSheets].flatMap(s=>{try{return [...s.cssRules]}catch{return []}}).filter(r=>r.type===CSSRule.KEYFRAMES_RULE).map(r=>r.name).includes('crown-appear')` → false.

**Proposed cure.** crown-appear is a design-language beat, not seat geometry: promote it to demo/styles/animations.css (which already exists and is the declared home for global keyframes) and drive it from a `.crown-badge` CLASS. The inline style attribute dies with it. Adopt the rule repo-wide: if the reference is inline, the keyframe must be global; if the keyframe is scoped, the reference must be a class in the same block. No third combination is legal.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-21 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** `serializePickerColor` answers a different question rather than failing: it suppresses the library's `{ok:false, color_invalid_input}` for the four non-CSS spaces and silently substitutes oklch — and ColorInput.vue:104 renders that substitution two lines beneath the sentence "Any valid CSS color string is accepted."

This is the masking fallback edict 2 forbids, sitting at the bottom of the funnel every colour readout in the app runs through.

**Evidence.**

All 17 spaces incl. the 4 non-CSS ones are user-selectable (color-model.ts:75-78 DISPLAY_COLOR_SPACE_NAMES = {...PICKER_SPACE_NAMES, hex}). The sibling consumer GUARDS the identical call: ColorSpaceSelector.vue:161 `if (CSS_PICKER_SPACES.has(converted.space)) return serializePickerColor(converted);` else renders `hsv · 25 · 0.8 · 0.95`.

**Reproduction.** node --input-type=module against ./dist/subpaths/{color,css}.js: build hsv(25,0.8,0.95,1), call serializeCssColor → {ok:false,color_invalid_input}; then convertColor(...,'oklch') + serializeCssColor → the oklch string the demo returns instead. **Proposed cure.** serializePickerColor returns Result<string, ColorIssue> and never converts. Callers wanting the oklch projection request it by name (serializeAsOklch), so substitution becomes a request instead of a silent default. ColorInput.vue:104 then renders either the CSS spelling or the honest non-CSS spelling ColorSpaceSelector already implements — one helper, one home, both call sites. **Mechanism.** The shim hides the outgoing face by class only (opacity 0 + inert on the face element). The popover content is teleported to the body, so neither the opacity nor the inert reaches it, and its open state lives in a local ref of a component that is never unmounted — a class-only swap emits no lifecycle event for the outgoing face.

**Evidence.**

```
Captured: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-actionbarlayer/D-02-stranded-popover-after-swap.png (ActionToolbar's "Copy color" popover superimposed on ColorInput's "Enter a color" popover). Reproduced live (probe 3): afterHover {portals:2, texts:[…,"Copy colorClick to copy the current color to the c"]}; afterSwap {portals:2, same texts} while faces = [{cls:"… dock-layer", inert:true, op:"0"}, {cls:"… dock-layer is-active min-w-0", inert:false, op:"1"}]. Code path: demo/shell/dock/ActionButton.vue:2-45 (portalled Popover), :81 `isOpen = activeHover === hoverKey`, demo/shell/dock/ActionToolbar.vue:85 local `activeHover`, :87-91 `defineExpose({ clearHover })`; demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:29 declares `actionToolbarRef`, :103 binds it, zero reads.
```

**Reproduction.** Playwright, /#/: open the action bar; dispatch pointerenter/pointerover/mouseenter/mouseover on `.dock-layer button[aria-label="Copy color"]`; wait 700ms (past the 300ms open-delay); count `[data-reka-popper-content-wrapper]` → 2; click [aria-label="Open color input"]; wait 700ms; re-count → still 2, with the "Copy color" text present.

**Proposed cure.** Let the face own the mount: `<DockLayer id="actions">` unmounts its content on dissolve, so `activeHover` dies with it and the portal unmounts — no imperative clearHover, no dead ref. If glass-ui intends faces to stay mounted, that is the next relay mark to BI (successor to the now-discharged M2): "a dissolving face's portalled overlays are not dismissed", with D-02 attached as consumer evidence.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** One concept, two homes: DockStatusLamp.vue + status-lamp.ts and ApiOfflineChip.vue are the same component written twice. The pure resolver is homed in the consumer's feature directory rather than beside the transport state it resolves, which forces the duplication.

**Mechanism.** Module placement error — a pure resolver homed in the consumer directory (demo/shell/dock/) instead of beside its state (demo/platform/transport/availability.ts). Reuse from the second seat would require a palettes→shell lateral feature edge (the demo otherwise has only two such edges, both `import type`: usePalettePorts.ts:19, ColorPicker.vue:130), so the second implementation is structurally forced. Unique semantic ownership violated by placement.

**Evidence.**

```
Labels byte-identical: demo/shell/dock/status-lamp.ts:54 `label: "dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`"` vs demo/palettes/browser/status/ApiOfflineChip.vue:17; status-lamp.ts:60 `label: "backend offline — saved locally"` vs ApiOfflineChip.vue:25. Roles identical (status-lamp.ts:39 alert|status; ApiOfflineChip.vue:13,21). Measured CSS declaration-set intersection: lamp .dock-status-lamp = 18 decls, chip .api-offline-chip = 13 decls, IDENTICAL = 11; only-in-chip = ['border-radius: var(--radius-pill)','padding: 0.3rem 0.7rem']. Twin keyframes: DockStatusLamp.vue:110-118 `lamp-dot-pulse` vs ApiOfflineChip.vue:82-89 `offline-dot-pulse` — identical bodies (0%,100%{opacity:1} 50%{opacity:.35}), identical `2.4s var(--ease-standard) infinite`. Duplication is documented not cured at status-lamp.ts:8-9 and DockStatusLamp.vue:41-42 ("one status language, two seats").
```

**Reproduction.** grep -c comparison of the two SFCs plus the normalized declaration-set diff (pasted in the report). ApiOfflineChip.vue:36-37 re-derives the matrix inline (`availability.value === "unavailable"` / `=== "misconfigured"`) and is covered by zero rows of test/status-lamp.test.ts. HYPOTHESIS (not reproduced): with ≥1 saved colour on /#/palettes both seats render simultaneously as two role="alert" nodes with identical text — measured document.querySelectorAll('[role="alert"]').length === 1 on an empty session because CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:116's `v-if="savedColorStrings.length > 0"` gate was false.

**Proposed cure.** Move the resolver to demo/platform/transport/api-status.ts as `resolveApiStatus(availability, isDev) → ApiStatusFace | null` (state/role/label, using glass-ui's StatusDotState vocabulary); delete demo/shell/dock/status-lamp.ts and ApiOfflineChip.vue; both seats render ONE new demo/shared/ui/ApiStatusPill.vue built from glass-ui Chip + StatusDot. Every edge becomes downward (shell→shared→platform, palettes→shared→platform).

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-13 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The demo's declared value.js type surface does not match the published export map: three tsconfig paths targets do not exist, two published subpaths (including the demo's second-most-used) have no paths entry and typecheck against a stale installed copy of the package inside the repo that IS the package.

**Mechanism.** Two independent declarations of one public surface. vite.config.ts:44-51 GENERATES its runtime alias set from package.json#exports; tsconfig.demo.json#paths is hand-maintained and has drifted. Where a paths entry is absent, TS falls through to node_modules — and a self-installed copy of the repo's own package sits there, so vue-tsc checks a stale .d.ts while Vite bundles the live dist. The `.` root paths entry types an import no real consumer can write (an exports map without a "." key yields ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED).

**Evidence.**

```
package.json#exports keys = ./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize (7, NO "."). tsconfig.demo.json paths keys = @mkbabb/value.js @mkbabb/value.js/color /parsing /math /easing /units /transform /quantize (8). `test -f dist/index.d.ts` → MISSING; dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts → MISSING; dist/subpaths/units.d.ts → MISSING (against a dist built 2026-07-27 11:52). Demo import counts: @mkbabb/value.js/color ×25, /css ×10, /math ×6, /easing ×5, /quantize ×4 — /css and /value have NO paths entry. node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js is a real installed 4.0.0 tarball (readlink → not a symlink; own package.json/LICENSE/README/dist dated Jul 17 21:10). Drift measured: dist/subpaths/css.d.ts = 12490 B vs node_modules copy = 10910 B; diff shows `declare type Alpha_2`, `Channel_2`, `ChannelsBySpace_2` present live and absent installed. dist/subpaths/css.js 43973 B vs 43972 B.
```

**Reproduction.** node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('./package.json').exports).join(' '))"; then the tsconfig paths key dump; then `test -f` on the three missing targets; then `ls -l` + `diff` of dist/subpaths/css.d.ts against node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts. All commands and outputs pasted in the report.

**Proposed cure.** Generate tsconfig.demo.json#paths from package.json#exports with the same script that generates the Vite aliases — one source of truth, drift structurally impossible. Remove @mkbabb/value.js from the repo's own node_modules so exactly one copy of the library exists in the graph. Add a `.` export to package.json#exports or delete the bare-specifier paths entry; do not type an import no consumer can write.

**Defect.** `--type-mono-caption` is a phantom CSS custom property with zero definition sites anywhere, masked at three consumption sites by three different fallbacks; the lamp consequently paints at a fixed 11px outside the design system's fluid caption scale.

**Mechanism.** A Tailwind @utility NAME was read as if it implied a matching custom property. The literal fallback then hid the broken contract permanently — a masking fallback (edict 2) over a design-system recipe the demo already owns elsewhere (edict 4).

**Evidence.**

```
`grep -rlo -- "--type-mono-caption:" demo/ src/ node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` → no output (zero definition sites). Live: getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--type-mono-caption') === ""; --type-caption === "clamp( 0.75rem, 0.71rem + 0.21vw, 1rem )". Computed .dock-status-lamp fontSize = 11px. Three consumers with three masks: DockStatusLamp.vue:54 `var(--type-mono-caption, 0.6875rem)`, ApiOfflineChip.vue:47 same, ComponentSliders.vue:310 `var(--type-mono-caption, var(--type-caption))`. glass-ui ships the recipe as `@utility text-mono-caption { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--type-caption); letter-spacing: var(--type-tracking-caps); text-transform: uppercase }` (dist/styles/typography/utilities.css), already used at 8 demo sites including demo/shell/dock/menus/ProfileSection.vue:132 and PaletteCardMenu.vue:37. --type-tracking-caps = 0.1em vs the lamp's hand-rolled 0.06em.
```

**Reproduction.** Navigate http://localhost:9000/#/ and evaluate getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--type-mono-caption') → ""; getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.dock-status-lamp')).fontSize → "11px". Static: the grep above returns zero definition sites.

**Proposed cure.** Delete all three `var(--type-mono-caption, …)` sites and apply glass-ui's `text-mono-caption` utility (paired with `fira-code` as at ConsoleRail.vue:75). Also drop the dead `, 9999px` and `, oklch(0.58 0.19 25)` fallbacks — both --radius-pill and --destructive resolve live, and the sibling chip already writes --radius-pill bare.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-4 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** role="alert" with an empty accessible name below 1024px: the only text in the live region is display:none, which removes it from the accessibility tree — and the in-file comment asserts the opposite.

**Mechanism.** The accessible name is a property of the resolved face (status-lamp.ts:40 already carries `label`), but the rendering decision that destroys it lives in an unrelated media query in the SFC with no contract between the two modules. Three test suites, zero coverage of the pairing.

**Evidence.**

```
DockStatusLamp.vue:67-69 `.lamp-label { display: none }`, lifted only at :70-74 `@media (min-width:1024px){ display:inline }`; dot is aria-hidden at :18; root carries :role="lamp.role" at :16. Comment at :65-66 claims "The role + label stay in the accessibility tree (visually-hidden, not v-if'd)" — false: CSS Display §1.3 (display:none generates no boxes, contents not rendered) and HTML-AAM exclude non-rendered subtrees from accessibility APIs. MEASURED at innerWidth 430: labelDisplay "none", role "alert", lamp.innerText === "", rect 25.99×17.99. At innerWidth 1440: labelDisplay "block", innerText "dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`". Coverage gap: test/status-lamp.test.ts asserts only the pure matrix; e2e/smoke/oracles/o22-status-lamp.spec.ts:56-83 asserts data-variant/role/geometry at desktop only, never the accessible name; the visual audit's a11y probe records only smallTapTargets/imgNoAlt/namelessButtons (REPORT.json results[].probe.a11y), and namelessButtons inspects buttons — an unnamed alert is invisible to it.
```

**Reproduction.** Playwright: browser_navigate http://localhost:9000/#/ ; browser_resize 430×900 ; evaluate → { labelDisplay: "none", role: "alert", lampInnerText: "" }. Then resize 1440×900 → innerText restored. Full outputs pasted in the report.

**Proposed cure.** Adopt glass-ui StatusDot's `label` prop (L-3), or replace display:none with sr-only/clip-rect. Never display:none the only text in a live region. The compact/expanded decision belongs in the shared ApiStatusPill's `compact` prop, tested once, not in each seat's media query.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-6 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The api-client provide/inject seam is unsubstitutable — a DI wrapper around module singletons with one provider, no parameters, and no test double — and its only measurable effect is to make the component un-mountable in tests, which is what forced the resolver extraction that L-1 then mislocated.

**Mechanism.** An abstraction with exactly one implementation and no injection point is not a seam; it is indirection. Its cost is real (the component cannot be mounted without an App-root provider), and paying that cost produced the extracted-resolver pattern that was then homed in the wrong directory — L-6 is the proximate cause of L-1.

**Evidence.**

```
useApiClient.ts:36-44 `createApiClient()` takes NO parameters and returns { request, adminRequest, sessionToken: sessionTokenRef, availability: apiAvailability, baseUrl: BASE_URL } — `availability` IS the module ref exported at availability.ts:47. One provider: App.vue:189 provideApiClient(). Three consumers, all reading only `availability`: DockStatusLamp.vue:30, ApiOfflineChip.vue:35, PaletteCardMenu.vue:216. useApiClient.ts:56-60 throws when no provider stands above. Yet the docs claim "never a hard module-singleton import" (useApiClient.ts:2-16, echoed at DockStatusLamp.vue:28-29). test/status-lamp.test.ts never mounts the SFC — it imports the extracted pure function only.
```

**Reproduction.** Read useApiClient.ts:36-44 (zero-parameter factory closing over module state) and grep -rn 'provideApiClient|createApiClient' demo/ → exactly one provider site (App.vue:189) and zero substitutions anywhere in demo/, test/, or e2e/.

**Proposed cure.** Either give the seam a reason to exist — `createApiClient(deps)` with an injectable transport so tests can drive faces through the mounted component — or delete it and import `apiAvailability` directly at the three consumers (three one-line edits). Do not keep a seam that cannot seam.

**Defect.** Layering inversion plus a module-tree cycle: demo/shell (the shell) depends on demo/palettes (a feature) at 5 edges, while demo/palettes depends back on demo/shell — and demo/platform/auth/ already exists as the correct home for the identity port.

**Mechanism.** usePalettePorts.ts is the residue of the retired usePaletteManager god facade (its own header, lines 21-31). RF-15 §b split the god object into five ports but left all five in the god module's FILE, so the module boundary never moved. Port 1 (Session) is not a palette concept.

**Evidence.**

```
`grep -rn 'from "\.\./.*palettes/" demo/shell/` → DockViewSelect.vue, Dock.vue:18, SlugEditLayer.vue:5, ProfileSection.vue:14, MobileMenuDropdown.vue:13, all importing ../palettes/usePalettePorts. ### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-4 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** All three controls render 22x22 because glass-ui's compact dock-control variant ships NO hit-target floor and is explicitly exempted from the dock's own coarse-pointer floor — and the repo's own T-36 cure for exactly this was applied per-instance to a sibling SFC, so it did not propagate here.

Because it is per-instance there is no structural mechanism by which the next compact consumer inherits it. A law enforced by a comment is not enforced.

**Evidence.**

```
Live at localhost:9000, state-invariant (measured inert AND active): all three = w22 h22, width_css/height_css '22px', padding '4px', glyph 14x14 (w-3.5 h-3.5). Producer rule, node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/controls/icon-button.css: `.dock-icon-button--compact{width:var(--dock-compact-control-size,auto);height:var(--dock-compact-control-size,auto);min-width:var(--dock-compact-control-min-width,0);padding:var(--dock-compact-control-padding,0.25rem)}`. touch-floor.css: `@media (pointer:coarse){.dock-icon-button:not(.dock-icon-button--compact):not(:where(.glass-dock *)){min-block-size:var(--dock-touch-target,2.75rem)…}}`. CORRECTION TO MT-F004: measured center distances 47.00 / 75.00 / 28.00 px, all >= 24, so WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 spacing exception IS met — these PASS AA. They fail SC 2.5.5 (AAA 44x44) and the producer's own --dock-touch-target:2.75rem intent. The audit harness's flat 24x24 rule does not implement the spacing exception.
```

**Reproduction.** Playwright evaluate on http://localhost:9000/#/ measuring button[aria-label='Switch to slug'|'Generate new slug'|'Cancel'] getBoundingClientRect + getComputedStyle; plus the two grep/cat commands over glass-ui dist CSS.

**Proposed cure.** (1) Producer, correct home per edict 4: glass-ui gives --dock-compact-control-min-width/-height a 24px default and drops the :not(.dock-icon-button--compact) clause from touch-floor.css — a glass-ui BH relay obligation. (2) Until then, set the tokens ONCE on .glass-dock in Dock.vue's scoped block and delete .dock-tools-btn's local copy. Never min-w-6/min-h-6 utilities on the three DockControl tags.
