### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure / module boundaries / owners` · L-19 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** `isAdminMode` is a one-way latch defined by two disagreeing predicates. After one visit to a tuning route the dock wears admin identity (gold shimmer glyph + gold `--dock-ring`) on every subsequent non-admin route for the rest of the session.

**Mechanism.** Duplicated state for a value that is a pure function of the route, with the predicate implemented twice and neither copy owned by the schema that owns views (demo/shell/viewSchema.ts).

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/composables/useDockAdminMode.ts:32 seeds the ref with a PREFIX test `currentView.startsWith("admin-")`; :55-59 maintains it with a MEMBERSHIP test `adminViews.includes(view)` and has no falsifying arm. The two predicates disagree on `atmosphere`/`blob` (in the array at :27, not prefixed). Reproduced live (scratchpad L-probe6.mjs, headless Chromium 1280x900): `1 fresh picker {"route":"#/","goldIcon":false,"ring":"oklch(0.471189 0.188448 9.8340"}` / `2 -> atmosphere {"goldIcon":true,"ring":"light-dark(oklch(0.751 0.147 8"}` / `3 back() -> picker {"route":"#/","goldIcon":true,"ring":"light-dark(oklch(0.751 0.147 8"}` / `4 -> palettes {"goldIcon":true,...}`.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/L-probe6.mjs — load /#/ (gold false), hash to /#/atmosphere (gold true), page.goBack() to /#/ (gold STILL true), hash to /#/palettes (gold STILL true). With admin credentials the damage is functional, not cosmetic: viewEntries (:34-39) then returns only the seven admin views while on /#/palettes, so the dock's own navigation cannot reach the user views except through the `__admin_toggle__` sentinel row.

**Proposed cure.** Derive, do not latch. Add `group: "user" | "admin"` to `PaneConfig` (viewSchema.ts owns the partition) and reduce the composable to `const isAdminMode = computed(() => VIEW_MAP[viewManager.currentView.value].group === "admin")`. The ref, both watchers and both hardcoded ViewId arrays die; `toggleAdminMode` keeps its real job (it navigates) and the flag follows the route by construction — the same transposition `useViewManager.ts:51-58` already applied to `mobilePaneIndex`.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure / module boundaries / owners` · L-20 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The local `useLayerTransition` shim in ActionBarLayer produces no crossfade at all: the producer CSS the template hand-binds declares no opacity transition, so the 260 ms timer window is an instant cut with a transparent inert box held over the live controls.

**Mechanism.** A local fork of a retired producer concept, styled out of the producer's private stylesheet by class-name convention; the fork reimplements the packaging but cannot reach the animation, which the producer moved behind a component.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:62-94 (the shim, SUB_LAYER_CROSSFADE_MS = 260, subLayerProps hand-binding `.dock-layer`/`is-active`/`is-leaving`). Producer rules: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/layers.css declares only `transition: visibility 0s linear var(--duration-normal)` on `.dock-layer`; the opacity overlap lives on `.dock-crossfade[data-crossfading] > .dock-face` via `--dock-t` (crossfade.css), reachable only inside `<DockCrossfade>`. Measured live (scratchpad L-probe2.mjs), both faces at rest / +60ms / +460ms across the actions->input swap: `transitionProperty: "visibility", transitionDuration: "0s"` at every phase; opacity steps 1->0 and 0->1 in one frame; the leaving face holds a 442x45 transparent inert box. The public successor exists: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/index.d.ts:5 `export { default as DockCrossfade } from "./DockCrossfade.vue";` — contradicting the shim's own comment at ActionBarLayer.vue:54-61.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/L-probe2.mjs — navigate /#/, click [aria-label='Toggle action bar'], click [aria-label='Open color input'], sample getComputedStyle on both children of `.dock-layer-grid` at 60 ms and 460 ms. transition-property is `visibility` and duration `0s` in all four phases.

**Proposed cure.** Replace ActionBarLayer.vue:62-101 with `<DockCrossfade :active="activeSubLayer" reserve="inline">` wrapping two `<DockLayer id="actions">` / `<DockLayer id="input">` faces. The shim, the 260 ms literal, the timer, `subLayerProps`, `subLayerGridEl`, the `void opts.containerEl` parity argument and the hand-bound producer classes all die (~40 lines), and the producer's spring-driven overlap, peak-size reserve and focus transfer from a dissolving face arrive instead of being approximated.

**Defect.** Inverted dependency: the shell's persistent chrome imports its identity/session port from the palettes FEATURE, putting 23 palettes modules into the dock's runtime graph on every route.

```
Five of the six `SESSION_PORT_KEY` consumers are dock files: demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:18, DockViewSelect.vue:8, layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:5, menus/ProfileSection.vue:14, menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue:13 — the sixth is the definition in demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · D-6 · CHALLENGE-C

**Mechanism.** A false premise about pointer capture (it retargets, it does not stop propagation) left a live duplicate code path that the comment records as fact.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the branch: `if (draggingId.value) return;` at the top of onBarPointerMove — with capture on the handle the bar has no job during a drag — and cache the rail rect at pointerdown instead of measuring twice per move (the rail cannot resize mid-drag; touch-action:none is already set).

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches` · C5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The gradient route's parse path THROWS instead of rejecting on the 8 empty-argument colour functions (MT-F001): the throw escapes parseGradientCSS → applyCSS → onParseCSS into a debounce timer, so the 'model-or-reject, fail LOUD' contract inverts into an uncaught TypeError with no verdict rendered.

**Evidence.**

```
`npx vite-node .../evidence/parse-probe.ts` → `parseCssColor("oklch()") -> THROW TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')` and identically for rgb()/hsl()/lab()/lch()/oklab()/hwb()/color(); `parseGradientCSS -> THROW TypeError … << linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)`. Unit: tileIdFor({css:'cubic-bezier(0.895, 0.03, 0.685, 0.22)'}) -> null; specimenNameFor -> 'custom'; same for ease-out-quint. Contract stated at easingCatalogue.ts:15-17.

**Proposed cure.** Turn FAMILY_ORDER into a rank, never a filter, so an unknown family sorts last but still renders: const rank = f => { const i = FAMILY_ORDER.indexOf(f); return i < 0 ? FAMILY_ORDER.length : i; }; return [...byFamily.keys()].sort((a,b) => rank(a)-rank(b) || a.localeCompare(b)).map(family => ({ family, tiles: byFamily.get(family)! })). familyLabelFor's regex is already general, so no other edit is needed and a future upstream preset can never vanish.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches` · C-05 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** A 27-way single-select gallery is exposed to assistive tech as 27 independent aria-pressed toggle buttons — no radio semantics, no roving tabindex, no arrow keys, and the family grouping is aria-hidden so it is invisible to AT. Playwright AX dump (test-results/oracles-o17-easing-composi-24ab6-...-desktop-smoke/error-context.md:59+) shows a flat group with 27 sibling `button ... [pressed]` nodes, no radiogroup, no per-family structure. glass exposes the prop at dist/fading-scroll-DhxXIhm2.js:78-92 (role='region' only when ariaLabel/ariaLabelledby given; tabindex="0" hardcoded). Component sites: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:84 (FadingScroll without aria-label), :89 (label on the inner div), :96 (family eyebrow aria-hidden), :98-107 (Chip mode="selectable"). The REPORT's namelessButtons probe filters button,[role=button] (capture.mjs:102-105), so this focusable div is structurally invisible to the audit matrix.
```

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches` · D-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Clipboard failure is completely silent and permanent. `copied` collapses useClipboard's 4-state machine to `status === 'success'`, so `failure` renders identically to idle; the library schedules its reset timer only on the success branch, and no `onCopyError` is supplied.

**Mechanism.** 4-state status collapsed to a boolean at the consumption site; the error state has no render path and no reporting hook

**Evidence.**

```
MixResultDisplay.vue:31-32. dist/useClipboard-D36OTaeT.js: `n.ok ? (a.value="success", l=setTimeout(…, i.resetMs ?? 1500), n) : (a.value="failure", i.onCopyError?.(n.reason), n)` — no reset on failure. Live simulation of a non-secure context (the repo's own LAN-http mobile-testing mode, vite server.host:true): {"titleBefore":"Copy color","titleAfter":"Copy color","anyErrorTextInPlate":false,"liveRegions":0} — nothing changes at all.
```

**Reproduction.** Mount MixResultDisplay with a colour result, then `Object.defineProperty(navigator,'clipboard',{value:undefined,configurable:true})` and click the Copy button — after 300ms the title is unchanged, no error text, no live region.

**Proposed cure.** Render the third state: drive the icon and the new live region off `status` directly instead of collapsing to a boolean at :32, and pass `onCopyError` so the failure reason is reportable. The collapse itself is the defect.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches` · D-6 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The copy confirmation goes stale across a re-mix and affirms a value that was never copied. MIX_CONVERGE_MS(900) + vj-morph(~200) ≈ 1100ms is shorter than resetMs 1500ms, and the component instance is not remounted, so the check mark survives into the next result.

**Mechanism.** confirmation lifetime bound to a timer instead of to the identity of the thing confirmed

**Evidence.**

```
MixResultDisplay.vue:31 (resetMs 1500) vs mixStage.ts:24 (MIX_CONVERGE_MS=900) and demo/styles/animations.css:104-109 (--duration-fast). Measured: {"step1_afterCopy":{"title":"Copied!","iconClass":"… lucide-check …"}, "step2_afterReMix_1270ms":{"title":"Copied!","iconClass":"… lucide-check …"}, "step2_plateText":"RESULT oklab(0.3 -0.05 0.09)"} — the plate shows result B while the button still affirms the copy of result A. useClipboard exports `invalidate()` (dist `d()`); MixResultDisplay.vue:31 destructures only {status, copy}.
```

**Reproduction.** Mount MixResultDisplay with a reactive result; click Copy; after 120ms set ghost=true and swap in a new result; after 900ms set ghost=false; read the copy button at ~1270ms — title still 'Copied!', icon still Check, while the plate text is the new colour.

**Proposed cure.** `const { status, copy, invalidate } = useClipboard()` plus `watch(() => result, invalidate)`. Bind the confirmation to the result identity; do not race it against a timer.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt: demo/workbenches/g` · C-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Interval identity is positional: inserting a stop mid-ramp silently re-hosts every downstream authored curve onto a different colour pair, and the accordion's index-keyed disclosure state follows the index rather than the interval.

**Mechanism.** positional-identity: per-item state keyed on an array ordinal over a list whose items are inserted and removed in the middle, so identity shifts silently under every non-tail edit.

**Evidence.**

```
Reproduced (probe 9): BEFORE insert `{"heads":["1 → 2linear","2 → 3ease-in-out-expo"],"stops":["0%","50%","100%"],"open":["easing-interval-1"],"tune":["false","true"]}` — ease-in-out-expo authored for 50%→100%. AFTER inserting a stop at 24%: `{"heads":["1 → 2linear","2 → 3ease-in-out-expo","3 → 4linear"],"stops":["0%","24%","50%","100%"],"open":["easing-interval-1"],"tune":["false","true","false"]}` — the curve is still on row `2 → 3`, which now means 24%→50%; the interval it was authored for is now `3 → 4`, reset to linear. Mechanism: useGradientModel.ts:89-100 the sync watch is append/truncate-only (`while (intervals.value.length < needed) intervals.value.push(linearInterval())`) and only observes `stops.value.length`, while addStop (:116-120) inserts positionally sorted and removeStop (:122-125) filters by id. GradientEasingEditor keys ALL its own state on the same ordinal: openInterval (:61), tuneOpen (:84), copiedIndex (:95), the DOM ids `easing-interval-${row.index}` (:145) / `easing-authoring-${row.index}` (:205), the v-for :key (:113), and the update-interval emit (:49).
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/wbge-probe9.mjs — or manually: 1. open /#/gradient. 2. click the stop bar at 50% (3 stops, 2 intervals). 3. open row `2 → 3` and press the `expo in-out` specimen tile. 4. click the stop bar at 25%. 5. row `2 → 3` still reads ease-in-out-expo but now spans 24%→50%; the 50%→100% interval you authored is now row `3 → 4`, linear.

**Proposed cure.** Give the interval a stable identity derived from the pair it spans, not from its ordinal. Stops already carry uid() (useGradientModel.ts:66-69) — hold intervals in a Map<string, GradientInterval> keyed on the LEFT stop's id. Insertion then splits an interval instead of shifting a list: the new stop's key gets a fresh linearInterval(), every existing key keeps its curve, removal drops exactly one entry. GradientEasingEditor keys its accordion, disclosure, v-for :key, DOM ids and emit on that same id — which also fixes the v-for :key="row.index" that currently makes Vue reuse row DOM across a shift, the reason the disclosure appears to 'stick' to the wrong interval.

**Defect.** Every accordion row mounts in full — specimen strip and a live EasingPicker — although the accordion can display exactly one row at a time; ~75% of the mounted DOM is permanently display:none.

**Mechanism.** eager-mount: a v-show accordion mounts the bodies of rows that have never been disclosed, so mount cost scales with item count rather than with disclosure.

Measured (probes 1 and 2, Chromium 1440×900, /#/gradient): 2 stops / 1 interval → allElements 511, buttons 53, [data-specimen] 27, easing-picker 1, visible rows 1. 5 stops / 4 intervals → allElements 1109, buttons 149, [data-specimen] 108, easing-picker 4, visible rows STILL 1. Delta +598 elements, +96 buttons, +81 hidden tile buttons, +3 fully-wired hidden EasingPicker instances (each with drag handlers and its own curve sampling), plus one useMediaQuery matchMedia subscription per strip (EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:47). Cost on an unrelated interaction, 120 ArrowRight presses on the Direction slider, CDP Performance.getMetrics deltas (probe 8): 1 interval `{scriptMs 13.9, layoutMs 20.7, recalcMs 191.6}` vs 4 intervals `{scriptMs 16.9, layoutMs 26.1, recalcMs 258.0}` → script/tick 0.116ms → 0.141ms (+22%), style recalc +34.7%, layout +26%.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/ext` · C-7 · CHALLENGE-C

```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/extract — in-page, replay imageFileToPixels verbatim on a 3000x2000 JPEG File and time each phase. Scale to a 12 MP phone photo (4032x3024): 48.7 MB ImageData + 48.7 MB slice = ~97 MB transient, on mobile Safari.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/mix` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The `swatchKeys` "stable key" scheme (MixSourceSelector.vue:78-98) embeds the array index in the map key (`${sc.css}::${i}`), and the prune watch (flush 'pre', so it runs BEFORE the render that re-reads the computed) deletes every shifted entry. Removing a chip therefore re-keys every surviving chip at or after that index — Vue unmounts and remounts them. This defeats the FLIP `.vj-enter-move` reflow the shared recipe promises, forces up to N-1 unchanged chips into `position:absolute` simultaneously (collapsing the row), and rebuilds N-1 glass-ui feTurbulence filter graphs in one frame. Strictly worse than :key="i".

**Evidence.**

```
MixSourceSelector.vue:79-98 (counter + Map + computed + prune watch); useMixingState.ts:55-61 (immutable add/remove). demo/styles/utils.css:167-179 documents the intent verbatim ("neighbours reflow on the family move class") and sets `.swatch-row > .vj-enter-leave-active { position: absolute }`; demo/styles/animations.css:99 defines `.vj-enter-move`. glass-ui dist/watercolor-dot.js:96,119-127 mounts a per-instance useId()-named <filter> with feTurbulence numOctaves="5" whose own header calls per-frame re-rasterization the Safari §H hazard. MAX_COLORS=12 (MixSourceSelector.vue:38) sets the worst case at 11 rebuilt filters.
```

**Reproduction.** $ node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-sourceselector/swatch-key-churn.repro.mjs (algorithm transcribed verbatim from :79-98, driven through useMixingState.removeColor/addColor) →
render 1  [red,green,blue]      keys = [ 0, 1, 2 ]
render 2  [green,blue]          keys = [ 3, 4 ]   <- green/blue DID NOT CHANGE
render 3  [green,blue,gold]     keys = [ 3, 4, 5 ]
render 4  [green,gold]          keys = [ 3, 6 ]   <- green STILL unchanged
counter   = 7

**Proposed cure.** Key on identity, not position. Mint an id at the single mint point — useMixingState.addColor returns `{ id: ++seq, css, source }` — and use `:key="sc.id"`. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/mix` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** MixSourceSelector.vue:246-268 wraps <PaletteCard> in a native <button>, producing `button > div[role=article][aria-label] > ... > button`. The HTML button content model forbids interactive descendants; the inner "Palette menu" Button becomes a tab stop inside a button and the card's role/aria-label collide with the wrapper's own :aria-label. This directly contradicts PaletteCard's documented contract.

**Mechanism.** a11y — nested interactive content; consumer overriding a component's documented semantic contract

**Evidence.**

```
MixSourceSelector.vue:246-268 (native <button> with :aria-pressed/:aria-label wrapping <PaletteCard>). PaletteCard.vue:2-4, verbatim: "W5-a11y: role=\"article\" provides a landmark for each palette; button semantics on the card are omitted because inner interactive controls must be reachable — using article + click is the correct pattern for a card container that also houses nested interactive elements." PaletteCard.vue:83-105 unconditionally renders <Button icon-only variant="ghost" size="sm" aria-label="Palette menu">; PaletteCardMeta adds a vote control on the same path.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE live — savedPalettes is empty on the probed tree so palettes mode renders EmptyState only. Static: the wrapper is unconditional in the template and the inner <Button> is unconditional in PaletteCard. Labelled a hypothesis at the live-DOM level.

**Proposed cure.** Adopt PaletteCard's contract instead of overriding it: drop the wrapper <button>, bind @click="togglePalette(palette)" to the card's own `click` emit, and express selection through the card's own state surface. If a pressed semantic is genuinely wanted on a card, it belongs in glass-ui/PaletteCard as a `selectable` mode, not a consumer-side wrapper (edicts 3 and 4).

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/mix` · C-6 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The MAX_COLORS=12 ceiling lives only in the view and only on one of the two add paths. addCurrentColor() (:69-73) checks cssColorOpaque truthiness but never canAddColor; the palette-swatch path (:220) emits addColor with no guard at all; and useMixingState.addColor (useMixingState.ts:55-57) is an unconditional append. The cap rides entirely on a :disabled attribute that C-1 proves is dropped, and becomes trivially bypassable the moment C-1 is repaired. It also duplicates an undeclared constant: mixStage.ts:29 MAX_DROPS=12 silently truncates the choreography at :157.

```
MixSourceSelector.vue:37-40 (MIN_COLORS/MAX_COLORS/canAddColor), :69-73 (addCurrentColor, no canAddColor read), :172 (the sole :disabled consumer), :220 (unguarded emit). useMixingState.ts:55-57 `selectedColors.value = [...selectedColors.value, { css, source }]` — grep for MAX in useMixingState.ts returns nothing. mixStage.ts:29 `const MAX_DROPS = 12`, :157 `origins.slice(0, MAX_DROPS)`.

### `CHALLENGE-D — assume the design is flawed (visual truth, sta` · D-5 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The count slider's horizontal axis simultaneously encodes two incompatible quantities: palette index (0..n-1 mapped to 0..100% of the track) and cardinality (count 1..12 mapped to 0..100%). The resulting affordance is affirmatively misleading.

**Mechanism.** F3 — depiction inflation. The extract k-slider pattern was transplanted without its precondition: there, track position plausibly IS cluster index; here the axis is cardinality, so the two meanings cannot coexist on one rail.

**Evidence.**

```
GenerateControls.vue:65-73 paints the track by index: `const pct = colors.length === 1 ? 50 : (i / (colors.length - 1)) * 100`. :297-307 drives the thumb by count, `:min="1" :max="12"`. Live measure at count=5: gradient stops at `0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%` while `thumbCentreFrac: 0.367` (aria-valuenow 5, min 1, max 12 → (5-1)/11 = 0.364). The five colours span the entire track while the thumb sits at 36.7% of it, so 63% of the track is painted with colours that already exist — reading as 'drag right to reach these'. The comment at :62-64 claims 'the instrument shows its own state'; it shows a second, contradictory state.
```

**Reproduction.** Navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/generate. Read `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('div[style*="linear-gradient"]')).backgroundImage` → stops at 0/25/50/75/100%. Read the slider: `document.querySelector('[role="slider"]').getAttribute('aria-valuenow')` → "5", min 1, max 12. Compute the thumb centre as a fraction of the gradient layer's rect → 0.367. The last colour sits at 100% of a track whose thumb is at 36.7%.

**Proposed cure.** Give the rail one unit. Either paint the track neutral and let it be a pure cardinality axis (the honest reading), or redefine the ramp's x-position to mean count. Then adopt the §5 domain-neutral axis composition whole — VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:104 names 'Generate count' explicitly and requires label, unit and reserved live value. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-6 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Selection ring paints the wrong ground and shares one cascade channel with the focus ring: ring-offset-2 + ring-offset-background stamps --background (never the plate the card sits on), and focus-visible:ring-2 outranks the selection ring on the same --tw-ring-* properties, so a focused selected card loses its selection colour.

**Mechanism.** Selection is drawn at the wrong level (an outer wrapper with utility rings) instead of on the producer's own selected register, so it inherits --background as its offset ground and collides with the focus utility on one custom-property channel.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured on the selected seat: box-shadow "... rgb(251,250,248) 0 0 0 2px, oklch(0.470927 0.093396 169.83403) 0 0 0 4px" (light); --tw-ring-offset-color: "hsl(24 9% 4%)" (dark), "light-dark(hsl(40 30% 98%), hsl(24 9% 4%))" (mobile). Class string (:256-261): 'focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring/40' + 'ring-2 ring-primary ring-offset-2 ring-offset-background'. Both Tailwind v4 utilities write --tw-ring-width/--tw-ring-color/--tw-ring-shadow; .focus-visible\:ring-2:focus-visible has specificity 0,2,0 vs .ring-2 at 0,1,0. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1: "boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier" and "Focus remains visibly distinct from selection in both schemes, forced colors and reduced transparency." Light capture also shows the ring occluding the card's cartoon-surface cast that its unselected sibling keeps.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE for the focus collision — HYPOTHESIS. WebKit/macOS omits buttons from Tab order by default (60 Tab presses never reached the seat) and the Chromium arm did not receive the seeded library; the offset-ground and cast-occlusion halves ARE measured (probe-mix.mjs palettesMode.afterSelect + scratchpad/mix-palettes-light-1440.png).

**Proposed cure.** Selection moves onto the producer's pressed seat (with D-5) and uses a register that is not the focus channel — a producer-owned selected face/border rung — leaving focus-visible as the sole owner of --tw-ring-*. The ring-offset against --background dies with the wrapper.

```

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-11 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The one motion the component designs is architecturally prevented: TransitionGroup keys embed the array index, so removing one chip invalidates every surviving chip's key — the row plays three leaves and two enters instead of one leave plus a move, and the shared .vj-enter-move neighbour reflow can never fire.

**Mechanism.** SelectedColor ({css, source}) carries no identity, so the site manufactured one from position — which is exactly the quantity a removal changes.

**Evidence.**

```
MixSourceSelector.vue:79-89 keys on `${sc.css}::${i}`. Exact algorithm replay (node -e): initial [0,1,2] -> after removing index 0 [3,4] -> re-add [0,1,2] -> duplicates [0,5]. demo/styles/utils.css:168-178 exists precisely so "neighbours reflow on the family move class" (.vj-enter-move); with index-bearing keys no element survives to be moved. The watch at :90-98 then prunes the map, guaranteeing keys are never reused.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE in the running app (the populated state is unreachable per D-1). Algorithm replayed exactly: node -e '<swatchKeys replay>' — output pasted in the report §D-11.

**Proposed cure.** Mint identity at the source: useMixingState.addColor stamps a stable id on each SelectedColor; the key becomes sc.id and the key map, the counter and the pruning watcher (~20 lines) are deleted outright.

Full state table in the report: custom UNHANDLED, hovered DESIGNED WRONG (D-03), pressed ZERO SURFACE DELTA (D-02), focused CLIPPED (D-11) and louder than selection (D-12), overflowing UNHANDLED (D-10), RTL BROKEN (D-05), forced-colors BROKEN (D-06); reduced-motion HANDLED; empty/loading/error correctly n/a (build-time constant catalogue); zoom 200% no change vs 1440.
```

**Reproduction.** Open /#/gradient, expand the interval, press the sliders icon to disclose the authoring canvas, drag either control point to any non-preset position. Head reads `custom`; `document.querySelectorAll('.specimen-tile[data-state="on"]').length` -> 0. (Derived from the code path with certainty — the DOM consequence is structural, not probabilistic.)

**Proposed cure.** `custom` is a first-class specimen state and needs a rendered register. Either give the strip an explicit `custom` tile, or make the strip's no-tile-pressed state visibly and textually MEAN custom so it agrees with the head — the kf precedent quoted at easingCatalogue.ts:215-217 puts Custom in the sidebar, which the constitution's Easing composition also supplies as the code inspector.

**Mechanism.** A hand-maintained copy of a generated truth. vite.config.ts derives its self-alias set FROM package.json#exports precisely so it "can never drift"; the typecheck half is hand-written and drifted. Because TS paths substitution pre-empts exports resolution, deleting "./color" from the exports map leaves the demo typecheck GREEN while every real consumer breaks — a false proof of the public API, plus 3 dangling targets.

**Evidence.**

```
exports (7): ./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize. tsconfig.demo.json paths (8): . /color /parsing /math /easing /units /transform /quantize. `ls dist/index.d.ts dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts dist/subpaths/units.d.ts` → all three 'No such file or directory'. tsc --traceResolution, two imports in the SAME file demo/color-session/generate-color.ts: '/color' → "'paths' option is specified... Trying substitution './dist/subpaths/color.d.ts'... use it as a name resolution result" (no 'Entering conditional exports', no Package ID); '/css' → "Entering conditional exports. Matched 'exports' condition 'types'. Using 'exports' subpath './css'... with Package ID '@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts@4.0.0'". The tsconfig header asserts "the exports map is a CLOSED 8-key set" — it is a closed 7-key set with different names.
```

**Reproduction.** npx tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit --traceResolution 2>&1 | grep -iE "value\.js/(css|color)'" -A 6  — shows the two divergent mechanisms; `ls dist/index.d.ts dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts dist/subpaths/units.d.ts` exits 1 on all three.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the @mkbabb/value.js* paths block from tsconfig.demo.json outright — self-reference through package.json#exports already resolves (the /css trace proves it, with a real Package ID), so all seven subpaths would resolve through the genuine exports map and removing a subpath would turn the demo typecheck red, which is what a dogfood is for. ### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-3 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The rail axis is mapped twice over two different boxes: the forward map (pointer -> position) is TypeScript over the BORDER box (getBoundingClientRect), while the inverse map (position -> pixels) is CSS calc where `100%` resolves against the PADDING box. They disagree by the 1px border at each end, so the two maps are not inverse.

**Mechanism.** one geometric law with two implementations in two languages over two coordinate origins; the CSS one silently changes meaning if a border or padding is ever added to .gradient-rail

**Evidence.**

```
GradientStopEditor.vue:75-81 (forward: origin rect.left=224, span rect.width-20=442) vs :55-57 (inverse: `calc(10px + (100% - 20px) * p/100)` where 100%=460, origin=225). LIVE measured: rail x=224.0 width=462.0 borderLeft=1px; handle "Gradient stop at 0%" style.left="calc(0% + 10px)" measured centre cx=235; handle "…100%" style.left="calc(100% - 10px)" cx=675. Forward map at those exact pixels: pos(235)=0.226, pos(675)=99.774. LIVE confirmation: clicking the bar at x=235 — the exact pixel where the 0% handle is painted, at y=railTop+4 so the bar owns the gesture — minted a stop at 0.2%, rendered `style.left="calc(0.2% + 9.96px)"`, cx=235.88.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/gradient -> in the console, click the rail at exactly `bar.getBoundingClientRect().x + 11` with clientY = rail top + 4 -> the new stop reads 0.2%, not 0%, and its handle lands ~0.9px right of the pointer. Error is antisymmetric: 0 at 50%, ±0.23% at the ends.

**Proposed cure.** A single useRailGeometry(el, halfPx) exposing toPosition(clientX) and toOffsetPx(position) over ONE box, built on clamp+scale from @mkbabb/value.js/math, with the handle positioned in px rather than calc(%) so the two directions are provably inverse. Ghost and handle then ride the same map by construction.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-4 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The self-declared "ONE sampling law" is implemented twice, and the model's interpolation space never reaches the emitted CSS. GradientVisualizer.colorAtPosition re-implements the interval walk / easing / mix that sampleCoalescedStops owns, then injects it into this component as an optional function prop — so the ghost dot and the rail it floats over are painted by two different implementations. Separately, rampGradient emits `linear-gradient(90deg, …)` with no `in <space>` clause, so the browser blends between sub-stops in sRGB while the model's law is oklch; COALESCE_RESOLUTION=32 exists to make that error small, i.e. the coalescing machinery is a polyfill for a CSS Color 4 feature the target browsers already ship.

**Mechanism.** the concept "the colour of this ramp at position p" has no exported home, so it leaks into a component prop; and the model's declared interpolation space is dropped at the serialization boundary, forcing a 32-sample approximation of an exact platform feature

**Evidence.**

```
useGradientCSS.ts:171-174 declares "The ONE sampling law"; useGradientCSS.ts:175-216 implements it; GradientVisualizer.vue:64-88 re-implements it and passes it as `:color-at` (GradientVisualizer.vue:139) into GradientStopEditor.vue:16. useGradientCSS.ts:223 `return \`linear-gradient(90deg, ${parts.join(", ")})\`` — no interpolation-space clause though model.interpolationSpace is in scope. Live computed --rail-ramp confirms: `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(75% …) 80.00%, …)`, no `in oklch`.
```

**Reproduction.** Structural — two call sites, both quoted with file:line. The sRGB-vs-oklch deviation between adjacent sub-stops is bounded by the 32-sample density and was NOT separately measured: that half is labelled a HYPOTHESIS.

**Proposed cure.** model/sample.ts exports both sampleAt(model, position) -> AnyColor (the ghost AND the bar-click mint) and sampleRamp(model); model/serialize.ts emits `linear-gradient(<dir> in <space>, …)` and coalesces ONLY across intervals whose easing is non-linear. Since parseGradientCSS seeds every parsed interval to the `linear` preset (gradientParse.ts:295-298), the common case collapses to an exact two-stop `linear-gradient(in oklch, …)`. The colorAt prop is deleted.

**Mechanism.** Unique semantic ownership violated twice: the concept is absent from @mkbabb/value.js (the constellation's colour library), present in @mkbabb/glass-ui (a UI library — itself an inversion of dependency direction), and privately re-implemented a third time in demo/.

**Evidence.**

```
PRODUCER: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/color/index.d.ts:81 `export type ColorHarmony = "analogous"|"complementary"|"split-complementary"|"triad"|"tetradic"|"monochrome"`, :87 `deriveHue(anchorHue, harmony, hueSpread, t)`; documented at dist/components/aurora/composables/color.d.ts:29-34 as 'the PUBLIC alias of the shared ColorHarmony vocabulary … The blob and aurora derive from this ONE union.' DEMO RIVAL: demo/color-session/generate-color.ts:68-85 `HARMONY_NAMES = ["golden","analogous","complementary","triadic","split-complementary","random"]` with its own generateHues at :93-149. CONSUMERS: GenerateControls.vue:264-278 (+capitalize at :83-85) renders 'Triadic'; demo/scenes/atmosphere/AuroraPane.vue:121-127, typed AuroraHarmony=ColorHarmony via @mkbabb/glass-ui/aurora, renders the glass-ui union with 'triad'.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — static, but exhaustively enumerated: the two unions, their two generators, and their two rendered menus are all cited at file:line above. The user-visible 'Triadic' vs 'triad' divergence is derivable from the two type declarations plus the two capitalisation paths.

**Proposed cure.** One vocabulary, one home, and the home is the colour library, not the component library. Fold ColorHarmony into pass-1's proposed `@mkbabb/value.js/palette` subpath and have glass-ui CONSUME it (colour vocabulary flowing library → design system, not the reverse); retire the demo's rival. RF-17 library-evolution wave — 4.0.0 is immutable, so this is a next-cut row, not a megatranche edit.

```
`grep -rn "export function serialize|export const serialize" src/css/ src/easing.ts` → serializeCssColor, serializeKeyframeSelector, serializeCssValue, serializeTimelineOptions — no timing-function serializer, while `/css` exports `parseTimingFunction` (src/subpaths/css.ts). The identity match at easingCatalogue.ts:220 (`SPECIMEN_TILES.find(t => t.css === interval.css)`) is a string compare, so it returns undefined, `tileIdFor` returns null, `specimenNameFor` (line 229) returns "custom" — all 30 bezier tiles render unpressed and every closed specimen row's head reads `custom` for a named preset, with no error raised anywhere.

**Proposed cure.** Add `serializeTimingFunction(ast: CssTimingFunction): string` to `src/css/`, exported from `/css` as the exact inverse of `parseTimingFunction`, round-trip tested in the existing test/bbnf-equivalence idiom. `bezierLiteral`/`stepsLiteral` delete; glass-ui's private minter delegates. ### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-5 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** Interval identity is positional while stop identity is id-based, and the two are synced across modules by a length-only watcher that appends/truncates at the end — so inserting or removing a stop silently reassigns authored curves to the wrong stop pairs.

**Mechanism.** a shadow array with no modelled identity, kept in size by a length signal that carries no positional information, in a different module from the identity-bearing collection it shadows.

**Evidence.**

```
useGradientModel.ts:33-37 (GradientStop has `id`); intervals have none. useGradientModel.ts:89-100 `watch(() => stops.value.length, len => { …intervals.value.push(linearInterval()); … intervals.value.length = needed })` — told only THAT the length changed, never WHERE. `removeStop` (122-125) removes by id from anywhere. `addStop` (116-120) sorts by position so an inserted stop can land first. The subject cements the ordinal contract: GradientEasingEditor.vue:48-50 `"update-interval": [index: number, …]` → useGradientModel.ts:134-140 `updateInterval(index, value)`.
```

**Reproduction.** Source-derived (all three sites quoted in the report). 1) initial `stops=[A@0%,B@100%]`, `intervals=[linear]` (useGradientModel.ts:79-83). 2) press `ease-out-back` on row `1 → 2` → `updateInterval(0,…)` → `intervals=[back]`. 3) click the rail near 0% → GradientVisualizer.vue:91 `addStop(...)` → sorted, new stop lands FIRST. 4) watcher sees len 2→3 and pushes `linearInterval()` at the END → `intervals=[back, linear]`. 5) `back`, authored for A→B, is now interval 0 = N→A; A→B is linear. Symmetrically `removeStop(firstStopId)` drops the LAST interval, shifting every curve one pair left; the specimen rows relabel (useSpecimenRows.ts:61) and report the wrong assignment as truth. Live confirmation was ABANDONED — the shared dev browser at :9000 is under concurrent control by other seats (the page self-navigated /#/gradient → /#/extract → /#/atmosphere mid-evaluate; other seats' ?probe=4 / ?pro

**Proposed cure.** Architectural transposition: the easing belongs to the LEADING STOP, not a parallel array — `interface GradientStop { id; cssColor; position; easing: AuthoredEasing }` (the last stop's easing is simply unused). The length watcher DELETES; add/remove become identity-correct by construction; `updateInterval(index,…)` becomes `updateStop(id, { easing })` — the same id-addressed door every other mutation already uses; the subject's emit becomes `"update-easing": [stopId: string, value: AuthoredEasing]`; useSpecimenRows derives rows by a pairwise walk over one array instead of zipping two.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-5 · CHALLENGE-L

Root cause at useMixingState.ts:26-29: `export interface SelectedColor { css: string; source: string; }` — no identity field.
```

Replace with the selector the consumer actually wants, taking the palette rather than pixels, and move the chroma tiebreak into the library where the color math lives: `export function dominantOf(palette: readonly QuantizedColor[]): QuantizedColor | null`. ### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** value.js's public `/css` surface parses timing functions but cannot serialize them, so the CSS-literal minting law is hand-implemented THREE times across two packages: glass-ui's `useEasingPicker.readout`, this component's `bezierLiteral`/`stepsLiteral`, and a frozen third copy in `linearInterval()`.

**Mechanism.** asymmetric public surface: a grammar module that parses but does not serialize forces every consumer to hand-mint the inverse. N consumers → N copies of one law, each maintained by comment rather than by code.

**Evidence.**

```
src/subpaths/css.ts:53 exports `parseTimingFunction`, :54 exports `serializeCssColor` — the color grammar is symmetric, the timing grammar is not. `grep -rn "export function serialize" src/` → serializeCssValue, serializeCssColor, serializeKeyframeSelector, serializeTimelineOptions; NO serializeTimingFunction anywhere. Copy 1: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/easing/composables/useEasingPicker.d.ts `readout: ComputedRef<string>` ("The complete re-parseable readout literal"). Copy 2: easingCatalogue.ts:48-56, whose comment at :41-45 declares it mirrors glass-ui byte-for-byte. Copy 3: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:56 `css: "cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)"` hardcoded. easingCatalogue.ts:44-45 names copy 3 as its own precedent "generalized to the whole catalogue". `bezierLiteral`/`stepsLiteral` are exported but consumed only inside their own file (grep: 4 hits, all in easingCatalogue.ts) — dead public surface on top of duplicated law.
```

**Reproduction.** `grep -n "parseTimingFunction\|serializeCssColor" src/subpaths/css.ts` → :53 :54; `grep -rn "export function serialize" src/` → 4 hits, none for timing. Then `grep -rn "toFixed(3)" demo src --include=*.ts --include=*.vue` shows the demo's mirror at easingCatalogue.ts:49.

**Proposed cure.** value.js `/css` exports `serializeTimingFunction(ast: CssTimingFunction): string` — the exact inverse of `parseTimingFunction`, with `parse ∘ serialize ≡ id` as a round-trip property test over the whole bezierPresets corpus + the steps space. glass-ui's `readout`, `bezierLiteral`, `stepsLiteral` and `linearInterval`'s frozen string all collapse into one call; the "byte-identity with the picker" law stops being a cross-package comment and becomes a fact of the grammar module. Same shape the library already got right for colors.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-4 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** A 27-tile, 133-DOM-node selection strip is mounted for EVERY interval row inside `v-show`, although `openInterval` is a single ref so at most one row can ever be open. The subtree-scoped querySelector workaround exists solely to survive the duplication it should have prevented.

```
GradientEasingEditor.vue:61 `const openInterval = ref<number | null>(0)` (single); :112 `v-for="row in specimenRows"`; :144 `v-show="openInterval === row.index"` (mounts); :152 the cheap ramp IS gated `v-if="openInterval === row.index && openIntervalRamp"`; :161 `<EasingSpecimenStrip>` is NOT gated. The component documents the consequence and works around it rather than removing it — EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:38-40 "scoped to THIS strip's own subtree (sibling rows mount hidden twins of every data-specimen id)". ### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure / module boundaries / owners` · L-18 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The sampler reads the alpha byte from the canvas and discards it. `data[3]` is never referenced; the offscreen canvas is created without `{alpha:false}`, and `image/*` is accepted, so a transparent PNG pixel is reported and saved as opaque #000000.

**Mechanism.** a lossy carrier (6-digit hex string) chosen where the library's own byte↔color pair is alpha-complete in both directions

**Evidence.**

```
useImageSampler.ts:116-118 (`formatHex(data[0], data[1], data[2])` — data[3] absent), :32-35 (`formatHex` has no alpha parameter), :83 (getContext without alpha:false); demo/workbenches/extract/ImageDropZone.vue:30 `accept="image/*"`. ```

**Reproduction.** Drop any logo PNG with a transparent background on /#/extract, open the eyedropper, sample the transparent region: readout claims #000000 and 'Add to palette' writes an opaque black swatch. No warning.

**Proposed cure.** Stop going through a hex string: `rgb(data[0], data[1], data[2], data[3] / 255)`. Alpha survives end-to-end and the display side is already ready. Pairs with the first pass's `fromRgba8` proposal for src/color/operations.ts.

**Defect.** The magnifier is DPR-blind: a fixed 110x110 backing store for a 110 CSS-px box, so on any devicePixelRatio > 1 the one surface whose job is pixel fidelity is composited upscaled. glass-ui publishes the DPR policy; zero demo modules consume it; a sibling workbench re-derives it by hand.

### `L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, directi` · L-r2-2 · L

**Defect.** The gradient's persisted domain type IS a Vue widget's v-model payload: `GradientInterval = EasingPickerValue`, imported from @mkbabb/glass-ui/easing. Three of its six fields are written only to satisfy the widget's type and read by nothing in the gradient tree.

### `L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, directi` · L-r2-3 · L

**Defect.** An invariant module-level catalogue (27 specimen tiles) and a full EasingPicker are instantiated once PER INTERVAL inside the v-for, though at most one row is open at a time. One interval row is 30.9% of the whole route's DOM.

**Mechanism.** Shared, stateless, invariant UI placed inside the iteration that consumes it — cost linear in interval count for a single-open surface.

**Evidence.**

SPECIMEN_FAMILIES is a module const (easingCatalogue.ts:198), identical in every row. openInterval is a single `ref<number|null>` (GradientEasingEditor.vue:61). Three downstream workarounds exist because of it: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:41 ("sibling rows mount hidden twins of every data-specimen id"), its rowEl-scoped querySelector (:55) and no-scrollIntoView rule (:39-46, the O-19 flat-netting root cause), and the v-show-never-v-if picker law (GradientEasingEditor.vue:16-18).

### `L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, directi` · L-r2-5 · L

**Defect.** Four names for three types across the value.js↔glass-ui seam, bridged by two casts in this component's catalogue — and value.js declares the jump union TWICE, independently, in one file, with a runtime membership check guarding a type the compiler already closes.

**Evidence.**

Casts: easingCatalogue.ts:136 `const position = term as JumpPosition;` and :108/:123 `[...points] as BezierPoints`.

### `L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, directi` · L-r2-8 · L

**Defect.** value.js is failure-explicit by design but publishes no unwrap: no subpath exports ok/err or an unwrap helper, only the Result type. The demo hand-rolls the unwrap-or-throw 17 times, twice as the same function five files apart.

**Mechanism.** A library published the discipline (explicit Result) and withheld the ergonomic, so seventeen consumers re-invented the escape hatch, each with its own message format and none with a shared type.

**Evidence.**

```
`cat src/foundation/result.ts` → exports only `Result`, `ok`, `err`; src/subpaths/color.ts:9 exports the Result TYPE alone; no subpath exports an unwrap. `grep -rn "throw new Error(\`" demo --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue' | grep -i error.code` → 17 sites (useGradientCSS.ts ×3, useGradientInterpolation.ts:37, easingCatalogue.ts:103, mixStage.ts:106, useMarkdownColors.ts ×2, generate-color.ts ×3, color-utils.ts:18, ink.ts ×4, palettes/mix.ts:36). Five are in this component's own chain. useGradientCSS.ts:71-77 and easingCatalogue.ts:98-104 are the SAME function, differing only in the error prefix; both are typed `ReturnType<typeof CubicBezier>` while also fed steppedEase results, which type-checks only by coincidence of shape.
```

**Reproduction.** The grep above returns 17 hand-rolled sites; `diff` the two easingValue bodies (useGradientCSS.ts:71-77, easingCatalogue.ts:98-104) — identical but for the string literal.

**Proposed cure.** Publish the unwrap from the foundation as an eighth subpath: `export function unwrap<T, E extends {code: string}>(r: Result<T,E>, context: string): T { if (r.ok) return r.value; throw new Error(`${context}: ${r.error.code}`); }`. Seventeen hand-rolled sites collapse to seventeen call sites of one function with one message grammar, and easingValue stops existing twice.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/color-picke` · C-7 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Every boot rewrites the address bar with a colour the user never picked, violating the hydrate.ts 'born hydrated, ONE commit' law App.vue's own comment asserts.

**Mechanism.** An identity-changing write performed for a value-level clamp, observed by an identity-based watcher — the boot commits a URL write no user action requested.

**Evidence.**

```
Clean browser context (empty localStorage) loading http://localhost:9000/#/generate settles at http://localhost:9000/#/generate?space=lab&color=lab(92%25+88.8+20+/+82.7%25) — measured in every isolated probe run. Mechanism code: useColorPipeline.ts:50-52 unconditionally re-assigns model.value at setup (clampColorToSpaceDomain returns a fresh object; the `if (model.value.color)` guard is always true), tripping the identity-based watcher at useColorUrl.ts:79-82 → router.replace. App.vue:245 then :377 fix the composition order; App.vue:369-376 claims the opposite ('an idempotent re-commit').
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/probe-app.mjs (fresh context per run) — read `location.href` after load; it always carries ?space=&color= even with empty storage and a bare hash.

**Proposed cure.** Make the boot clamp a no-op write: compare the clamped colour to the incoming one and skip the assignment when nothing changed (or clamp inside hydrate before the ref exists, which is where the ordering law already says the first value is decided).

**Defect.** Two owners of "read the colour out of the URL"; the router-side reader is inert at boot (vue-router's initial navigation is asynchronous, so `route.query` is empty during App setup) and its result is logically subsumed by the hydration source, making the `!appliedFromUrl` guard term unable to change any branch.

**Mechanism.** dual ownership of one concept, one instance vestigial after a transposition

**Evidence.**

```
Reader 1: demo/color-picker/composables/boot/hydrate.ts:51-61 hand-parses the hash with URLSearchParams, requires both space+color. Reader 2: demo/color-session/useColorUrl.ts:26-31 reads route.query.space/color, requires both. hydrate.ts:49-50's stated justification ("runs before router installation") is false — index.html:211 `app.use(router)` precedes :212 `app.mount()`, so App setup runs after installation. The real mechanism: node_modules/vue-router/dist/vue-router.js:1462-1466 starts the initial navigation with `push(routerHistory.location)` — a Promise — inside `install`, so `currentRoute.value` is still START_LOCATION_NORMALIZED (query {}) when App's setup runs synchronously inside app.mount(). Hence useColorUrl.ts:70 `const appliedFromUrl = applyUrlToModel()` is false on every cold load. Subsumption: both readers require both params, so appliedFromUrl===true ⟹ hydration.source==="url", and App.vue:378 `if (!appliedFromUrl && hydration.source !== "url")` already gates on the latter.
```

**Reproduction.** Deterministic source read, both halves: vue-router.js:1462-1466 (async navigation start) + index.html:210-212 (synchronous mount ordering) + the conjunct-subsumption argument over hydrate.ts:51-61 vs useColorUrl.ts:26-31.

**Proposed cure.** hydrate.ts owns the FIRST value (already correct); useColorUrl owns the LIVE sync only — delete its boot-time applyUrlToModel() call and the appliedFromUrl return, and reduce App.vue:378 to `if (hydration.source !== "url") restoreFromStorage();`. One owner per phase. Correct hydrate.ts:49-50's rationale to the real one (the router's initial navigation is a promise) — that is the fact a future reader needs.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-25 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Non-concentric corner: the full-bleed colour strip carries the card's OUTER 16px radius while sitting at the border's INNER edge, where 14px is required. Together with three stacked zero-blur casters this is the mechanism behind the owner's own mark, which the prior seat's report never references.

**Mechanism.** Clip responsibility was moved onto the child (to avoid 1-bit rasterization at compositing-layer bounds) without moving the radius arithmetic with it. Three copies of a 16px arc at three offsets diverge maximally at the rounds and converge along the straight edges, so the cast reads clean on the sides and faceted/stepped at the corners.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured live: card `border-top-left-radius: 16px`, `border-top-width: 2px`, strip inset from card left = `2px` (i.e. exactly at the inner edge), strip `border-top-left-radius: 16px`. Concentric requirement = 16 − 2 = **14px**. Owner artifact: `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/owner-marked/OM-2-card-shadow-sharp-corners.png`. Shadow half, computed: `oklab(0.28 …/0.32) -3px 3px 0px 0px, oklab(0.28 …/0.26) -5px 5px 0px 0px, oklab(0.28 …/0.18) -7px 7px 0px 0px` — three hard copies, zero blur, zero spread. Radius applied at PaletteCard.vue:36 (`rounded-t-card`), forced by the deliberate refusal of overflow-hidden at :16-18.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with any populated palette; read `border-top-left-radius`/`border-top-width` on `[role="article"]` and `border-top-left-radius` + `getBoundingClientRect().left` delta on its strip child. Visual: owner-marked/OM-2-card-shadow-sharp-corners.png.

**Proposed cure.** The concentric arithmetic should never be authored by hand. Cure step 1 (`<Card … :shadow="false">`) removes the three casters and therefore the visible artefact; the strip radius then belongs to a producer-side inner-radius token (`calc(var(--radius-card) - var(--card-border-width))`) rather than a repeated `rounded-t-card` literal at the consumer.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-26 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** In dark mode the cel shadow is effectively the same luminance as the surface casting it, and the alpha was raised to compensate rather than the contrast fixed.

**Mechanism.** A hard-edged cel shadow requires luminance headroom beneath the surface; a dark card has none, so the register degrades to a grey smear whose only surviving signal is the offset silhouette. The alpha bump from .32 to .46 is evidence someone noticed the weak read and compensated with opacity instead of contrast.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured on the same element, light vs `.dark`: card `background-color` `oklab(0.913 …)` → `oklab(0.345 …)`; shadow colour `oklab(0.28 …)` → `oklab(0.34 …)`; alphas .32/.26/.18 → **.46/.38/.26**. L(shadow) − L(card) = **−0.633 light** vs **−0.005 dark**. Token: `--shadow-cartoon-md` uses `light-dark(hsl(24 10% 10%), hsl(30 14% 90%))` then `clamp(0.28, l, 0.34)`, so the dark arm takes the LIGHT source colour and clamps it down to 0.34 — landing on the card's own 0.345.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/palettes; read `boxShadow` and `backgroundColor` on `[role="article"]`, then `document.documentElement.classList.add('dark')` and read both again.

**Proposed cure.** Not a token patch — the ruled tuple already says `shadow: false` for this species (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.1). Cure step 1 removes the caster entirely; a matte specimen slip needs no cast shadow on either scheme. If any producer follow-up is warranted it is a letter to glass-ui that `--shadow-cartoon-md`'s dark arm clamps into its own surface band.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-27 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The identity row has no overflow design in any direction: once the title is starved to 0 (D-2), the remaining `shrink-0` content exits the card box and then the viewport. The prior seat measured a 37px chip↔menu overlap; the mechanism is unbounded.

**Mechanism.** Title absorbs 100% of negative free space (line-clamp's overflow:hidden zeroes its automatic minimum), reaches 0, and the remaining unshrinkable content simply overflows. `REPORT.md`'s `horizontalOverflow: 0` misses it because an ancestor clips before the document scroll width grows — the content is lost, not merely off-screen.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-16 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** cardRefs is a deep-reactive map of component public instances whose entries are never released, because the ref callback's `el &&` guard skips the unmount null.

**Mechanism.** Local hygiene — imperative child-instance coupling stored in the wrong reactivity primitive with no teardown.

**Evidence.**

```
BrowsePane.vue:209 `const cardRefs = reactive<Record<string, InstanceType<typeof PaletteCard>>>({});` and :94 `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.slug] = el)"`. Vue invokes the function ref with null on unmount; the guard skips that call, so no key is ever deleted. `reactive` (not shallowReactive/markRaw) means each read returns a reactive proxy wrapping a component public instance, so property access is tracked inside the component's own instance graph. `grep -rn "shallowReactive|markRaw" demo/palettes/` → zero hits.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE for the accumulation arm — requires a reachable API to populate and page the wall past the 50-cap. Labelled a hypothesis on runtime consequence; the code shape (no delete path, deep reactive) is confirmed.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the ref map entirely — the feedback it drives belongs in the inspector D-03 is missing (see D-17). If a collection must survive, use a plain Map with an explicit null-branch delete.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-11 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Motion: an untokenized magic 50ms delay, a Transition mode="out-in" + nextTick focus race that almost certainly leaves the input unfocused in a real browser, and a max-height transition arm that is a no-op while its overflow:hidden side effect still clips.

**Mechanism.** transition mode and imperative focus timing chosen independently; a magic constant standing in for a real settle signal

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteSlugBar.vue:4 `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` around a v-if/v-else pair; :176-181 `setTimeout(() => { slugEditMode.value = true; nextTick(() => searchBarRef.value?.inputRef?.focus()); }, 50)`. 50 is not any --duration-* or --spring-* token in demo/styles/animations.css. Under mode="out-in" Vue mounts the incoming branch only in the outgoing branch's afterLeave, long after nextTick, so searchBarRef is null and ?. swallows the focus. animations.css:104-119 gives .vj-morph-*-active a max-height transition parameterised by --vj-morph-collapse/--vj-morph-expanded plus overflow:hidden; this site sets neither (scoped block :239-243 is a comment and an @reference only). CREDIT: reduced motion is satisfied for free by the global guard (animations.css:80).
```

**Reproduction.** NEGATIVE in jsdom — probe P1 reports `input present = true, activeElement = INPUT, focused input? = true`, because jsdom reports no transition duration so Vue resolves the leave synchronously. The failure is real-browser-only and I could not produce the frame: the component mounts in no browser (D-1). LABELLED A HYPOTHESIS for the focus arm. Corroboration: the live successor SlugEditLayer.vue:16-23 dropped BOTH the Transition and the setTimeout and focuses directly.

**Proposed cure.** Drop the out-in Transition around a control swap (or focus from the transition's after-enter hook, not nextTick), and delete the 50ms guess — the live successor already proves neither is needed.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-10 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** tsconfig.demo.json's `paths` block advertises a value.js public surface that package.json#exports does not have — three phantom keys pointing at files that do not exist, two real exports omitted — and its own header states the wrong map.

**Mechanism.** A hand-maintained second copy of a generated map — a false public surface advertised by the very config that is meant to be the trust boundary.

**Evidence.**

```
`node -p "Object.keys(require('./package.json').exports).join(' ')"` → `./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize` (7 keys, NO root "."). tsconfig.demo.json paths keys → `@mkbabb/value.js @mkbabb/value.js/color /parsing /math /easing /units /transform /quantize`. Phantoms: bare root (target ./dist/index.d.ts — absent; `ls dist/` shows subpaths/ + 3 chunks), /parsing (dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts — absent), /units (absent). Omitted: /css and /value (both real exports). The header asserts "the bare `.` root + the 7 subpath barrels … a CLOSED 8-key set". vite.config.ts:41-50 GENERATES its alias set from package.json#exports so it "can never drift"; tsconfig hand-maintains a second, drifted copy. Latent break: `import … from "@mkbabb/value.js"` typechecks via paths but has no Vite alias (no `.` export) → falls to node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 → ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. Currently zero such demo imports (grep → one prose mention at demo/shared/utils.ts:12).
```

**Reproduction.** Compare the two key sets above; `ls dist/subpaths/` shows color css easing math quantize transform value — no parsing, no units, and no dist/index.d.ts.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the six @mkbabb/value.js* paths entries. `tsc --traceResolution` proves TypeScript already resolves the whole map through Node self-name resolution honouring `exports` exactly as a real consumer does (measured on /css) — strictly more faithful than the paths shortcut. Removing them makes drift impossible rather than merely discouraged.

**Defect.** `action-rotate` composes two `forwards` animations that both animate `transform`; the pulse's authored three-stop scale curve is silently discarded.

**Mechanism.** two keyframe sets composed on the same element with overlapping property tracks; the later name silently wins the whole property

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/ActionButton.vue:124-136 — `.action-rotate { animation: action-pulse 0.4s … forwards, action-spin 0.4s … forwards; }` where action-pulse sets transform scale(1.3)->1.15->1 and action-spin sets rotate(0) scale(1.3) -> rotate(-360deg) scale(1). CSS Animations 1 §3: when two animations set the same property, the one later in the animation-name list wins. Both confirmed running at runtime: anims=["action-pulse-29f59cb1","action-spin-29f59cb1"].
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/gradient; click the `Reset` (rotateOnClick) action button and read svg.getAnimations() — both animations present, only action-spin's transform observable.

**Proposed cure.** Fold the rotation into a single `action-rotate` keyframe set carrying scale, stroke and rotation together — one animation, one authored curve. Edict 6 is satisfied: the motion is moved, not deleted.

**Defect.** The resting mask erases the field's right border and both right corner radii, and fades the accent-stroked send arrow into the page ground — a pink glyph on a background dissolving to pink.

A mask applies to the element's whole rendering including border and box-shadow. frames/A-rest-light.png read directly: the white field dissolves into the pink page across its right 40px, the right border and corner radii are gone, the box reads as unclosed, and the pink arrow sits in the middle of the dissolve.

**Reproduction.** frames/A-rest-light.png + frames/probe-1.json A-rest-light.styles. .color-input:focus clears the mask (:303-306) and frames/C-overflow-dark.png confirms the focused box is whole — so the defect is exclusively in the resting state, which is the state the entire visual census captured.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shell/dock/Colo` · R3-8 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Whether the user's first invalid input reports at all depends on how the page booted — and the dominant boot path is the silent one. `initialParse` survives boot to eat the user's first real error.

**Mechanism.** a boot-scoped suppression latch on app-lifetime state, whose consumption depends on persistence and URL state invisible to the user

**Evidence.**

```
useColorParsing.ts:50,86,88 — initialParse starts true and suppresses the first failure's flash. The only consumer is restoreFromStorage -> parseAndSetColor(storedInput) at useColorPersistence.ts:73, gated twice: demo/color-picker/App.vue:378 `if (!appliedFromUrl && hydration.source !== "url") restoreFromStorage();` and useColorPersistence.ts:68 `if (!hadPersistedColor) return false;`. hydrate.ts:100-127 builds the model directly and never calls parseAndSetColor. So URL-colour boot -> silent; first-ever visit -> silent; returning visit without a URL colour -> flashes. The app writes the colour into its own URL: every observed load landed on `.../#/?color=%23abcdef` or `.../#/?space=lab&color=...` (REPORT.json /#/ probe.url, all four matrices).
```

**Reproduction.** Code path traced end to end (App.vue:378 -> useColorPersistence.ts:68,73 -> useColorParsing.ts:50,86,88) plus REPORT.json probe.url across all four matrices. Sharpens round-1 C-6 from 'the first invalid input produces no error' to 'whether an error appears at all is a function of state the user cannot see' — two bug reports saying 'nothing happened' and 'it flashed red' can be the same build.

**Proposed cure.** Delete initialParse. Its job — don't flash red at a user who has not typed yet — is already done correctly by the callers: the boot paths that seed the model no longer go through parseAndSetColor at all (hydrate.ts), and the one that does (restoreFromStorage) is restoring a value the user themselves last committed. A latch that survives boot to eat a real error is a masking fallback (edict 2).

**Mechanism.** an inverse lookup performed by linear search because the inverse index was never built alongside the forward one

**Evidence.**

```
useCustomColorNames.ts:61-66 walks normalizedCustomNames (name -> xyz) comparing values. Callers: formattedCurrentColor, currentColorMeta, canProposeName (three scans per invalidation) and savedColorLabel at useColorNameResolution.ts:48-53 (once per saved swatch). getApprovedColorNames accepts limit up to 500 (api/src/modules/color/schema.ts:27) and the demo passes none (color-names.ts:23-31), so the registry is server-sized. ```

**Reproduction.** Same harness, test E in roundtrip.probe.ts. Not currently hot only because R3-3's 100 ms debounce caps invalidations at ~10/s — fixing R3-3 as prescribed removes that accidental cap, so the two must be repaired together.

**Proposed cure.** Build the inverse index (xyz -> name) inside the same loop that builds normalizedCustomNames at useCustomColorNames.ts:20-33. One extra Map.set, O(1) lookups, and the collision case of R3-2 becomes visible at registry-build time — which is where it wants to be caught.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-14 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Direction and bidi: every offset is physical, and the field renders a CSS-colour string with no LTR isolation.

**Mechanism.** Physical-axis geometry plus an un-isolated LTR technical value inside a container that may be RTL — under RTL a value beginning with `#` or `/` reorders on screen while the model keeps the original bytes, so what the user reads is not what the parser receives.

**Evidence.**

```
ColorInput.vue physical offsets: `pr-9` (:18), `right-2` (:35), `.send-btn { right: 0.25rem }` (:337), `.error-badge { right: 0.5rem }` (:350), `mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, …)` (:300). No `dir` attribute and no `unicode-bidi: isolate` on the value (measured attribute list: data-v-…, contenteditable, role, aria-label, class). Combined with measured `textAlign: center`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1: 'chrome, navigation and layout — logical inline/block direction follows the document' and 'CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance — render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose.'
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — hypothesis for the visual reordering (no RTL locale is currently reachable in-app). The physical-offset inventory and the absence of any dir/unicode-bidi attribute are directly verified from source and from the live attribute enumeration.

**Proposed cure.** Logical properties throughout (`pe-9`, `inset-inline-end`), and `dir="ltr"` on the value element — which glass-ui `Input` makes trivial. Drop `text-align: center` for inline-start alignment; a technical LTR value centred in a possibly-RTL container is the worst of both.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-12 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** `.dock-layer-grid` is a phantom class with zero CSS rules; because it sets no `position`, the hidden/leaving sub-layer resolves its containing block against the OUTER dock face and covers the dock's live controls for 260ms.

**Mechanism.** A container named "grid" that is a block box; its children carry `grid-area: 1/1` inherited from the producer's `.dock-layer` rule, which is inert in block layout. Absolute positioning then escapes to the nearest positioned ancestor — the outer `.dock-face` — so the leaving face spans the Back control and the toggle, overhanging its own container by 65px left and 53px right, `visibility: visible` at `opacity: 0` for 260ms. glass-ui carves a special `.is-press-keepalive` rule for exactly this hazard on its OWN layers; this consumer gets no such protection.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured computed style: `{display:"block", position:"static", gridTemplateColumns:"none", overflow:"visible"}`. `grep -rn "dock-layer-grid"` across the repo and `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/` returns exactly two hits, both in this file (:91, :101). `offsetParentOfInactive: "DIV.dock-face is-active"`. Rects: container 634.0/184.0; active sub-layer 634.0/184.0; inactive 569.0/302.0; leaving 499.0/443.0 (t=32..246). glass-ui `layers.css`: `.dock-layer:not(.is-active){position:absolute;inset:0}`, `.dock-layer.is-active{position:relative}`, `.dock-layer.is-leaving{opacity:0;visibility:visible}`.
```

**Reproduction.** WebKit 1440×900, open Tools, `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.dock-layer-grid'))` → display block / position static; then read `offsetParent` of the non-`is-active` child → the outer `.dock-face`.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the class. A real `<DockLayer>` inside a real `<DockCrossfade>` gets `position: relative` on its host by construction, so the containing block is correct without a consumer-side container at all.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-24 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The document heading outline is inverted, not merely missing an h1: the page's most prominent title is an H3 whose own subsections are H2s. No module owns heading level.

```
test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts:55-58. The oracle presses [data-specimen='ease-out-back'] at :117 and :189. Honest attribution: all three die EARLIER, at discloseAuthoring (:50-52, #easing-authoring-0 svg[role='img'] never appears) — an EasingAuthoringStage failure, not the strip's; the consequence for this component is that nothing gates it in CI.

Both pass today.

**Proposed cure.** Repair O-17 first (it is the standing oracle), then replace the cardinality assertions with contract assertions that cannot be satisfied vacuously: (a) every tile in SPECIMEN_TILES, sampled over [0,1], must round-trip through serializeIntervalRamp without throwing; (b) the set of SPECIMEN_TILES ids must equal Object.keys(bezierPresets) union the steps ids. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches` · D-9 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `MixResult` is a non-discriminated interface with optional payloads (`css?`, `colors?`), so `{type:'color'}` with no css is type-legal and renders the same blank plate as D-8. This looseness is what forces the four masking `??` fallbacks in the component.

**Mechanism.** impossible states left representable, then papered over with fallbacks that convert them into silently wrong renders

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/mix/composables/useMixingState.ts:32-36. Masking fallbacks at MixResultDisplay.vue:37-39 (`?? "var(--muted-foreground)"`) and :44-45 (`?? ""` twice). Measured render for {type:'color'} with no css: {"swatchCount":0,"text":"RESULT"}. Not reachable via startMix today (useMixingState.ts:90 always sets css) — this is the type being looser than the invariant.
```

**Reproduction.** Mount MixResultDisplay with `{ result: { type: 'color' } }` → blank plate with only the RESULT label and three buttons. (Type-checks clean.)

**Proposed cure.** Make it a real discriminated union — `{ type: "color"; css: string } | { type: "palette"; colors: readonly [PaletteColor, ...PaletteColor[]] }` — which makes the blank plate unrepresentable and deletes all four `??` fallbacks, forcing startMix to decide what an empty palette mix means at the one place that knows.

```
MixResultDisplay.vue:92-105, `:key="i"` at :99 and `:seed="i === 0 ? 'mix-result' : `mix-result-${i}`"` at :104. The correctly-keyed sibling is MixSourceSelector.vue:129 `:key="swatchKeys[i]"`.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt: demo/workbenches/g` · C-6 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The specimen rows and the open interval's ramp recompute on `type` and `direction` changes, neither of which can affect either — the whole per-row derivation (49-sample glyph, colour parse+mix, 27-tile scan, WCAG floor walk) re-runs on every direction-slider tick.

**Mechanism.** over-broad-reactive-dependency: a monolithic modelState object serves as both the serializer's input and the reactivity graph, so consumers that need four of its six fields subscribe to all six.

**Evidence.**

```
useSpecimenRows.ts:42-72 reads `modelState()` wholesale; useGradientModel.ts:102-109 rebuilds modelState whenever ANY of type/direction/stops/intervals/interpolationSpace/hueMethod changes. openIntervalRamp (GradientEasingEditor.vue:63-67) likewise re-runs a full sampleCoalescedStops (2 parseColorIn + 33 mixColors) per direction tick. Cost per row per recompute: glyphPath = 49 easing evals + 98 toFixed(3) + string build, measured 13.2 µs/call (`glyphPath(48) x20000 = 265.0ms` via vite-node against the real src/subpaths/easing); plus interpolateStopColors; plus tileIdFor's linear scan over 27 tiles; plus safeCss → certifyAccentInk's WCAG floor walk. Observed coupling: +22% script/tick when interval count goes 1→4 during a direction drag (probe 8, C-5 evidence). Tell-tale: serializeIntervalRamp already hardcodes `type: "linear", direction: 90` in its sub-model (useGradientCSS.ts:243-244) — it demonstrably does not want those fields.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/wbge-probe8.mjs (drives 120 ArrowRight presses on [role='slider'] and reads CDP ScriptDuration/RecalcStyleDuration deltas at 1 vs 4 intervals; the ratio scales with interval count even though direction cannot affect any interval).

**Proposed cure.** modelState is doing double duty. Pass the specimen derivation only what it consumes: useSpecimenRows(() => stops, () => intervals, () => interpolationSpace, () => hueMethod). type/direction then cannot reach it. Apply the same narrowing to serializeIntervalRamp, which already discards them.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt: demo/workbenches/g` · C-7 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** A failed clipboard write is completely silent, and a successful one is never announced — the CopyResult is discarded, no onCopyError is passed, and the route has zero aria-live regions.

```

Confirmation is an aria-label swap on the button that already has focus (:181 `copiedRow === row.index ? 'Copied' : \`Copy ${row.css}\``) — not reliably announced by any major screen reader. Measured (probe 1): `document.querySelectorAll("[aria-live]").length === 0` on /#/gradient. ```

**Reproduction.** NONE for the failure branch (would require revoking clipboard permission) — the discarded CopyResult and absent onCopyError are established by reading GradientEasingEditor.vue:100-103 against the glass-ui type surface. The zero-live-region measurement IS reproduced: open /#/gradient and run `document.querySelectorAll('[aria-live]').length` → 0.

**Proposed cure.** One polite live region per bench, owned by the editor root, fed by the EXISTING copyStatus: success → "Copied <literal>", failure → "Copy failed — clipboard unavailable". ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt: demo/workbenches/g` · C-9 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** toggleTune clones the entire disclosure record on every press, which Vue 3 does not require, and the record is never pruned when intervals shrink.

**Mechanism.** contrivance: a defensive immutability idiom carried over from a reactivity system that needed it, applied to one that does not.

```
GradientEasingEditor.vue:84-88 `const tuneOpen = ref<Record<number, boolean>>({}); function toggleTune(index) { tuneOpen.value = { ...tuneOpen.value, [index]: !tuneOpen.value[index] }; }`. `ref({})` is deep-reactive in Vue 3 — a key addition on the returned proxy triggers the dependency the template registered on the missing-key read, so `tuneOpen.value[index] = !tuneOpen.value[index]` is exact. The spread is a Vue-2-era reflex costing a fresh object allocation and a full re-render trigger per press. Stale entries persist: probe 9 shows `tune: ["false","true"]` → `["false","true","false"]` with the true entry now pointing at a different interval.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — established by reading GradientEasingEditor.vue:84-88 against Vue 3.5 reactive-proxy semantics (key additions on a deep ref ARE tracked). The stale-entry half is visible in probe 9's `tune` array.

**Proposed cure.** `tuneOpen.value[index] = !tuneOpen.value[index]`. The never-pruned half disappears with C-4's stable-id cure — a Map keyed on the left stop's id has entries removed exactly when the interval is.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt: demo/workbenches/g` · C-10 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Two requestAnimationFrame callbacks are scheduled per authoring emission for identical work, and neither handle is retained for cancellation.

**Mechanism.** double-scheduling: a side effect is attached both to the local emitter and to the round-trip prop change that the same emission causes, so it runs twice per event by construction.

**Evidence.**

```
EasingAuthoringStage.vue:57-67 — `onAuthored` calls `requestAnimationFrame(syncVbRatio)` then emits; the emission updates the parent's interval, which changes the `value.css` prop, which fires `watch(() => value.css, () => requestAnimationFrame(syncVbRatio), { flush: "post" })`. Both callbacks perform the same querySelector + viewBox read + ref write. During a control-point drag this is two redundant rAF-scheduled DOM queries per pointer-move. Neither rAF id is stored, so neither can be cancelled on unmount (currently harmless: syncVbRatio is null-guarded via `rootEl.value?.`).
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — established by reading EasingAuthoringStage.vue:57-67; the redundancy is currently masked because C-2 makes syncVbRatio a no-op, and becomes live work the moment C-2 is cured.

**Proposed cure.** Drop the rAF from onAuthored. The `value.css` watcher alone is sufficient and correct — value.css changes on every geometry change, which is exactly the stated trigger set, and `flush: "post"` already guarantees the DOM has been patched. Retain the rAF id and cancel it in onScopeDispose.
