**Defect.** `isProcessing` is false during the image-decode window: quantizeFromFile awaits imageFileToPixels BEFORE runQuantize sets isProcessing=true, so nothing renders during the decode — and if the decode throws, nothing ever renders (C-5).

**Mechanism.** loading state raised downstream of the first expensive await instead of at the operation boundary

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useImageQuantize.ts:105-108 (the await) vs :86-87 (where error/isProcessing are actually written). Measured blind window on a 6 MP file: total_mainthread_ms 24.3 (createImageBitmap 8.6 + getImageData 13.8 + slice 1.8), multiples of that on mobile Safari for a 12 MP capture.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/extract — replay imageFileToPixels on a 3000x2000 JPEG and time it (24.3ms here); during that entire window the component is in its resting state with no indication that work has begun.

**Proposed cure.** Raise isProcessing at the TOP of quantizeFromFile inside a try/finally, so the loading state brackets the whole operation rather than only its worker tail. (Cure C-10 alongside it — a loading flag nobody can perceive is only half the fix.)

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/ext` · C-15 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Camera failures are filed as quantize errors. The component reaches through the session object to write a writable computed whose setter targets the worker's error ref, so a camera fault occupies the quantizer's error channel and the next successful quantize silently erases it. A raw DOMException is template-interpolated, so the user reads 'Camera access denied: NotAllowedError: Permission denied'. There is no dismiss.

**Mechanism.** two unrelated failure domains sharing one channel; a component mutating composable-owned state directly instead of through an action — the encapsulation the session exists to provide, bypassed at the one place it matters

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:252 (`session.quantizeError.value = \`Camera access denied: ${err}\``); the writable computed at useExtractSession.ts:66-73; the erasure at useImageQuantize.ts:86 (`error.value = null`).
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/extract — deny camera permission: the quantize error line shows the stringified DOMException. Then drop any valid image: the camera message vanishes without the user having acknowledged it.

**Proposed cure.** A separate `cameraError` ref rendered on its own line, written through a `session.setCameraError()` action rather than by reaching into a computed; map the three real getUserMedia rejection names (NotAllowedError / NotFoundError / NotReadableError) to human sentences.

### `CHALLENGE-D — assume the design is flawed (visual truth, sta` · D-13 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Dead masking fallback: an unreachable zero-length branch in the slider gradient encodes a phantom 'empty' state the design never has.

**Mechanism.** F5 — states nobody drew. The branch is defensive scaffolding against a state the data model makes impossible, and it is why the empty state reads 'dead branch' rather than 'unhandled' in the state matrix.

**Evidence.**

```
GenerateControls.vue:66-67 — `const colors = palette.value; if (colors.length === 0) return "var(--muted)";`. But `palette` is `computed(() => generatePalette(count.value, preset.value, harmony.value, seed.value))` (demo/workbenches/generate/composables/useColorGeneration.ts:26-28) and `count` is bounded to [1,12] by the slider (`:min="1"` at GenerateControls.vue:301). `palette.value.length === count.value >= 1` always, so the branch is unreachable. Owner edict 2 forbids masking fallbacks.
```

**Reproduction.** Static, from source: `useColorGeneration.ts:26-28` defines palette as a computed of length `count`; `GenerateControls.vue:301` pins `:min="1"`. No input path can produce `palette.value.length === 0`, so `GenerateControls.vue:67` can never execute.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the branch. The gradient computation reduces to the stop map with no guard. Enforcing the invariant structurally (the count type is already bounded) rather than defending it at the render site is the idiom the project's retired-proof-idiom feedback calls for.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-18 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The loupe is optically wrong in four independent ways: it is centred under the finger, its backing store ignores devicePixelRatio, its magnification is 9.64x not the intended 10x because LOUPE_SIZE is used as a border-box, and it has no reticle marking which texel is the sample.

**Mechanism.** constants.ts LOUPE_SIZE/LOUPE_PIXELS are treated as CSS px rather than as a model; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2 requires 'reticle, loupe and numeric value remain one model'.

**Evidence.**

```
probe.mjs mobile: loupe backing 110x110, CSS box 106x106, dpr 3 -> 318 device px painted from a 110px bitmap (2.89x upscale of a deliberately nearest-neighbour image). The 110->106 delta comes from ImageEyedropper.vue:194-195 setting LOUPE_SIZE as width/height while :265 declares a 2px border, so 110/11=10 px per texel becomes 9.64 and the crisp blocks are resampled by 0.964. probe/shot-forced-colors.png: the loupe shows a red/blue checker while the readout says blue — unverifiable by eye.
```

**Reproduction.** node .../probe/probe.mjs — mobile.loupe backing vs cssRect vs dpr.

**Proposed cure.** Size the backing store to LOUPE_SIZE * devicePixelRatio, make LOUPE_SIZE the content box, offset the loupe from the touch point on coarse pointers, and draw the reticle on the sampled texel — the same model D-1 and D-6 need.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-19 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Empty, loading, error, CORS/tainted and out-of-bounds states do not exist; out-of-bounds in particular leaves a stale color displayed as if it were current.

**Mechanism.** The component has one happy path and no state machine around it.

**Evidence.**

```
useImageSampler.ts:114-115 sampleAt returns null out of bounds and the caller (ImageEyedropper.vue:156-162) does nothing — no message, no cursor change, stale readout retained. loadImage rejects on img.onerror (useImageSampler.ts:72-75) and onMounted(() => { loadAndFit(); ... }) (:237-240) never catches. img.crossOrigin='anonymous' (:70) routes every non-CORS cross-origin URL into that same silent arm; a tainted-canvas getImageData (:116) would throw inside a pointermove handler. No loading affordance exists between mount and decode.
```

**Reproduction.** Out-of-bounds is directly reproducible: tap the empty 45.1% of the stage (D-9) and observe the unchanged readout. The missing catch on loadAndFit is CONFIRMED by reading; its live reachability is a HYPOTHESIS pending a parent that can supply a remote URL — today ExtractWorkbench only passes same-origin data URLs.

**Proposed cure.** Give the overlay the four states it can actually occupy — decoding, ready, out-of-bounds, undecodable — with the decoding and error arms visible and the out-of-bounds arm clearing rather than preserving the stale sample.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-20 · CHALLENGE-D

**Proposed cure.** One bitmap: the offscreen canvas is the sampling authority and the visible layer paints only what it shows.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-12 · CHALLENGE-D

**Evidence.**

```
Measured on the composited chip surface rgb(242,228,211): resting label rgb(91,70,51) = 7.10:1; pressed label oklch(0.438 0.075 205) = 6.02:1; pressed glyph same accent = 6.02:1; family eyebrow (--muted-foreground x opacity 0.75) = 3.24:1 against a 4.5:1 floor for 9px text — FAILS. Compensations for the pressed state are only font-weight 600 and stroke-width 1.25 -> 1.75px, both sub-perceptual at 9px/22px, while a merely FOCUSED neighbour gets a saturated crimson ring (frames/D-desktop-light-focus-ring.png) — a transient state louder than the persistent one. EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:182-186 records the identical error being found and fixed for the glyph ("45% floated the sparkline under the WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 graphics floor … 65% clears 3:1"); the reasoning reached one of three ink species.

**Proposed cure.** Drop the `opacity` multiplier (it also breaks forced colors, D-06) and let --muted-foreground alone carry the eyebrow. **Defect.** The gradient serializers emit no `<color-interpolation-method>`, so the browser blends all 33 oklch sub-stops in sRGB; the entire coalescing apparatus exists to compensate for a serializer the library does not publish, on a platform that has supported the native form for years.

**Proposed cure.** Move `serializeGradient` into value.js `/css`, emitting `linear-gradient(in oklch longer hue, <stops>)` natively and baking sub-stops ONLY where an interval carries a non-linear easing (easing genuinely cannot be expressed natively; space and hue-method can). **Reproduction.** Add a fourth member to LeftoverStrategy at demo/palettes/mix.ts:19 and run typecheck: MixConfigBar.vue:85 errors (missing Record key), MixConfigBar.vue:83 does not — the Select renders 3 of 4 options with no diagnostic.

**Proposed cure.** One LEFTOVER_STRATEGIES: {value;label;description}[] beside the type in the (relocated, per L-2) mix module, with the union DERIVED from it — `type LeftoverStrategy = typeof LEFTOVER_STRATEGIES[number]["value"]` — so the list is the single source and drift is impossible. First pass measured 1.26x at N=200000 — see §C of the report; magnitude is measurement-sensitive, direction is not.

**Defect.** A type-level module cycle between the model, the serializer and the parser — which is why the module named for the composable also owns the types, which is why the dead re-export barrel felt necessary.

useGradientModel.ts:15 imports values from ./useGradientCSS and :16 from ./gradientParse; useGradientCSS.ts:31-34 imports types back from ./useGradientModel; gradientParse.ts:22 imports linearInterval from ./useGradientCSS and :23-27 imports types from ./useGradientModel.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects (SearchFilterBar.vue, a` · C-11 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The filter popover can neither shrink nor scroll: max-height is none, overflow-y is visible, and there is no floating-ui `size` middleware — so once the tag list and the Clear-all row are present the content is projected to exceed a phone viewport with no way to reach the bottom.

**Mechanism.** popover sized by content with collision handling that can shift but not resize — no size middleware, no max-height, no inner scroll container on the content root

**Evidence.**

```
Measured live at 390x664 with the tag section absent: dialog height 441.5px; on the popover root `overflowY: "visible"`, `maxHeight: "none"`, `scrollHeight: 439` === `clientHeight: 439` (no inner scroll). Arithmetic: the tag block adds max-h-28 = 112px plus its section label and padding (~43px) and the Clear-all row adds ~44px -> ~640px against a 664px viewport.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — labelled a HYPOTHESIS. Not reproduced because the live tag catalog is empty (`curl -s https://api.color.babb.dev/colors/tags` -> `[]`), so the tag block never renders. Separately I observed one transient 81.5px bottom overflow (dialog y=304, height 441.5, bottom 745.5 vs viewport 664) which floating-ui's collision shift then resolved to a fitting position — that transient is NOT reported as a defect.

**Proposed cure.** Give the popover content a `max-height: var(--reka-popover-content-available-height)` with `overflow-y: auto` on the content root (root-level, in the glass-ui PopoverContent variant rather than as a per-instance override), so the panel scrolls instead of clipping regardless of tag count.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (third independent pass on demo` · C-28 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `ActionBarToggle`'s `slotLive` early return makes the watch's re-arm dead code: on a later false->true edge `settled` is never restored by the watch, and the invariant the O-15b oracle asserts is held only by an unacknowledged `transitionend` side channel.

**Mechanism.** a state machine whose stated owner (the watch) is not its actual owner (a DOM transition event), so the invariant holds by luck

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/ActionBarToggle.vue:52-68 — `if (slotLive.value) return;` short-circuits after the first `visible === true`, while `settled.value = false` is set on every false edge at :56; the only restorer is `@transitionend.self="onSlotSettled"` (:69-72, bound at :78) setting `settled.value = visible`. That class is exactly what e2e/smoke/oracles/o15-dock-register.spec.ts:74-79 asserts (`is-settled`, then `.action-bar-toggle-inner` computes `overflow: visible`). MEASURED, fresh context 1440x900, in-app hash nav: boot `is-visible is-live is-settled`/overflow visible; #/browse `is-live`/overflow hidden; #/ `is-visible is-live is-settled`/overflow visible; #/admin/users `is-live`/overflow hidden; #/ `is-visible is-live is-settled`/overflow visible — it recovers today.
```

**Reproduction.** Measured and NEGATIVE at HEAD (the transitionend path restores `is-settled` on every re-entry). Filed as a latent structural defect: any change making the `grid-template-columns` transition a no-op (equal endpoints, `transition: none`, a content-visibility skip) silently pins the clip on and O-15b begins failing far from ActionBarToggle.vue:57.

**Proposed cure.** Drop the `slotLive` early return so the watch owns `settled` on both edges, and keep `onSlotSettled` as confirmation rather than as the sole restorer.

**Defect.** Test truth: a second vacuous-gate mutation distinct from pass-1 C-9's, plus the structural reason the blank-navigation defect was unreachable from e2e.

**Evidence.**

```
Deleting `<SelectValue v-if="isDesktop" />` (demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue:87) so the navigation never shows a view name on any route keeps the ENTIRE e2e suite green: every locator resolves the control by the explicit `aria-label` on DockTrigger (:68) — page-load.spec.ts:33, a11y-modality-support.spec.ts:128, a11y-web-modality.spec.ts:76, o14-preview-truth.spec.ts:200/240/286, mobile/page-load-mobile.spec.ts:52, fixtures/dock.ts:66 — and nothing asserts what the navigation SAYS. Every view switch goes through `openView(page, name)` (e2e/smoke/fixtures/dock.ts:56-80), which clicks an option IN the list and therefore can never reach a view that is missing from it. The admin routes ARE cold-loaded (admin/admin-walk.spec.ts:27-47, admin/a11y-authed-admin.spec.ts:28-30) but AUTHENTICATED — precisely the branch where the label renders. The one unauthenticated cold load of an affected route (o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:929, /#/atmosphere) only measures contrast, so a blank label removes text from its census and makes it pass more easily. Zero coverage of the C-23/C-24 surface: `grep -rn "Switch to slug|Generate new slug|enter slug or token" e2e/ test/` -> no matches; `grep -rln "useDockAdminMode|usePopupMutex|shell/dock" test/ demo/test/` -> only status-lamp.test.ts and picker-blob-config.test.ts, neither of which constructs Dock.vue.

**Reproduction.** NONE needed — the mutation is named exactly and the locator inventory is pasted. To confirm: delete DockViewSelect.vue:87 and run the smoke suite.

**Proposed cure.** One route-parametrised assertion: for each ViewId, cold-load it UNAUTHENTICATED and assert (i) the view-select trigger's accessible text equals VIEW_MAP[id].label, (ii) the open listbox reports that view aria-selected, (iii) document.querySelectorAll('h1').length === 1. **Mechanism.** Design-system variance expressed at the consumption site rather than in the design system.

**Evidence.**

```
ActionBarToggle.vue:154-158 `.dock-tools-btn { --dock-compact-control-padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; margin-inline: 0.25rem; gap: 0.5em; }` — the mechanism (a producer token hook) is honest but the placement is a consumer overriding one instance of a design-system control (edicts 4 + 5). ActionBarToggle.vue:95 and :96 bind `:style="{ color: accent }"` twice, once on the icon and once on the label span, for a single inherited property. Measured consequence: the trigger renders 32×32 CSS px at 390px viewport vs 44×44 for the non-compact dock controls (`Back`, `Save edit`) in the same run — clears WCAG 2.5.8 AA (24px), fails 2.5.5 AAA (44px). Recorded not charged: glass-ui's own coarse-pointer floor (dist/components/dock/styles/controls/touch-floor.css) excludes EVERY control inside `.glass-dock` via `:not(:where(.glass-dock *))`, so the 44px question is producer-wide.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-actionbartoggle/probe/C3-route-census.mjs (mobile-390 leg) reports w/h 32×32 for `.dock-tools-btn`; the sibling comparison came from the same probe run at isMobile viewport (Back / Save edit at 44 unscaled).

**Proposed cure.** Move the box-model step-up into glass-ui as a DockControl shape/size variant and relay it to the active glass-ui BH inbox per the standing relay edict. Set `color` once on the control root (or one `--dock-tools-accent` custom property on `.dock-tools-btn`) and let the icon and label inherit — one binding instead of two.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/shell/dock/Doc` · D-19 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The advertised 'bounded view-switch hue sweep' interpolates in oklab (rectangular), so it cuts a chord through the desaturated middle rather than travelling the hue arc, and every intermediate frame is a colour useViewAccents never gamut-mapped or contrast-guarded.

**Mechanism.** a `<color>`-typed registered property interpolates componentwise in oklab; hue travel requires an angle-typed axis. The W7-4 guard (gamut-map to cusp + WCAG 3:1 re-guard) is applied to endpoints only.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured per-rAF across a picker→gradient switch (probe/probe-dvs2.mjs): {"distinctValues": 10, "first": "oklch(0.471189 0.188448 9.83402)", "mid": "474ms oklab(0.471189 -0.0231664 -0.10933)", "last": "796ms oklch(0.471189 0.132793 249.834)", uniqSample includes "oklab(0.471189 0.0209336 -0.0794474)"} — chroma 0.188 → 0.082 → 0.133 while L stays pinned at 0.4712. Registration: demo/styles/foundation.css:192-198 `@property --accent-view { syntax: "<color>"; }`. The claim it contradicts: DockViewSelect.vue:155-158, 'the navigation still SWEEPS to the new view's hue'.
```

**Reproduction.** `node probe/probe-dvs2.mjs` and read the C1 block. (This measurement also PROVES the transition is live rather than dead code — the first pass argued it from registration alone.)

**Proposed cure.** Animate an `<angle>`-registered hue and compose the colour from it if the arc is what is wanted; otherwise correct the comment to describe the chord and state explicitly that the guard covers endpoints only.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · R3-12 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The demo's global reduced-motion transition guard is inert app-wide; the producer's rule wins, so this component's PRM behaviour is accidental rather than designed.

**Mechanism.** A `*`-selector `!important` guard in consumer CSS outranked by a producer `!important` rule at higher specificity — so the consumer's declared PRM policy for transitions has no effect anywhere in the app.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured under `reducedMotion: "reduce"`, frames/r3probe3.json: `transitionDuration: "0.1s"`, `animationDuration: "1e-05s"`, with matching rules `{sel: ":not([data-allow-motion])", media: "(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)", td: "0.1s", imp: "important"}` (glass-ui, specificity 0,1,0) and `{sel: "*, ::before, ::after", td: "0.01ms", imp: "important"}` (demo/styles/animations.css:184-193, specificity 0,0,0). The producer rule wins. This CORRECTS round-2 section 5, which credited compliance to the demo guard.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-18 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Eight of fifteen enumerated states are unhandled or visually broken. Notably there is no empty state (no placeholder was ever chosen — the direct cause of D-2's blank label), no loading state (the admin row pops in unannounced after auth settles), no error state (`inject(SESSION_PORT_KEY)!` is a bare non-null assertion, so a missing provider crashes the product's only navigation), and disabled is never expressed though the producer supports and styles it.

**Mechanism.** States were designed for the happy path (populated, hovered, reduced-motion) and the remainder were left to the producer or to chance. Per the seat brief's own rule, a state that was never designed is a design defect.

**Evidence.**

```
Template read + live DOM. empty: DockViewSelect.vue:92-98 v-for with no v-else, and no `placeholder` on SelectValue (:87) — measured textContent "" on 7 routes. loading: pm.isAdminAuthenticated is async, gating :122. error: line 35 `inject(SESSION_PORT_KEY)!`. disabled: producer supports it on Select and SelectItem (`data-[disabled]:opacity-disabled` in menuRowClass) and it is never passed. focused: measured broken (D-1). selected: measured zero delta (D-3) and mis-signalled (D-20). RTL: measured broken (D-8). zoom-200: measured label "" (D-4). truncation: `[&>span]:line-clamp-none` removes the producer clamp without a replacement.
```

**Reproduction.** Per-state reproductions are given in D-1/D-2/D-3/D-4/D-8/D-20; for the error state, remove the SESSION_PORT_KEY provider and the dock throws at line 35.

**Proposed cure.** Design the missing states explicitly: a placeholder that names the current destination is impossible by construction once D-2's single enumeration lands (no value can lack an option); the async auth gate gets a stable reserved row rather than a pop-in; and the non-null assertion becomes a typed provider contract, since a nav that crashes on a missing provider has no recovery path.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure / module boundaries / owners` · L-22 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The demo's declared view of the published library surface has drifted from `package.json#exports`: tsconfig.demo.json maps a nonexistent `dist/index.d.ts`, declares two subpaths that are not exported, and omits two that are — while calling itself a mirror of the generated Vite alias set.

**Mechanism.** A hand-maintained declaration of a generated surface: the runtime alias set is derived from exports, the type paths are not, so the two views of the public API drift silently.

**Evidence.**

```
`package.json#exports` keys = ['./color','./value','./css','./easing','./math','./transform','./quantize'] — 7 keys, no '.' root. tsconfig.demo.json paths declare `@mkbabb/value.js` -> ./dist/index.d.ts (`ls dist/index*` -> no matches found), plus `/parsing` and `/units` (neither in exports; no src/subpaths/parsing.ts or units.ts — `ls src/subpaths` -> color, css, easing, math, quantize, transform, value), and omit `/value` and `/css` (both exported; `/css` used 10x in demo and 4x inside glass-ui's dist). The file's header calls this 'the 8 public keys' / 'a CLOSED 8-key set' that 'mirrors the vite.config.ts runtime self-alias generated from the same map'; vite.config.ts:41-50 generates one alias per exports entry -> 7 aliases and no bare-root alias.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — latent, not live. No demo file imports the bare `@mkbabb/value.js` specifier (`grep -rn '@mkbabb/value.js"' demo` -> the only hit is prose at demo/shared/utils.ts:12), and glass-ui's three specifiers (/color, /css, /easing, measured in its dist) are all covered by the generated alias set, so one instance serves the running app. Were the bare specifier ever written it would resolve to node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 — the published copy npm installed for glass-ui's peer dep — a second instance of this library behind an undeclared specifier.

**Proposed cure.** Generate the tsconfig `paths` from `package.json#exports` exactly as the Vite aliases already are (one loader, one source of truth), or add a real `"."` export plus `dist/index.d.ts`. Either way the two declarations of the public surface cannot drift apart again — this is the axis T.W1's dogfood keystone was fought over.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation audit of demo/workbenches/gener` · C-18 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** WatercolorDot reads its `seed` prop once at setup, so the consumer's colour-derived `:seed="gen-${css}-${i}"` only ever applies its mount-time value — the 'seeded stable per (color,i)' claim decays after the first regenerate.

**Mechanism.** A by-value option passed to a composable that treats it as static, while the consumer passes a value it expects to be reactive. Family: NON-REACTIVE-OPTION-READ-ONCE.

```

**Reproduction.** NONE — I did not capture a before/after silhouette diff, and the dots are unreachable for interaction anyway (C-1). Labelled a hypothesis on the observable effect; the code path itself is quoted above and is not in doubt.

**Proposed cure.** Consumer side (BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8): pass a stable `gen-${i}` seed, since a colour-derived seed is a category error against that contract and buys nothing. Producer side (relay, optional): make useWatercolorBlob take seed as a getter/ref so the silhouette and the wet edge stay in agreement.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-9 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The dropdown preview-strip cost claim holds at the default count but fails by 2.8× at the maximum; the strips are plain template function calls (never memoized), and the chip module's segment budget is private so the host over-generates.

**Mechanism.** Asymmetric module surface: the ramp chip publishes its sampling budget so hosts can size their work, the strip chip hides its cap — so at count>7 the host pays to generate stops the renderer discards. Compounded by the absence of memoization: every re-render of the mounted SelectContent recomputes all 16 strips.

**Evidence.**

```
Claim at GenerateControls.vue:88-93: "10 rows × 5-12 library generations is sub-millisecond". Measured (node/V8, bundled core): one generatePalette count=5 = 0.097 ms; count=12 = 0.362 ms; 10 preset strips @count=5 = 0.871 ms (claim HOLDS); 6 harmony strips @count=5 = 0.699 ms; 10 preset strips @count=12 = 2.80 ms (claim FAILS 2.8×). presetStops/harmonyStops at :94-100 are plain functions called from the template. STRIP_SEGMENT_CAP=7 is a private const in demo/color-session/color-chips/PreviewStrip.vue while the sibling RAMP form exports RAMP_SAMPLE_COUNT from color-chips/sample.ts and its barrel.
```

**Reproduction.** esbuild-bundle demo/color-session/generate-color.ts, then bench 10× generatePalette per preset at count 5 and 12 — 0.871 ms and 2.80 ms respectively over 500 iterations after warmup.

**Proposed cure.** Export STRIP_SEGMENT_CAP from the color-chips barrel (symmetry with RAMP_SAMPLE_COUNT) and wrap the two truth functions in computeds keyed on (count, preset, harmony, seed). NOT 'generate only 7' — generateHues derives its step from count for the analogous harmony, so a 7-generation is not the prefix of a 12-generation and truncating would break the seed-exactness law. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 for this file.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-11 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** `tsconfig.demo.json#paths` is a hand-maintained second mirror of `package.json#exports` and has rotted: it declares three keys that do not exist and omits two that do and are used — while `vite.config.ts` GENERATES the same mirror from the exports map precisely so it cannot drift.

**Mechanism.** two mirrors of one fact, one generated and one hand-rolled; the hand-rolled one rotted and now typechecks only because TS bundler resolution self-references through package.json#exports for the two omitted subpaths — the paths block is simultaneously stale and redundant.

**Evidence.**

```
package.json#exports = 7 keys {./color, ./value, ./css, ./easing, ./math, ./transform, ./quantize}. tsconfig.demo.json declares `@mkbabb/value.js` → ./dist/index.d.ts (NO `.` key in exports; `ls dist/` → anchors-*.js, gh-pages, operations-*.js, result-*.js, subpaths — no index.d.ts), `/parsing` → ./dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts (does not exist), `/units` → ./dist/subpaths/units.d.ts (does not exist), and OMITS `./css` and `./value` — `./css` is actively used at demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:25 (`parseTimingFunction`). The file's own comment calls it "the CLOSED 8-key set" / "the 8 public keys". Contrast vite.config.ts:36-51, which builds anchored-regex aliases from `package.json#exports` with the stated rationale "GENERATED (not hand-rolled) so the alias set can never drift from the exports map".
```

**Reproduction.** `ls dist/ dist/subpaths/` and `python3 -c "import json;print(list(json.load(open('package.json'))['exports']))"` against the paths block in tsconfig.demo.json.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the value.js entries from tsconfig.demo.json#paths and let self-reference through `exports` resolve them (one source of truth, the same one vite reads). If an explicit map is wanted for build determinism, generate it the way vite generates its aliases. Either way: one mirror, not two.

### `L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, directi` · L-r2-15 · L

**Defect.** Measurement caveat recorded so no one re-derives a wrong number: the page's resource-timing buffer capped at its 250-entry default during my probes, silently dropping later entries.

**Mechanism.** Default resourceTimingBufferSize truncation.

**Evidence.**

```
`performance.getEntriesByType('resource').length` returned exactly 250, and a probe consequently reported `gradientSfc: []` on a page that had plainly loaded the gradient modules (rowsRendered: 1, tiles: 27 in the same call).
```

**Reproduction.** Any evaluate reading performance.getEntriesByType('resource') on this app after full settle returns exactly 250.

**Proposed cure.** Any future perf probe on this app must call `performance.setResourceTimingBufferSize(2000)` via addInitScript before navigation. The chunk facts in L-r2-9 come from the network log and on-disk prebundle sizes, not from the truncated buffer.
